title: Spec fixes before the panel: F58 (DUR-14 vs CNF-47), the same-code sentence, commit lean-01/02
description: 1) File F58 in 16-open-findings.md: DUR-14's T <- max(min(T, fire_at - eps), now) can numerically exceed the old T when now > T, so CNF-47's 'never grows' is the wrong theorem; the right ones are T' <= max(T, now) and (now <= T -> T' <= T). title: Milestone 7: selected Escapes, accounting bridge, SILENCE as a two-run relation
description: ADR-0023 decision 10 item 7. Selected set: List (EscapeId × Bool) keyed by Escape commitment id with DUR-10's OR-merge; a normal-PIN entry never released whatever sweepActive does (F54 fix row 4); every holder decision and hot acceptance writes every window (DUR-20) as a writes count equal under both PINs. DUR-22 denominator computed from ChainView + the selected set with restoreAll; theorem it is the same value on every pass while the set only grows; distinguish equality across candidates in one environment, preservation across the sequence, agreement across nodes — if the across-pass claim needs more than DUR-22's construction supplies, return the precise gap to DUR-22 as a finding (first reader §4). Accounting bridge: POL-18/POL-19 reserve/refund/age-out transitions establish milestone 3's counting premises for POL-20's cohort; ADR-0014's trace becomes a reachable exhibit and the withdrawn completion bound a refuted theorem (¬ ∀ window, completed <= n/t × cap) while the admission theorem holds; SPN-33 mempool settlement refunds nothing. SILENCE: Obs structure (response shape, /pending, /healthz bucket, /events queue, peer message shapes and sizes, abstract work counts) with observe ∘ step = stepObs ∘ observe on every prefix where now < current T (DUR-14 dynamic, may be zero, sticky once ended); two worlds = one request body with two enrolments (SEC-10); leaky twins: DEF-12's arm-conditioned marker and F54's conditional window traversal; docstring says counts are not durations (F22, SEC-47). F3, F4, F13 kept as traces with no repair chosen. Glossary gains observer projection and concealment horizon when this lands.
notes:
Q1 DECIDED 2026-09-19 (four-reader panel, .context/m7-q1b-*.md; landed as F59 + amendments to DUR-22/24/28/31, CNF-140, MAN-9, ADR-0020, commit e74d9ff): Coverage denominator = filter on the chain read + every distinct selected input outpoint added once (counted regardless of the read; precedence over exclusions) — NOT confirmed+restored-excluded; rebuild Coverage.denominator from a ChainView + selected set. Theorems: (i) one value per pass; (ii) floor: P >= union of selected inputs on every pass; (iii) per-node single sweep under "both selected at this node's first release"; (iv) aggregate burn <= (100-pct)% of swept. Exhibits kept: restoreOne (F54), unconfirmed-external-deposit two-pass trace, subtracting-shape breaks the floor, cross-node 2-of-3 trace, late-selection trace, phantom-prevout denial. No snapshot, no ingress rule.

Q2 DECIDED 2026-09-20 (three-reader panel, .context/m7-q2-*.md; the clock gap landed as F60). SILENCE relation: one request body, two enrolments (NOT two PIN bodies; CNF-40 is the conformance approximation). Horizon = the duress run's CURRENT T (DUR-13 then DUR-14 shrinks), guard on the state ENTERING each step so the arming receipt is always inside the prefix (its effects are the last shared observable, and DEF-12's twin sits there); sticky by prefix quantification, since Effective is not monotone. Freeze-invisible is a LIVE INVARIANT over the holder-decision scan, not an unconditional inequality, and carries a non-decreasing-sample hypothesis (F60). Obs carries response BYTES/refusal codes, Effect.broadcast, /healthz locked_down + last_deadline_tick, ordered peer effects with destinations and sizes — not shapes and aggregate counts; omits timing class, allocations, lock-hold time (F22/SEC-47). Theorem shape = coupling invariant between the two runs with equal observable effects per step, NOT observe-commutes-with-step. Twins: (a) DEF-12 arm-keyed marker, (b) F54 conditional window traversal, (c) static T — FAITHFUL, ADR-0012's 2026-07-15 log says "One true silence break -> FIXED: dynamic T", so a real guard parameter; plus a fourth NEGATIVE EXHIBIT (not a flip): duress-only selected-entry insertion, which also opens SPN-41's capacity probe. One node; the federation horizon is the first node's crossing, a corollary, and no federation claim is made.

Q3 DECIDED 2026-09-20 (three-reader panel, .context/m7-q3-*.md; landed as F61 CLOSED + F62 OPEN + POL-20 and DOM-24 amended). Accounting bridge = a ledger transition model (reserve at acceptance POL-18/SPN-29, refund only at terminal-without-exposure POL-18/SPN-33, one-way age-out POL-19) COMPOSED WITH milestone 4's kernel — a ledger-only model cannot make ADR-0014's trace reachable (needs holder decisions, releases, settlement, completion). Bookkeeping: Ledgers.counting has TWO hypotheses (hcap, hq), not three; hq already fuses "at least t-c acceptances" with "still charged at the cut", so H2/H3 are bridge lemmas, not arguments. No-age-out lemma: TRUE, needs only that the reservation is in the trailing interval; POL-17 not needed; saturating Nat subtraction truncates toward live; requires non-decreasing HotClock samples in the trace (Kernel.Reachable admits arbitrary Env samples today — add the premise). Cohort exclusion is PER RESERVATION; per spend the conclusion is false. H1 needs the one-way-release model (F62). A1 also needs a reservation map keyed by commitment id with the authoritative amount, and a well-formed cohort (distinct ids, amounts matching) or Ledgers.charge's hcap cannot be derived. ADR-0014 refutation is EXISTENTIAL over a reachable trace (exists start, completed in [start, start+W) > (n/t) x cap), not a bare forall-negation; the trace hits exactly 2V so it refutes the n/t reading and NOT the loss-div-t sizing rule. New twin required by decision 6: DEF-5 / F57's settlement-refund row (current retains on mempool-only settlement per SPN-33, withdrawn refunds on any settlement), distinct from milestone 4's pending-log flag. The ledger is NOT in Obs but IS part of Q2's two-run relational invariant (later HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED and work counts are observable); DUR-11 keeps the freeze off it, POL-21 puts the frozen candidate's refund strictly after Lockdown, past the horizon.
close_reason: Milestone 7 complete: the Armed overlay, the coverage denominator, the Hot ledger and accounting bridge, and SILENCE as a two-run relation, with F59-F64 recorded along the way

title: Milestone 3: lifecycle arithmetic (F52 alternation, POL-20 counting theorem, SPN-38 cross-node prefix)
description: ADR-0023 decision 10 item 3; pulled ahead of the encoders by both panel readers. (a) SPN-46 age over a ChainView structure (tip, confirming : TxId → Option Block, mtp : Block → Nat) with the source as a guard parameter .chainMtp | .perNodeLog; F52's alternation table (one compromised signer rotating which honest node co-signs, seven links in fifteen days against a thirty-day interval) admitted under .perNodeLog and refused at its second link under .chainMtp on every honest node; the WTC-25 replacement exhibit (unconfirmed refresh's higher-fee replacement admissible under .chainMtp). (b) POL-20's counting theorem over a list of honest ledgers: each ledger's charges <= cap, each counted spend in >= t − c ledgers ⇒ (t − c) A <= (n − c) cap; corollaries per shape. Not the accounting bridge (milestone 7). (c) SPN-38 cross-node cumulative prefix: two nodes with equal a and latches one apart release overlapping prefixes so DUR-28's 'highest rung at or below the latch with >= t partials on every input' is reached. Acceptance: each twin red on its flip; the F51 DUR-30-split row.
close_reason: Milestone 3 landed on main as 26fa141 (direct implementation; all nine gates green; F52 source flip red at exactly the two F52 exhibits and the F51 anchor flip red at five, both run locally as the workflow runs them)

title: Milestone 4: the release and Carrier kernel (panel done 2026-09-17; build as ADR-0023 decision 10 item 4 amended)
description:
ADR-0023 decision 10 item 4 AS AMENDED by the second panel (2026-09-17, `.context/m4-panel-brief.md`
and the two answer files; both readers: amend, then build). The item is the spec;
this bead is its build order. Both readers' scratch kernels closed on core Lean; the second reader's
(~500 lines + Exhibits) is house-shaped and is the starting
point.

Modules (namespace BtcPolicy):
- `Clocks.lean`: `Wall`, `Effective`, `Mono`, `Mtp`, `HighWater` with `private mk ::` and private
  fields; `Effective.ofWall` (SPN-13), `Mono.deadline : Mono → Wall → Effective → Option Mono`
  (NCH-33); `Mono.before`, `Wall.atOrBefore`, `Mono.withinWindow` (POL-19 as written: raw
  wall_now). No coercions. No generation index.
- `Kernel.lean`: `Node` (armed, poisoned, lockedDown, carriers with cid/duress/holders/E/D, candidates
  with hot/quorum/frozen/terminal/settled/broadcast/released/packageOk/fireAt:Option/expiry),
  `World` (node + exposure : List (Sighash × input × signer)), `Env` (wall, hw, mono, chain view
  with seen txs), `Event` (accept, receipt, firePass, packageAccepted, send, settle, prune, tick,
  panic, adversaryExposes), `nodeStep`, `step` (world lift), `pending` as a projection. Guard
  parameters each an inductive with `current` in the owning module: retirement (mono | wall,
  NCH-35), `Reauth` (beforeSend | beforeAssembly, DUR-29/SPN-39), `PoisonGate` (asserted |
  byLockOrder, DUR-9), `Defeat` (terminalFlag | mempoolResidency, SPN-33). Sighash as a named
  boundary structure (function of tx and input index only), a parameter of step.
- Theorems in Kernel: `no_hot_partial_while_armed` + `inv_reachable` by induction over
  `Reachable`; `D_immutable`; `armed_sticky`; `exposure_monotone`; `terminal_sticky`,
  `terminal_never_due`, settle-marks-conflicts; `poisoned_releases_nothing`; `receipt` touches
  holders only.
- `Exhibits.lean` (only place theorems over `current` live): DEF-1 excursion twin (keeps intent /
  loses it), decision-9 exposure case (two commitments one sighash: world-level finalizable,
  commitment-keyed and node-local-pruned both false), CNF-143 trace twin (no broadcast / broadcast),
  DEF-4 poison twin, F57 row 8 twin, positive normal release, bounded enumeration from the
  package-accepted state (depth 2 finds the race under the flip; docstring states start state +
  alphabet + "exhibit, no completeness").
- Tags: NCH-33, NCH-35, DUR-5, DUR-8, DUR-9, DUR-11, DUR-29, SPN-13, SPN-33, SPN-38, SPN-39,
  POL-19 at clause granularity; no CNF id in tools/formal (decision 2).
- CI (gates.yml + check_gate_controls if needed): four flips red in Exhibits.lean only with exact
  counts (measure on a scratch copy first); plus a compile-must-fail control for the DEF-1 term
  (Wall passed where Mono expected: exact "Application type mismatch") and for the private-field
  hole (raw field / minted constructor refused); a coercion added in a scratch mutant must make
  the control fail.
- A rendered region is NOT required by this milestone; if one is emitted, it goes under
  `### DEF-1 — …` (regions gate fixed for heading-form requirements, bps-dzd).

Scope cut (stated in the module docstring): hot egress only; Escape half of the CNF-143 race,
overlay beyond `armed`, selected_escapes, Hot ledger, T dynamics, DEF-7 preflight, multi-node
world → milestone 7. Boundary hypotheses named in the docstring: unforgeability, backend truth,
delivery/F39, lock discipline, ≤ t−1 compromise, clock sample provenance, SEC-45 wrong-at-acceptance.

Done when: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green, every flip measured red locally,
`lake exe gate` walks every new tagged declaration under the allowed axioms, one commit on main +

title: Milestone 8: backend, operator and runtime refinement (reorg cursor, delivery reducer, trace adapters)
description:
ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "Reorg cursor and cache model (DEF-6, DEF-21), the delivery reducer
and watch selection (DEF-8, F56), and implementation trace adapters — the boundary at which
btc-policy-lean's runtime evidence meets the model." This is the boundary where runtime evidence
meets the model; nothing here is a proof about a running node.

SPLIT, planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after a three-adviser consultation, mirroring milestone 7's component-sized tickets:

  .11.1  DONE (7d17216): Delivery.lean, the delivery-knowledge reducer and watch target
         (OPR-49..OPR-51), DEF-8 and F56 as guard twins.
  .11.2  Watchtower cursor and scan proofs: WTC-11 (three of four sites), WTC-12, WTC-13,
         WTC-14; owns the shared backend-view vocabulary; guard CursorShape -> DEF-6.
  .11.3  Vault-unspent cache and wallet anchor: WTC-5..WTC-10 and WTC-11's fourth site; guard
         ImportBracket -> DEF-21. Blocked on .11.2.
  .11.4  Watchtower recognition and alert queue: WTC-17..WTC-22; guard Recognition
         (validated | coSigned | evaluated, dated ADR-0001 -> ADR-0012) with WTC-18's two
         refutations as twins; pays Silence.lean's WTC-20 debt. Blocked on .11.2 (WTC-21).
  .11.5  Package ancestry and replacement: WTC-23..WTC-25 (WTC-25 partly in RefreshAge.lean
         under F52, not duplicated); guard ReplacementAncestry -> F54's row. Blocked on .11.2
         and .11.3.
  .11.6  The language-neutral trace FORMAT (alphabet record, round trip, one decided synthetic
         trace, negative exhibits); no guard. Blocked on .11.2..11.5. NOT blocked on bps-8s0.7:
         the replay adapter is implementation and lives in btc-policy-lean.

DECISIONS RECORDED. Two modules for cursor and cache, not one (their theorems need different
facts; the vocabulary is owned once). The watchtower ticket splits at the package boundary
(WTC-23..25 drive Kernel.packageAccepted, not the watchtower state machine). The watchtower is a
duty of every node, not a deployment (ADR-0001; reconfirmed 2026-09-24).

OUT OF THIS MILESTONE, on purpose. WTC-15: its arithmetic is already formalized in
BumpTarget.lean under DUR-30, and its backend-selection contract is operational. WTC-16 is a
MAY the composer holds that never enters a node decision. WTC-2's weighted median is not
formalized anywhere and is not claimed here. F45 (alert delivery when the channel is down) is a
design question about delivery, not detection, and stays an open finding.

Order: .11.2, then .11.3 and .11.4 in either order, then .11.5, then .11.6.

title: Formal gate accepts sorryAx on untagged constants: a @[csimp] lemma proved by sorry reroutes the emitters with every gate green
description:
The formal gate walks every project constant (`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Exe.lean:99-110`) but tests only `isNativeDecideAxiom` on untagged constants; `sorryAx` on an UNTAGGED project constant is accepted. So a `@[csimp]` lemma "proved" by `sorry` registers a compiler replacement for a tagged definition, the emitters print the replacement, and every step of `tools/check_formal.sh` stays green. `csimp` is also absent from the source grep at `tools/check_formal.sh:37` (only `implemented_by` / `extern`).

Reproduced 2026-09-16 in a scratch copy at HEAD `ac6ff47`: append to `BtcPolicy/Cursor.lean` before `end BtcPolicy.Cursor`

```
def fastCap (_ : Anchor) (_ _ _ _ _ : Nat) : Option Nat := some 99
@[csimp] theorem quotaRungCap_fast : @quotaRungCap = @fastCap := by sorry
```

then `nix develop --command bash tools/check_formal.sh` exits 0 (build green with only a `declaration uses sorry` warning, "0 outside the axiom policy", leanchecker --fresh accepted every declaration) and `tools/formal/.lake/regions.jsonl`'s SPN-38 table carries `| 99 |`. Same defect class as the macro-expanded implemented_by that commit 949d63f closed; ADR-0023 decision 3 says the emitters print what the kernel proved about.

Repair: apply the `allowed` axiom filter (the one line 118 applies to tagged declarations) to EVERY project constant, not only tagged ones — that refuses `sorryAx` anywhere in the project, which closes the csimp path and the untagged-sorry path together. Add the csimp source form to the `implemented_by`/`extern` grep too if a one-line grep covers it, but the axiom walk is the load-bearing fix. ADR-0023 decision 3 currently says `Explore` "may hold untagged scratch": amend in place so scratch under Explore is also sorry-free (or say Explore holds nothing that fails the walk). Add one CI negative control in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` in the shape of the existing formal-gate controls: the csimp+sorry mutation above in a `cp -r` scratch copy, `check_formal.sh` red, the log naming the refused constant.

Acceptance criteria:
- The reproduction above is red at `lake exe gate`, naming `quotaRungCap_fast` (or whichever constant carries the sorry) and `sorryAx`.
- A new gates.yml step proves it, runnable locally with the same commands.
- KEEP working: the unmodified tree is green on `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`; every existing formal-gate control in gates.yml still red for its stated reason; an untagged, sorry-free scratch declaration under `BtcPolicy.Explore` is still accepted.
- ADR-0023 decision 3 amended in place to match (git keeps history; a wholesale rewrite of the paragraph is fine).
- Files: `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Exe.lean`, `tools/check_formal.sh` (optional grep), `.github/workflows/gates.yml`, `docs/adr/0023-*.md`. No other files.

Source: reviewer A's review of commit 949d63f (confirmation pass, 2026-09-16), reproduced independently. Reviewer D did not report it.
close_reason: landed in 5aa3830: axiom filter over every project constant, csimp grep, CI negative control, ADR-0023 decision 3 amended

title: Copies gate per-file hit count misses a swap: a malformed copy plus a new valid copy in one file is green
description:
`tools/check_copies.py:265-266` holds the corpus-wide copies scan to a per-file HIT COUNT baseline (`tools/copies-baseline.json`): red on a fall, red on an unrecorded rise. A count cannot see a swap: when one existing copy becomes unrecognizable and a new valid copy is added in the same file, the per-file count is unchanged and the malformed copy escapes.

Reviewer D's example (unverified, verify first): in `README.md` change `(2 − 1/t)` to `(3 − one/t)` and append a valid `(2 − 1/t)` elsewhere in the same file; the gate exits 0, although AGENTS.md says an inline figure is held to the value its declaration emits.

the exclusions (selected-Escape and resident-rung outputs), then union in each distinct selected
input outpoint ONCE at its `witness_utxo` value, counted whatever the read says of it; counted
inputs take precedence over every exclusion. Never subtract after unioning.

Theorems:
- Within one pass every selected Escape is measured against the same value.
- The floor: on every pass the denominator is at least the union of the selected Escapes' inputs.
- Per-node single sweep: two input-disjoint Escapes both selected at this node's first release
  cannot both cover, whatever moved the denominator between their passes.
- Aggregate burn: this node's total sweep burn is at most `100 − escape_coverage_pct` percent of
  what it sweeps, which is also what makes DUR-24's own fee-cap sentence true.

Bridge to `Ledgers.counting`, which has TWO hypotheses, `hcap` and `hq`, not three: `hq` already

  samples, without which a charge can be released at one sample and be live again at a later one.

  each cohort amount equal to the stored amount, distinct honest ledgers.
- The cohort counts only reservations not refunded while unexposed, PER RESERVATION: per spend the
  counting theorem's conclusion is false, not merely unproved (F61).

since the trace needs holder decisions, releases, settlement and completion. State the refutation

the docstring: timing class, allocation counts, store-lock hold time. Counts are not durations
(F22, SEC-47: "End-to-end timing has no hard gate"), and a unit-cost model must not be advertised
as constant-time.

Two worlds: ONE request body with two enrolments, the enrolment table being the secret. Not two
PIN bodies — the coordinator knows what it sent, so two bodies differ in a public input. CNF-40's
"identical under both PINs" is the conformance experiment that approximates this, not its
statement.

The relation is a COUPLING INVARIANT between the two runs with equal observable effects at each
step, not `observe ∘ step = stepObs ∘ observe`: identical observations do not determine the next
output, and exposing hidden fields to make a projection commute would defeat the purpose.

The horizon is a guard on the state ENTERING each step: unarmed, or the effective sample below
that state's current `T`. So the arming receipt is always inside the prefix and its own effects
are the last shared observable, which is where DEF-12's twin lives. Sticky by prefix
quantification, because `Effective` is not monotone. The horizon may be zero (DUR-14: "a hot
spend whose Hold already matured at arm time collapses the window to now").

Freeze-invisible is a LIVE INVARIANT over DUR-13's holder-decision scan, carrying 7.1's
non-decreasing-sample premise: without it a matured hot spend is due under normal and frozen
under duress at a sample still below `T` (F60, the retained trace).

Twins, guard parameters red in `Exhibits.lean` only: DEF-12's marker keyed on the arm bit instead
of the pin-uniform `committed`; F54's conditional window traversal; and static `T` — faithful,
ADR-0012's 2026-07-15 log records "One true silence break → FIXED: dynamic T". Plus ONE negative
exhibit that is not a flip: a duress-only selected-entry insertion, which also opens SPN-41's
capacity probe.

The ledger (7.3) is not in `Obs` but is part of the relational invariant: a duress-only refund
surfaces later as a HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED and in the work counts.

Scope: one node. DUR-1 is per node ("Every observable a node emits"); peers' relays are inputs
held equal, and the federation horizon is the first node's crossing, stated as a corollary by
events with no federation claim made. Docstring names what is not claimed: machine timing, a
compromised node or pre-wrench coordinator (SEC-10), any Lockdown latency (DUR-15, F13, SEC-48),
the cover story's plausibility, and anything past `T`. F3, F4, F13 and F60 stay traces with no
repair chosen.

CONTEXT.md gains **observer projection** and **concealment horizon** when this lands (ADR-0023
decision 7: the terms enter the glossary when the first model uses them). Done when check-all is
green and all three flips are measured red locally. One commit + beads close.

title: Receipts carry their sender: Carrier.holders becomes distinct relay senders (F65, DUR-5, DUR-6)
description:
Direction chosen 2026-09-21, unanimous across a three-reader panel. None of the three
accepted the first proposal (keying exposure by recipient); all three kept `ADR-0023`
decision 9 intact.

WHAT TO BUILD. Give the receipt event its authenticated sender and replace the Carrier's
holder count with relay sender identities.

    | receipt (cid : Nat) (sender : Nat)      -- the wire's sender_node_id

    structure Carrier where
      ...
      relaySenders : List Nat                 -- replaces holders : Nat

    -- holder count = 1 + (eraseDups relaySenders).length; self stays implicit

WHY IT IS FORCED, not cosmetic. `DUR-5` counts "each distinct peer whose authenticated
relay of the same Carrier this node receives"; `DUR-6` requires "a sender already counted,
an uncommitted duplicate, or a committed intent MUST be an idempotent no-op". A `Nat`
cannot express "already counted", so one peer relaying twice reaches `t` and opens
`DUR-8`'s release gate a relay early, under either PIN. `ADR-0012` already specifies the
mechanism: a node "counts ITSELF ... plus the distinct `sender_node_id`s that relay it
back, and arms once that holder set reaches t".

WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY. Not a new safety result. `ADR-0012`: the count "is a timing/liveness
mechanism, NOT the safety proof"; the proof is the release gate, already carried by
`Kernel.no_hot_partial_while_armed`. Expect fidelity to `DUR-5` and `DUR-6`, plus a new
negative exhibit — one peer relaying twice arming a node below threshold.

DO NOT TOUCH decision 9 or `Exp`. Exposure is world level by execution, not omission:
"a commitment-keyed or node-local history loses the authority a partial released under one
commitment carries for a second over the same transaction, in both readers' probes".
`Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.exposure_key_exhibit` is that probe retained as a trap and
`no_resident_release_does_not_mean_safe` is the false statement a node-local reading proves.
`CONTEXT.md`: exposed authority "outlives everything node-local". `CONTEXT.md` also bans
"peer id" under *Node id*.

SILENCE. All three readers expect the two-run relation to survive: `Silence.Input.pinless`
feeds one common event to both runs and `pubCarrier` erases only `duress`, so sender
history stays coupled without widening `Obs`. The senders must be COUPLED, not erased —
equal counts with different holder sets diverge on the next duplicate. Repairs reach
`commits_pub`, `receipt_pub`, `pubCarrier`, the event cases and the marker/work proofs;
expected local and wide, not structural. Nobody could build, so this is unverified.

BLAST RADIUS. `Kernel`: `Carrier`, `Event.receipt`, `commits`, `receipt`, the `inv_step`
case (which never reads holders). `Silence`: the lemmas above. `Ledger.afterEvent`: new
arity. `Exhibits`: ~20 `.receipt` constructions. Decision 9, `Exp`, `finalizable`,
`Ledger`'s POL-18/POL-20 exhibits: untouched.

STILL OPEN, not part of this ticket. `Kernel.finalizable` decides `packageAccepted` from
world-level availability, so the model admits a node assembling a package from partials it
never received. One reader would split it — a global predicate still reading the exposure
so the trap keeps its subject, and a local one reading possession on `Cand` so candidate
pruning removes possession while world exposure stays forever — which needs an explicit
authenticated partial-receive event, since `adversaryExposes` must not imply delivery. The
other two would document the boundary and wait for delivery semantics. Decide separately.

PLACEMENT. Not milestone 8 (bps-8s0.11 is WTC reorg, OPR-49..51 outbound delivery
knowledge, STO trace adapters). `ADR-0023` decision 10 has no item for this; record a dated
scope extension referencing milestones 4 and 7 rather than rewriting their acceptance.

PRIMARY SOURCES, out of main. `prototype/federation-invariant` 2214a5f — `BtcPolicy/Fed.lean`
lifts `Kernel.Inv` to `Fin n -> Node` in nine lines of proof over an arbitrary interleaving,
for all n, axioms [propext, Quot.sound]. Its `finalizable_without_receiving` proves no
reachable execution — the premise supplies the count — so cite it as a statement about the
predicate, never as a trace. `prototype/quint-vs-decide` c176c67 — the retracted tool
measurement, four defects in `RESULTS.md`; tag `quint-prototype-as-reviewed` holds the
hashes an external companion cites.
close_reason:
Landed in d0245f7. Event.receipt carries sender_node_id; Carrier.relaySenders replaces holders : Nat; holderCount adds this node.

Two deviations from the ticket, both narrowing:

1. The ticket says 'holder count = 1 + (eraseDups relaySenders).length'. addSender dedups on INSERT instead, so the field is already a set and holderCount is length + 1. Stronger: DUR-6's 'idempotent no-op' becomes the identity on the Carrier, not a count that happens not to move (duplicate_relay_changes_nothing reads the clause literally). eraseDups on read was probed and has no usable core-Lean lemma for (l ++ [s]).eraseDups.length without Mathlib; addSender_nodup proves the set property the length rests on instead.

2. addSender also refuses this node's own id, which the ticket did not call out. DUR-5 counts 'each distinct PEER' and this node is already the +1, so without it a relay carrying the node's own sender_node_id counted the node twice and reached t a relay early — the same defect as the duplicate. Found by the code-review Standards axis. self_relay_is_not_a_second_holder is the exhibit.

Negative exhibit: duplicate_relay_is_one_holder. The withdrawn count is written out beside the holder set; the quorum conjunct is what goes red if the count comes back (the withdrawn count itself is trace arithmetic and runs no kernel term).

Untouched as instructed: ADR-0023 decision 9, Exp, finalizable, Ledger's POL-18/POL-20 exhibits. SILENCE preserved with the sender coupled, Obs not widened.

ADR-0023 decision 10 carries the dated scope extension against milestones 4 and 7. F65 stays OPEN on the finalizable half only.

title: F65: candidate possession — Cand.heldSigners, the shape everything else reads
description:
Land the possession field the rest of F65's open half reads. No behaviour change:
nothing consumes it yet.

WHAT TO BUILD.

    structure Cand where
      ...
      heldSigners : List Nat     -- DUR-28's "distinct valid partials", as this node holds them

`born` overwrites it with `[n.id]`: SPN-36 says a candidate is "born fully signed and fully
withheld" and SPN-32 that "The node MUST sign the spend, the Escape and every rung at
ingress", so this node's own signer is a member from registration. Do NOT add a separate
`ownSigned` bit -- `node.id` distinguishes self, and `born` always signs.

An idempotent insert helper, mirroring `addSender` but WITHOUT its self-refusal: NCH-25 says
"The store holds at most one partial per (rung, input, signer). A duplicate is an idempotent
ACCEPTED and never displaces the first", and self is a member here rather than excluded.

SHAPE, decided unanimously by a three-reader panel (.context/f65d-*). A bare `List Nat` of
signers, NOT `List (input, signer)` and NOT `List Exp`. This kernel collapses the input and
rung dimensions already -- `finalizable` filters `e.input == 0`, `firePass` emits
`queuePartial (sighash c.tx 0) 0`, and `Exp`'s docstring says "Input 0 stands for every
input" -- so a pair whose left component is permanently zero mimes DUR-28's "on every input"
rather than modelling it, and costs a pair's DecidableEq inside `decide +kernel`. `Exp` is
refused because `cid` and `hot` are diagnostic exposure metadata and CONTEXT.md says exposed
authority "outlives everything node-local", so hanging it on a prunable Cand fights the term.
State the deferred input and rung dimensions in one docstring sentence, as `Exp` already does
for one of them.

Read the field with `.eraseDups.length` wherever it is counted, so the count is total over
arbitrary Lean values rather than resting on a reachable-state invariant. This is deliberately
the OPPOSITE of the `relaySenders` decision in d0245f7/2e0c190, and the difference is why:
`holderCount` uses bare `length`, so it needed `relaySenders_nodup`; nothing counts increments
here.

`pubCand` MUST preserve `heldSigners` exactly -- a `pubCand_held` lemma plus a set congruence.
It is pin-uniform state; erasing it makes `packageAccepted_pub` unprovable later, because the
two runs' counts must be equal. `inv_frame` needs NO new component: `NodeInv` reads only
sweepActive, armed, frozen, hot, fireAt, windowClose and `hotBoundAt`'s fields, none of them
possession. (Verified against Silence.lean at 2e0c190.)

ALSO IN THIS TICKET. Rename `Exhibits.finalizableNodeLocal` to `releasedResidentQuorum`. It is
decision 9's retained WRONG model -- "the count a node-local history pruned with the candidate
would give" -- and leaving that name beside a real possession predicate puts two incompatible
notions of node-local finalizability in one file.

DONE WHEN. `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, the field exists and is
preserved by the projection, and no predicate reads it yet.
close_reason: Landed in db9983e. Two additions past the ticket's letter, both in its direction: addHeld_of_held, so the NCH-25 tag names a declaration a theorem exercises, and a docstring on Exhibits.cand recording that a directly seeded registry (twinNode, soloNode) holds no possession, which bps-8s0.14's exhibits must route around. The field, born's seed, addHeld, pubCand_held, pubCand_set_held and the releasedResidentQuorum rename are as specified; nothing reads the field yet.

title: F65: split finalizability — exposedQuorum (POL-18) beside heldQuorum (DUR-28)
description:
Split finalizability in two and give each half the requirement it actually renders. No
behaviour change: `packageAccepted` still reads the world-level predicate at the end of this
ticket.

WHAT TO BUILD.

Rename `Kernel.finalizable` to `exposedQuorum` and retag it `@[req "POL-18"]`. POL-18 is the
sentence it renders: "A partial that has left the node is finalizable authority in `t - 1`
compromised hands". It was tagged `@[req "DUR-28"]`, which is a misattribution -- DUR-28 is
"Finalization takes the highest rung at or below the latch with >= t distinct valid partials
on every input", a statement about what a node finalizes FROM. DUR-28 does not lose a Lean
home: `Cursor.finalized`, `Cursor.finalized_reaches`, `Cursor.split_finalizes_lower_latch` and
`Exhibits.dur30_split_finalizes_lower_latch` all carry it.

Add `heldQuorum (t : Nat) (c : Cand) : Bool`, tagged `@[req "DUR-28"]`, reading
`c.heldSigners.eraseDups.length`. Name chosen to pair with `exposedQuorum` and to avoid
implying the package, authorization and exact-vsize checks have passed -- DUR-28 requires
those separately.

Callers of the renamed predicate are wider than they look: `Exhibits.exposure_key_exhibit`,
`no_resident_release_does_not_mean_safe`, `HotLedger.def5_refused_with_current`,
`def5_admitted_with_withdrawn`, the F63 exposure exhibit, and `Ledger.lean`'s docstrings all

MARKDOWN WITH THE DECLARATION, per AGENTS.md. Add the `Held partial` glossary entry's
counterpart wherever DUR-28's local basis needs stating, citing SPN-36's "the partials
received per (input, signer)" and NCH-25's store rule. Do not restate the rule in a second
document.

title: F65: authenticated partial receipt — receivePartial, exposure and possession separated
description:
Give the model an authenticated inbound partial. Until this exists `adversaryExposes` is the
only way another signer's partial enters the world, which is why the model cannot tell
exposure from delivery. No behaviour change to assembly: `packageAccepted` still reads
`exposedQuorum` at the end of this ticket.

WHAT TO BUILD.

    | receivePartial (msg : Sighash) (input : Nat) (signer : Nat) (cid : Nat)

Deliberately `adversaryExposes`'s exact four arguments, so the trace migration in
bps-f65-cutover is a token swap rather than a rewrite.

The step does TWO things, and they must NOT be fused into one guarded match:

  1. Append the `(msg, input, signer)` row to `World.exposure`, UNCONDITIONALLY. A partial
     that reached this node has left its signer whatever this node then does with it. NCH-24
     answers `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE` for a pruned candidate -- fuse the two and the model claims
     a partial this node dropped never left its signer, which weakens the premise
     `exposure_key_exhibit` is retained to trap.
  2. Insert the signer into `heldSigners` ONLY on candidate lookup, guarded by
     `msg == sighash c.tx 0`.

BOUNDARY HYPOTHESIS, named in the docstring, not modelled. NCH-24 requires, in order, wallet
equality, signer equals sender, sighash type, the candidate exists, it is not expired, the
rung is found by txid, the user-signature hash matches, "the input and signer are in range",
and that "the signature verifies against this node's own recomputed sighash for that rung and
input and the signer's descriptor key (CHN-11); then store it". This event is the successful
post-validation store. Authenticated is NOT storable, and an event that merely carried a
signer id could otherwise manufacture possession. NCH-24's "except the delayed-slot exemption
of SPN-41" stays out of scope exactly as `Kernel.prune` already declares for the Escape
exemption.

SILENCE. `Input.pinless`, one common event in both runs, no branch on `armed`, duress or the
selected bits. `Obs` does not widen -- but the event must not simply fall through `respond`'s
`| _ => .silent` catch-all: NCH-25 makes a duplicate an idempotent `ACCEPTED`, so either reuse
`.ack` (already documented as "DUR-6's idempotent no-op, and a relay counted") or define the
event as an internal post-response transition and say which in the docstring.

BLAST RADIUS. Exhaustive `Event` matches in Kernel (inv_step, armed_sticky, D_immutable,
terminal_sticky, exposure_monotone, sweepActive_sticky, selected_grows,
T_written_only_by_arm_or_accept, relaySenders_nodup_step), `Ledger.afterEvent` and
`liveSum_afterEvent_le`, and SILENCE's step/invariant/work/marker proofs.

EXHIBITS. Receipt admits a peer and raises the held count; a duplicate receive asserts
UNCHANGED heldSigners -- not an unchanged `World`, because the exposure row may legitimately
append again; exposure without receipt still reaches `exposedQuorum` and not `heldQuorum`.

DONE WHEN. Gate green, the event exists, assembly unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented in 147f2bd953c5ed003a08c88f74ae9b11d68397df. Event.receivePartial preserves adversaryExposes's argument order; the world appends exposed authority unconditionally while the NCH-24-tagged store inserts through addHeld only on matching candidate id and recomputed sighash. Complete upstream validation is a named boundary hypothesis. SILENCE uses an explicit silent internal post-response arm and preserves the common pinless input and existing theorem statements. Receipt, exact duplicate-held-list identity, exposure-without-possession, pruned-candidate and mismatched-message exhibits pass. Assembly still uses exposedQuorum; existing peer traces, alphabet and exposure_key_exhibit are unchanged. F65 remains open for the cutover. Ran nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh unpiped before and after implementation: exit 0, every gate PASS; final formal index 499 tagged declarations, zero constants outside policy, fresh-kernel replay accepted every declaration.

title: F65: cutover — packageAccepted reads possession, with the bridge theorem
description:
Switch assembly onto node-local possession. This is the behavioural cutover and it lands as
one commit: the predicate swap, the release conjunct, the proof repairs and the trace
migration cannot be green apart.

WHAT TO BUILD.

`packageAccepted` reads `c.released && heldQuorum w.node.t c` in place of `exposedQuorum w c`
(the conjunct bps-8s0.13 left it reading).

THE `released` CONJUNCT IS A MODELLING ORDER, NOT A RULE READ OFF THE SET. Say so in the
docstring. SPN-39 puts finalization on the fire pass -- "On every fire pass, for each due
candidate, the node MUST ... finalize" -- but SPN-38 permits a pass that releases nothing:
"If `affordable_rungs = 0`, release nothing and advance no release bookkeeping on this pass."
`released` is therefore a valid proxy for "a pass processed this candidate" only inside this
kernel's no-quota abstraction, where `firePass` releases every due candidate. Word it as "this
node released the rung being assembled": `Cand` carries no ladder and the kernel finalizes at
`sighash c.tx 0`, so `released` IS `released_through` at rung 0, and the sentence upgrades to
`released_through >= rung` when DUR-28's latch enters the kernel. The durable shape is a
fire-pass assembly token carrying the selected rung; it is the
recorded upgrade path and is NOT built here, because an `Option Rung` field in a kernel with
no rungs is a boolean in disguise.

THE BRIDGE, as a theorem and not an exhibit: over reachable resident candidates,
`released && heldQuorum ==> exposedQuorum`. It needs `born`'s sanitization and the receive's
unconditional exposure append. It is FALSE for hand-built `World` values, so state it over
`Reachable`. Preserve the counterexample to unconditional inclusion -- own withheld possession
plus received peer authority -- since the two predicates remain incomparable in general.

SETTLED 2026-09-23, so no Consultation is needed: the bridge is FALSE over `Reachable` as the
kernel stands. `Kernel.receivePartial` takes no input; `step` for `.receivePartial m i s cid`
drops `i`, stores the signer whenever `c.id == cid && m == sighash c.tx 0`, and appends an
exposure row carrying `input := i`, while `exposedQuorum` counts only rows with
`e.input == 0`. So `.receivePartial (sighash tx1 0) 7 1 1` after acceptance gives
`heldQuorum` and, after `firePass`, `released`, with `exposedQuorum` false. The fix is
option (A), reached independently by the Manager of run 20260923T031645 and its adviser:
`Kernel.receivePartial` takes the input and the store guard becomes
`c.id == cid && input == 0 && msg == sighash c.tx 0`; the exposure append stays
unconditional. A partial on an unmodelled input is exposed authority but not modelled
possession, which is `Exp`'s "input 0 stands for every input" applied to the store and
`NCH-24`'s "the input and signer are in range" at the only modelled input. Say so in the
guard's docstring. Do NOT take the alternative of dropping the `e.input == 0` filter from
`exposedQuorum`, `exposedQuorumOf` and `finalizableByCommitment`: it re-keys exposed
authority against `ADR-0023` decision 9's `(message, input, signer)` in four places. The
input-7 receipt is itself the "exposed but not held" half of the DONE WHEN exhibit.
`Silence.receivePartial_pub` gains the input argument and one conjunct; the call in the
Silence step case passes `j`. Existing receipt exhibits all pass input 0 and are unchanged.

Proof sketch: two invariants carried over `Reachable` -- every held signer other than self
has an input-0 exposure row on `sighash c.tx 0`, and `released` implies self's input-0 row
exists -- plus a nodup-subset-length lemma (no Mathlib here; prove `addHeld_nodup` beside
`addSender_nodup`).

ENUMERATION, DECIDED: the optional `safeStep` conjunct cannot fail from `wReady`, which
already holds quorum once its peer step is `receivePartial`, so take the docstring option.
The DUR-29 negative control in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` requires the reauthorization
flip to yield exactly two errors, both in `Exhibits.lean`, on `race_refused_with_current` and
`bounded_from_ready`; the migrated traces must keep that count. `def5`, `twoRequestsTrace`
and `partialExposedOnly` keep `adversaryExposes`: their peers are compromised or undelivered
by design. The "compromised signer 2" comments on `raceTrace` and `wReady` go with the swap.

SILENCE. Repair `packageAccepted_pub`. `Silence.exposedQuorumOf` exists only to strip the
`World` from the old predicate; once `packageAccepted` reads `heldQuorum`, which already takes
`(t, Cand)`, delete it or narrow it to whatever the exposure theorems still need.

TRACE MIGRATION. `normalTrace`, `raceTrace`, `wReady` and both `adr0014` legs swap their
synthetic `adversaryExposes` peer step for `receivePartial`. In the bounded `alphabet`,
REPLACE the `adversaryExposes` symbol rather than adding an eleventh -- `traces_count :
(traces 3).length = 1000` is a theorem and 11^3 = 1331 turns it red.

AND BE HONEST ABOUT THE ENUMERATION. `safeStep` checks only "no hot queuePartial, no
broadcast, every hot candidate frozen" -- none of which possession can affect -- so
`bounded_from_ready` will stay true and blind through the new code. Either give `safeStep` a
conjunct that the new gate can fail (no broadcast below `t` held), or state plainly in the
docstring that it is not evidence for this gate. Do not let the word count stand in for
coverage.

The comment "`adversaryExposes` is the only way a partial from another signer enters the
world" is already gone; what remains in `Exhibits.lean` is the trace docstring saying the
trace "still uses `adversaryExposes`" for an honest peer. After the migration that sentence
is false too, so rewrite it, and grep both `Kernel.lean` (its module docstring and the
`Event` docstring) and `Silence.lean` for any remaining sentence that describes
`adversaryExposes` as the peer-partial path.

DONE WHEN. Gate green, and a new exhibit separates the predicates: a node with exposed
authority it never received cannot assemble, and one that received can.
close_reason: Landed as 8a74bbe: packageAccepted reads released && heldQuorum, receivePartial guards input 0, bridge theorem released_held_exposed over Reachable, traces migrated to receivePartial, four separating exhibits. Gate green (all 9) on 8a74bbe; DUR-29 negative control exactly 2 errors. Four reviewers reported no findings against the commit; reviewer B's one finding, two stale F65 sentences, is carried into bps-8s0.16. The judge of run 20260923T033345 produced no ruling (its session ended waiting on a backgrounded gate), so closed on that evidence.

title: M8.1 Delivery.lean: OPR-49's sticky delivery reducer, OPR-51's reissue predicate and watch target, DEF-8 and F56 as twins
description:
Milestone 8, ticket 1 — the operator's delivery knowledge and the watch target, as a bounded state
machine (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "the delivery reducer and watch selection (`DEF-8`, `F56`)").
The first of milestone 8's tickets; the reorg cursor (WTC-11..14, DEF-6), the cache and wallet
anchor (WTC-5..10, DEF-21), the watchtower classification and ancestry rules (WTC-17..25) and the
trace adapters stay on the epic until each is planned.

New module `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Delivery.lean` (namespace `BtcPolicy.Delivery`), imported from
`BtcPolicy.lean`, with its theorems over `current` in `Exhibits.lean` and one CI flip per guard
parameter in `.github/workflows/gates.yml`:

- OPR-49's sticky delivery state as a reducer over a list of per-endpoint attempt outcomes:
  "definitely not sent" → "possibly delivered", advanced by every outcome that is not `NotSent`,
  never moved back. Outcomes distinguish pre-connect `NotSent` (connect failed, or OPR-48's
  endpoint reached at or after the aggregate) from every post-connect outcome: `accepted` with a
  `commitment_id`, `NONCE_REPLAYED`, `400`, `413`, any other status, and a timeout, partial write,
  read or framing failure.
- The loop's stop rule: stop on `accepted` whose id equals the locally computed one; stop on
  `NONCE_REPLAYED` only when the state entering that attempt was already possibly-delivered;
  everything else continues (a mismatched `accepted` keeps its possible delivery and continues).
- OPR-51's reissue predicate: authorized exactly when EVERY endpoint was `NotSent`, proved
  equivalent to the reducer ending at "definitely not sent"; a single endpoint's `NotSent`
  authorizes nothing.
- OPR-51's watch target by request kind: output 1 of the primary for `spend`, output 0 for
  `clawback` and `refresh`.
- Two guard parameters with twins: DEF-8 (a post-connect failure read as `NotSent` authorizes a
  reissue after every endpoint failed post-connect; refused under `current`), and F56 (the watch
  fixed on output 1 has no output to watch on a one-in-one-out `refresh`; `current` watches
  output 0).

Done when `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green unpiped, each new flip is red
in `Exhibits.lean` and nowhere else and measured locally as the workflow runs it, and every
existing flip is still red at its count. No Markdown owner changes; the Run's
brief (2026-09-23) has the detail.

title: Citation gate does not read Lean docstrings: quoted attributions under tools/formal/ are unguarded
description:
`tools/check_citations.py` reads `*.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` only (its `glob` calls); it never
opens `tools/formal/`. A Lean docstring that quotes a requirement — `Delivery.lean` alone carries
28 quoted attributions to `OPR-48`..`OPR-51`, `OPR-65`, `OPR-68`, `API-16`, `DEF-8` and `F56` —
is held to its owner's words by review alone, and a requirement edited later drifts from the
docstring without any gate going red. AGENTS.md's rule ("A claim about what another requirement
says carries that requirement's own words") applies to docstrings as it does to prose.

Found by the bps-8s0.11.1 review (the brief wrongly said the gate checks docstrings). Options:
extend the QUOTED rule of `check_citations.py` to `tools/formal/**/*.lean` docstrings (`/-- … -/`
and `/-! … -/`), with the same owner resolution and a negative control in `gates.yml`; or record
in AGENTS.md that Lean docstring quotes are review-checked only. The first keeps the rule one
rule; the second is honest about the gap. Decide, then land with its control.
close_reason: Landed in abf7e18: the QUOTED rule and the UNQUOTED ratchet read /-- -/ and /-! -/ docstrings under tools/formal/, three multi-attribution sentences split (Kernel.lean, Silence.lean), three unquoted attributions reworded to summary verbs (POL-20 and CHN-4 'gives', POL-4 'requires'; 'gives' is deliberate, both figures are held by check_copies.py), baseline at zero, negative control in gates.yml asserting exit 1 and the diagnostic, README row. Follow-ups: bps-8s0.18 (nested block comment fails open), bps-8s0.19 (colon-form attributions unverified: the gate checks 3 of Delivery.lean's quoted attributions, not 28).

title: check_citations.py: Lean docstring extractor fails open on a nested block comment; fail closed
description:
`tools/check_citations.py` extracts Lean docstrings with `DOCSTRING = /-[-!](.*?)-/` over raw
source (landed in abf7e18, bps-8s0.17). Two inputs Lean accepts defeat it, both verified by the
bps-8s0.17 review (reviewers C, D) in scratch copies that compiled:

1. A docstring nesting a block comment — `/-! Intro /- remark -/ … `OVR-1` says "false quote". -/`
   — is truncated at the inner `-/`, so a false attribution after it is silently missed: exit 0.
2. A `--` line comment carrying a whole `/-- `OVR-1` says "…". -/` pair is read as a docstring:
   exit 1 on text the gate says it does not read.

Neither shape exists in the tree today (917 docstring openers, 917 extracted, zero `/- -/` block
comments under `tools/formal/`, per reviewers A and B), and the code comment at
`DOCSTRING` says so. Case 1 is the one that matters: a silent miss in a gate whose purpose is to
not be silent. The smallest honest fix is fail-closed, not a lexer: refuse (exit 1, naming the
file) any extracted docstring body that contains `/-`, so a nested block comment inside a
docstring turns the gate red until someone extends the extractor. Case 2 can stay: a false quote
in a line comment being refused is harmless. Add a regression probe for case 1 beside the
"Prove the citation gate can fail on a Lean docstring" step in `.github/workflows/gates.yml`, or
in `tools/check_gate_controls.py`, asserting exit 1 and the diagnostic.
close_reason: Landed in b4b910b: load() reports docstrings nesting /- (closer reconstructed), main() refuses with exit 1 naming file:line; workflow control asserts exit 1 and the diagnostic; README row and module docstring state the contract. Gate green, 33/19 unchanged. Panel: reviewers B, C, D no findings; A incomplete.

title: Citation gate: colon-form attributions (`ID`: "…") are unverified in Markdown and Lean; 135 of 341 Lean quoted spans
description:
The citation gate's QUOTED rule binds a quote to an attribution verb (`says`, `states`, `reads`)
or a possessive noun (`X`'s rule that …). A colon-form attribution — `` `OPR-49`: "The state
starts …" `` — has no verb, so the grammar never sees it, in Markdown or in Lean; the gate's
module docstring says so since abf7e18. The exposure measured by the bps-8s0.17 review (reviewer B),
current tree:

- Markdown: 174 quoted spans of 4+ words, 16 colon-form, 14 checked sentences.
- Lean docstrings: 341 quoted spans, 135 colon-form, 19 checked sentences.

So `bps-8s0.17`'s "Delivery.lean carries 28 quoted attributions" resolves to 3 checked by the
landed gate; the colon form is the dominant shape there. Covering it — a third `ATTRIB` shape,
`` `ID`: "…" `` with the quote directly after the colon, same owner resolution — closes most of
what remains unguarded, and needs its own negative control. Keep the STO-43/STO-14 rule: the
owner is the id the colon attaches to, not the nearest citation. Nested straight quotes inside a
quotation (`Delivery.lean`'s module docstring, the `OPR-49` quote) will surface once colon-form
is checked; curly inner quotes or an ellipsis split resolve them. Related: nothing ratchets the
count of checked quoted attributions, so a `says` → `gives` edit drops a sentence out of coverage
with every gate green; a "may grow, never shrink" signature list like `citation-baseline.json`
would hold it, if the count line proves insufficient.
close_reason: Landed in 7d99a62: ATTRIB gains the colon form; each quote belongs to the last attribution starting before it (finditer, Consultation: advisers A and C both chose nearest-preceding); the UNQUOTED rule runs per attribution with the colon form exempt (a short or split quote is skipped, baseline stays at zero); the 7 predicted drifts fixed as docstring text in Cursor, Kernel, Ledger, Silence; workflow control appends a two-attribution colon-form probe and asserts DOM-1 blamed and OVR-1 not; README row; clean line now 141 attributions, 120 in Lean. Residue filed as the follow-up bead (nested straight quotes in Delivery.lean's OPR-49 quote, attribution-shaped phrases inside quotes, POL-18 HISTORICAL false positive).

title: Citation gate: the nested-comment control should probe the straddle shape (/-/) that only the reconstructed closer catches
description:
The control "Prove the citation gate refuses a block comment nested in a Lean docstring"
(`.github/workflows/gates.yml`, landed in b4b910b for bps-8s0.18) probes with
`/-! Intro /- remark -/ … -/`, whose extracted body already contains `/-`. The detector in
`check_citations.py` `load()` tests `m.group(1) + "-/"` — the reconstructed closer is
load-bearing for the straddle shape `/-! Intro /-/ remark -/ FALSE. -/` (valid, balanced Lean:
the body ends in `/` and the closer's `-` completes a nested opener), which the extracted body
alone does not flag. The bps-8s0.18 review (reviewer B) verified: flagged with the closer, silent
without; the current probe stays red either way, so a later simplification back to the bead's
literal wording ("any extracted docstring body that contains `/-`") goes green, not red.

Fix: change the probe's printf to the straddle form
`/-! Intro /-/ remark -/ `OVR-1` says "a phrase OVR-1 has never contained anywhere". -/`,
which exercises both paths in one expression (verified by the Manager on a scratch copy of
b4b910b: exit 1, `Delivery.lean:330: a docstring nests a /- -/ block comment`). Cosmetic, same
commit if wanted: three `f`-prefixed continuation strings without placeholders in `main()`'s
refusal message (F541; no Python lint gate exists).
close_reason: Landed as 485292b: the nested-comment control probes the straddle shape /-/ and the scratch replay shows it goes red when the reconstructed closer is removed. Gate green (all 9) on 485292b, re-run after the Run. Reviewers A, C, D: no findings. Reviewer B's finding, that the control now covers only the closer arm and a narrowed detector fails open on a plain nested comment, is filed as bps-8s0.22 by the Manager of run 20260923T064246, whose judge session ended waiting on a backgrounded gate before it could close this bead.

title: Citation gate: nested straight quotes in Delivery.lean's OPR-49 quote go unchecked; attribution-shaped phrases inside quotes; HISTORICAL false positive on POL-18
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.19 review (reviewer B), all verified on 7d99a62; none introduced by that
commit, all pre-existing limits of `QUOTE` pairing and `HISTORICAL` that the colon form now makes
visible. Small, docstring and comment work; one guard optional.

1. `Delivery.lean` module docstring, the `OPR-49` quote (line ~7): nested straight quotes.
   `QUOTE` pairs them alternately, so `"The state starts "` (3 words) and `", advances to "`
   (2 words) are dropped by the 4-word filter and only the tail `" on EVERY attempt … never moves
   backward."` is checked; the inner phrases `definitely not sent` and `possibly delivered, exact
   bytes` are checked by nothing. Verified: replacing both with false phrases leaves the gate at
   exit 0 with the count line unchanged. The bead bps-8s0.19 named this exact spot. Fix as
   `Cursor.lean`'s `DUR-30` was fixed in 7d99a62: curly inner quotes (`norm()` folds them), so the
   whole quotation is one checked span.
2. State the limit in `check_citations.py`'s module docstring next to the short-quote and
   split-boundary limits: a quotation with nested or unpaired straight quotes is cut into
   alternating spans, and the short ones go unchecked (the `QUOTE` comment already says "paired
   quotes only"). Also two prose imprecisions there: "never to the chunk's first" should read
   "never to the chunk's first merely because it is first"; and UNQUOTED is "no quote of its own,
   after it and before the next attribution", which is what `m.start() < p < end` implements.
3. An attribution-shaped phrase inside a quoted span becomes a spurious attribution: `finditer`
   sees `` `DOM-1` states `` inside a quotation as an attribution with an empty span, so it lands in
   UNQUOTED and the gate goes red on correct prose. Nothing in the tree trips it today (0 ATTRIB
   matches fall inside a quoted span), but 16 requirement bodies carry such a phrase (`OVR-8`,
   `DUR-34`, `SEC-33`, `OPS-7` carry `` `POL-20` states: ``; `MAN-2` carries `` `OPS-1` states ``;
   `SPN-43` carries `` `SPN-19` states ``), so it is one docstring quotation away. Either skip an
   ATTRIB match whose `start()` falls inside a `QUOTE` span (a few lines), or declare it in the
   limits passage; if guarded, a negative-or-positive control is not required, but the docstring
   must say which.
4. `Ledger.lean` ~line 420, the `POL-18` colon form is silently exempted: the requirement's own
   quoted words contain "the original", which `HISTORICAL` matches, so the whole chunk is skipped.
   `HISTORICAL` was out of scope for bps-8s0.19; decide whether to tighten that alternation
   (e.g. require it outside quoted spans) or record it as the third undeclared reason a colon form
   goes unchecked.

Done: gates green unpiped; `citation-baseline.json` at zero; docstring text only in Lean; no
Markdown requirement body changed.
close_reason: Landed in e96ef32: OPR-49 quotation one span, in-quote guard, HISTORICAL reads prose outside quotes, two CI controls; residue filed as bps-8s0.23

title: Citation gate: the nested-comment control covers one detector arm at a time; probe both shapes and assert the refusal count
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.20 review (reviewer B), verified on 485292b. The detector in

Fix, one step still: append BOTH docstrings in the probe —
`/-! Intro /-/ remark -/ ... -/` and `/-! Intro /- remark -/ ... -/` — keep the `rc -ne 1` check
and the per-file `grep -Eq`, and add `grep -q 'FAIL: 2 Lean docstring(s) nest a block comment'`

refuses it" — `load()` reports, `main()` refuses).

Optional, same commit: finish the F541 cleanup 485292b started — placeholder-free `f`-prefixed

title: Citation gate: the in-quote guard silences an attribution after an unpaired straight quote; the nested-quote limit understates the miss; nothing detects a new nested straight quote
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.21 and bps-8s0.22 reviews (reviewers A, B), verified on e96ef32 and
21e8141. All three items were SETTLED 2026-09-23 by the maintainer after a three-adviser
consultation (two rounds), so no Consultation is needed: build what is
written here. Reference design: /home/master/p/provisiond/tools/check_citations.py, the origin
of this gate, whose rule is positional -- a quote "belongs to whatever introduced it", i.e. the
attribution it follows -- and whose unpaired-quote failure is loud, never silent.

ITEM 1, SETTLED: the in-quote guard becomes OWNERSHIP-BASED. Today `find()` drops an `ATTRIB`
match that starts inside ANY raw `QUOTE` span; since `QUOTE` pairs straight quotes
alternately, a stray unpaired straight quote earlier in a chunk opens a bogus span that
swallows a real attribution, silently. Probe chunk:
    Field is 6" wide and `OVR-1` says "this phrase OVR-1 does not contain at all".
On 0beca6c `find()` reported OVR-1 UNQUOTED; on e96ef32 and HEAD `bad`, `unquoted` and
`checked` are all empty. Build: suppress an attribution `m` only when some quote span (s, e)
has `s < m.start() < e` AND an earlier attribution `a` exists with `a.end() <= s` and `a`
itself outside every span (so a quoted pseudo-attribution never becomes an owner). That is
bps-8s0.19's "each quote belongs to the attribution it follows" applied to suppression, and
provisiond's rule generalised to many attributions per chunk. The MAN-2/OPS-1 positive control
stays suppressed (MAN-2 precedes its quotation). All three advisers scanned HEAD's 155
attribution-bearing chunks under this predicate: ZERO chunks change classification; the only
two odd-count chunks (Delivery.lean OPR-49, Kernel.lean NCH-25) are colon-form quotes SPLIT cut
at a sentence end and are unaffected. Control: a `gates.yml` step appends the probe to a scratch
Lean docstring and asserts exit 1 plus `reports what OVR-1 says without quoting it` (the
baseline is at zero, so the signature is new). Docstring: the sentence "Nor is an
attribution-shaped phrase inside a quoted span, which is being quoted, not made" becomes
"inside a span an earlier attribution introduced"; "A quote before the first attribution
belongs to no one" is already true of quote assignment and stays.

ITEM 2, SETTLED: the nested-quote limit understates the miss. The passage says the quotation
is "cut into alternating spans, and the spans under four words go unchecked"; for the
canonical case the unchecked text is the nested quotation itself, which falls BETWEEN spans
(on 0beca6c's OPR-49 line the raw spans were 3, 2 and 21 words and `definitely not sent` lay in
none of them; the verified words drop 33 -> 21, not 26 -> 21). Rewrite the sentence so it says
the nested quotations themselves, falling between spans, are checked by nothing -- subject to
item 3, which detects the common case.

ITEM 3, SETTLED: BOTH a detector and a declared limit. Detector (reviewer B's rule, matching not
counting): in `find()`, when a checked attribution owns two or more RAW `QUOTE` spans, take the
text from the first span's opening quote to the last span's closing quote (outer to outer,
interior quote characters left in place; `norm()` folds curly to straight) and test it against
the same `pool`. A match proves the spans are one quotation that nests straight quotes, cut by
`QUOTE`: FAIL with "quotation after `ID` is cut by nested straight quotes; write the inner
quotes curly". No match: today's per-span check, untouched. Reviewer B ran it: 0 hits on the clean
tree; straightening OPR-49's inner quotes fires once in Delivery.lean, and DUR-30's once in
Cursor.lean, with the count line unchanged at 142/121 either way (the miss this detects). A
false positive needs the owner's body to contain the writer's straight-quoted text verbatim,
which is nesting. Do NOT build the rejected forms: a checked-words ratchet (offset by
lengthening another quote; re-baselined on every legitimate shortening), a gap heuristic that
merges spans within N words (at N=5 fuses CHN-35, OPR-51, DUR-11 and reds a clean tree), or a
no-punctuation-gap report (fires on six to nine legitimate coordinated quotations, e.g.
DUR-11's `"..." and that "..."`, CHN-35's three phrases). Declared limit, kept beside the
detector: a nested quote whose outer-to-outer text does NOT match the body is still checked by
nothing; the remedy remains curly inner quotes. Control: a `gates.yml` step that straightens
OPR-49's inner quotes in a scratch copy and asserts exit 1 with the new message. Update the
`Exit 0 = ...` line for the new cause. With this, e96ef32's subject "reads a nested quotation
whole" becomes true.

Optional, same commit: the positive control's `grep -Eq 'reports what OPS-1 says|attributes
to'` is broad; `Delivery.lean attributes to` anchors it, and a `grep -q 'attributes to MAN-2'`
branch names "the probe's quote drifted from MAN-2's body" when MAN-2 is next edited. The
comment above the nested-comment control lost the clause "and the quote after it is never
read"; half a line restores it ("the false quote after each nested comment is what the refusal
keeps unread"). The `grep -q` on the `FAIL: 2` count fails silently under `set -e`; the
colon-form control's if/cat/::error::/exit 1 form would name the dropped arm.

Done: gates green unpiped; three new or tightened controls each shown red against the detector
from HEAD~ and green on the commit; `citation-baseline.json` at zero; no Markdown requirement
body changed; no Lean declaration changed (docstring text only if a quote needs curly marks).
notes: Residue from the bps-8s0.22 review (reviewer B), on 21e8141, same gates.yml neighbourhood as this bead's optional item: the comment above the nested-comment control lost the old clause "and the quote after it is never read". The false OVR-1 quote each probe carries asserts nothing (with the detector removed the gate is exit 0, 142 verified, because the regex ends the docstring at the inner -/), so nothing local now says why the quotes are there. Half a line restores it, e.g. "the false quote after each nested comment is what the refusal keeps unread". Optional in the same commit: the new grep -q on the FAIL: 2 count fails silently under set -e; the colon-form control's if/cat/::error::/exit 1 form would name the dropped arm.
close_reason: Landed as 0d0b4ad (gate, controls) and 2744d4a (loud controls, reachable drift branch, README row); residue filed as the new bead

title: Citation gate residue: the older controls' silent greps, the broad Delivery.lean drift grep, and four cosmetic notes
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.23 reviews (four reviewers; Rounds 1 and 2), verified on
0d0b4ad and 2744d4a. All small; none changes what the gate refuses. Same-commit candidates.

1. The five older citation controls in gates.yml still assert their diagnostic with a bare
   `grep -q` under `set -e` (the Markdown false quote, the Lean-docstring false quote, the
   nested-comment `:[0-9]+:` grep, the colon-form DOM-1 grep, the historical-marker grep). A red
   for the wrong reason prints nothing. bps-8s0.23 gave the two new controls and the `FAIL: 2`
   count the loud `if ! grep -q …; then cat citations.log; echo "::error::…"; exit 1; fi` form;
   give the older ones the same.

2. In the MAN-2/OPS-1 positive control the second drift grep is
   `grep -Eq 'reports what OPS-1 says|Delivery.lean attributes to'`. Now that the reorder puts it
   ahead of the exit-code check, an unrelated Delivery.lean attribution failure gets the wrong
   `::error::` label (reviewer B verified by appending a false OVR-1 quote to Delivery.lean in a scratch
   copy of the body). Narrow the alternative to `Delivery.lean attributes to OPS-1`; the
   `attributes to MAN-2` branch above it keeps the drift case. Near-unreachable in CI (the clean
   tree's check-all runs first), so cosmetic.

3. check_citations.py: `find()` names its new list `nested` while `load()` already returns a
   different `nested` (block-comment refusals) and `main()` unpacks the new one as `cut`. Rename
   the local to `cut`. Cosmetic.

4. check_citations.py: the declared nested-quote limit in the docstring omits that the detector
   runs only on a CHECKED attribution (one with a >=4-word span), so a colon-form quotation cut
   into all-short spans is missed by both arms. The four-word colon-form limit is declared two
   sentences earlier, so a reader can compose them; half a clause would make it explicit.

5. check_citations.py: `quoted()` with an empty needle (norm() of an all-punctuation span is "")
   returns True for a non-empty pool; for the nested detector that inverts to a spurious FAIL.
   Needs two >=8-character all-punctuation spans under one checked attribution, so theoretical.
   A `frags and …` guard, if touched at all.

6. The dev shell has no PyYAML, so a brief's `import yaml` parse of gates.yml cannot run there;
   `ruby -ryaml` and `yq` do. Either add pyyaml to flake.nix or note the ruby form in AGENTS.md.

Done: gates green unpiped; each control touched under item 1 shown to print citations.log and
its `::error::` when its grep is pointed at an absent string; count line unchanged at 142/121;
no requirement body, Lean declaration or baseline changed.

Gates green unpiped, count line 142/121 unchanged; four reviewers, no findings.
