title: M8.2 watchtower cursor and scan proofs: WTC-11..14, shared backend-view vocabulary, CursorShape -> DEF-6
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 2 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "Reorg cursor and cache model (DEF-6, DEF-21)").
Planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after a three-adviser consultation; the
split, boundaries and guard are SETTLED, so no Consultation is needed.

WHAT TO BUILD. The watchtower cursor of WTC-13 and WTC-14 as a transition system, with the
scan proofs of WTC-12 and three of WTC-11's four detection sites. Owners, to quote in
docstrings: WTC-11 ("A node MUST detect a reorg at every point where it binds a result to a
chain"), WTC-12 (the three checks, "any failure discarding the whole result"), WTC-13 (anchors
"at most 101, contiguous", "reconciled", "walks newest to oldest for the highest still-active
anchor", "clears and re-scans from genesis rather than wedging or silently advancing"), WTC-14
(below-tip pass "MUST return without advancing", changed tip "MUST discard its candidate
cursor", errored pass "keeps the unadvanced cursor", panic "resets the cursor to genesis").

MODULES. Two modules for cursor and cache were decided (not one): the cursor's proofs need no
cache state, and the cache's need only active-at-height and snapshot facts. This ticket owns
the SHARED backend-view vocabulary, defined once: a block reference (height, hash), the
active-chain read `activeAt : Height -> Option Hash`, the captured tip, and previousblockhash
linkage. Put it where .11.3 can import it without importing the cursor's transitions (a small
`Chain.lean`, or a clearly separated section). Do NOT enlarge `Kernel.ChainView` ({mtp, seen},
an environment input) or `Coverage`'s `Pass.read` to share types; neither carries height ->
hash. Keep this cursor apart from `Cursor.lean`, which is SPN-38's RELEASE cursor (CONTEXT.md
has both terms).

GUARD PARAMETER. `CursorShape := anchored | bareHeight`, `current := anchored`. `bareHeight` is
DEF-6's twin: "The watchtower cursor was a bare monotonic height that never rewound, so a
recovery-path or unrecognised spend re-landing below it after a reorg was silently missed". The
twin trace: a spend confirmed at height h, a reorg that drops it and re-lands it below the
cursor, the anchored cursor rewinds and re-scans it, the bare cursor advances past it. Exhibits
over `current` go in `Exhibits.lean`; the CI negative control flips `current` and requires the
named theorem red. Do NOT claim this closes all of DEF-6: its prohibition also covers DUR-31's
re-broadcast and SPN-25's prevout verification, which stay out.

THEOREMS, universal over the shape where the statement allows: (1) anchors are at most 101 and
contiguous on every reachable cursor; (2) an in-window reorg is detected by the single hash read
at the newest anchor and the cursor rewinds to the highest still-active anchor, dropping
everything above; (3) a reorg deeper than the window resets to genesis; (4) WTC-14's four pass
outcomes, each as a theorem over the pass function; (5) WTC-12's three checks as NECESSITY
exhibits, not flips: for each check, a trace that passes the other two and would bind a result
to an abandoned fork -- the fork below the range that rebuilt taller, the mixed-fork straddle,
the scan that ran entirely on an abandoned fork and returned to the captured tip. Coinbase
inputs skipped; "a missing one is an error, never a silent negative" as a refusal, not a
default.

WTC-11's fourth site, "a wallet anchor no longer active", is .11.3's; say so in the docstring
and point at it rather than proving half of it here.

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped; the DEF-6 flip measured locally with its exact error count in
`gates.yml`; the five necessity exhibits and the twin trace present; no Markdown requirement
body changed; CONTEXT.md's two cursor entries still true.
close_reason: Landed as 02e6c55 and ef8b256; gates green unpiped (616 tagged declarations), DEF-6 flip red at 4 in Exhibits.lean only; four reviewers clean in Round 2

title: M8.3 vault-unspent cache and wallet anchor: WTC-5..10, WTC-11's fourth site, ImportBracket -> DEF-21
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 3 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "Reorg cursor and cache model (DEF-6, DEF-21)").
Planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after a three-adviser consultation; the
split, boundaries and guard are SETTLED, so no Consultation is needed. Blocked on .11.2, whose
shared backend-view vocabulary (block reference, `activeAt`, captured tip) this module imports.

WHAT TO BUILD. The vault-unspent cache and the wallet anchor: WTC-5..WTC-10, plus WTC-11's
fourth detection site, "a wallet anchor no longer active". Owners, to quote in docstrings:
WTC-5 (the cache "of the confirmed outputs paying the vault" and its refusal), WTC-6 (the
serving order), WTC-7 (private keys disabled, blank, descriptor-based), WTC-8 (the completion
marker), WTC-9 ("If the wallet's completion anchor is no longer on the active chain the node
MUST latch"), WTC-10 (the sweep's read "MUST take one consistent snapshot"). Read each in
10-watchtower-and-chain.md before writing; the quotes above are fragments.

MODEL. A separate module from the cursor (decided): its proofs need only active-at-height and
stable-snapshot facts, never cursor transitions. State the cache as a function of a proven scan
(a .11.2 scan result) plus the wallet anchor; the completion-anchor latch of WTC-9 as a sticky
state; WTC-10's snapshot as one captured (tip, read) pair that the sweep consumes whole.
Connect the accepted snapshot to `Coverage`'s `Pass.read` (Coverage owns the denominator; this
module supplies what a pass reads) without enlarging Coverage's types.

GUARD PARAMETER. `ImportBracket := reProve | unbracketed`, `current := reProve`. `unbracketed`
is DEF-21's twin: "A reorg landing between the cold scan and the wallet import could import a
birthday proven on an abandoned fork, leaving an output permanently unwatched and inflating
apparent coverage", against the prohibition "the import MUST be bracketed by re-proving the
scan's own anchor (`WTC-7`)". Twin trace: cold scan on fork A, reorg to B between scan and
import, the bracketed import re-proves the anchor and refuses, the unbracketed one imports a
birthday B never had and one output is unwatched forever. DEF-9 is NOT an honest twin here (its
only difference is timing, which Silence.lean already excludes); do not add it.

THEOREMS: (1) WTC-5's refusal: an understated denominator is unreachable, i.e. every confirmed
output paying the vault on the proven chain is in the cache; (2) WTC-9's latch is sticky and
set exactly when the completion anchor leaves the active chain; (3) WTC-10: the sweep's read is
a single snapshot, so no interleaving of a chain advance between capture and use changes the
value the sweep sees; (4) the DEF-21 twin theorem over `current`, with the flipped refutation.

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped; the DEF-21 flip measured locally with its exact error count in
`gates.yml`; no Markdown requirement body changed; the CONTEXT.md entries for Coverage and
Vault unspent (if present) still true.
close_reason: Landed as 503da85 and ca4f964; gates green at 685 tagged declarations; DEF-21 flip red at 3 in Exhibits.lean only; four reviewers clean in Round 2. Residue in bps-8s0.11.8.

title: M8.4 watchtower recognition and alert queue: WTC-17..22, Recognition guard (ADR-0001 -> ADR-0012), Silence WTC-20 debt
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 4 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8). Planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after
a three-adviser consultation; the split and the guard are SETTLED, so no
Consultation is needed. Blocked on .11.2: WTC-21 takes the alert lock "only after the scan has
been proven (`WTC-12`)", so the queue's transitions consume a proven scan.

WHAT TO BUILD. Watchtower recognition and the alert queue: WTC-17..WTC-22. The watchtower is a
DUTY of every node, not a deployment (ADR-0001, "Vault nodes are the watchtower"; CONTEXT.md's
entry). Owners, to quote in docstrings: WTC-17 (scan "every 10 seconds, first pass immediate";
the precedence: empty branch selector is a `RECOVERY_PATH_SPEND` "even if the txid is in the
authorized set", otherwise not in the vault-authorized set is an `UNRECOGNIZED_SPEND`,
"otherwise no alert"; "The recovery exit is never swallowed"), WTC-18 (recognition "by
validation and acceptance, never by co-signing and never by evaluation"; the two refutations;
the authorized set as "the txids of every spend, Escape, rung, refresh and claw-back this node
accepted (`SPN-33`)"), WTC-19 (witness not script; fewer than two elements "reads as
non-recovery"), WTC-20 (RAM-only, "capped at 1 024 events with the oldest evicted first,
sequence-numbered from 1"; dedup on `spend_txid:outpoint`; "an evicted entry's key is released
so a later scan may re-alert it"), WTC-21 (snapshot the authorized set and release the lock
BEFORE the slow chain read), WTC-22 ("Watchtower duty continues during Lockdown").

GUARD PARAMETER. `Recognition := validated | coSigned | evaluated`, `current := validated`.
This is a dated semantic change (ADR-0001 revised by ADR-0012), so AGENTS.md requires the
parameter. Two twins, both from WTC-18's own sentences: `coSigned` -- "Only `t` of `n` nodes
sign a legitimate spend, so 'I did not sign it' false-alarms on `n − t` honest nodes" -- the
exhibit is a legitimate spend that alerts on n − t nodes under coSigned and nowhere under
validated; `evaluated` -- "a spend a node REFUSED was evaluated, so 'I evaluated it' would let an
attacker fanning a theft to honest nodes suppress its own alert" -- the exhibit is a theft fanned
to every honest node, refused by all, alerting everywhere under validated and nowhere under
evaluated. The CI control flips `current` to each and requires the named theorems red.

QUEUE MODEL. A RAM-only bounded sequence with a dedup key set: theorems that the length never
exceeds 1 024, that the sequence number is strictly increasing from 1, that a re-scan of a
retained spend enqueues nothing, that eviction releases the key so the same spend can re-alert,
and that WTC-17's precedence is total (every spend classifies to exactly one of three outcomes).
Alert shape: `kind`, `spend_txid`, `outpoint` as `txid:vout`, `script` as lowercase hex.

SILENCE DEBT. `Silence.lean`'s docstring says the kernel emits no alert, "so there is nothing here
to project (`API-18`, `WTC-20` are milestone 8's)". Pay it: either extend `Obs` with the queue's
observable (count and shape) and re-prove the coupling, or state in both docstrings, with the
argument, why the queue adds no observable divergence between the two PINs. WTC-22's "duty
continues during Lockdown" is a theorem over the lockdown state, not prose.

LOCK ORDER. WTC-21 as an ordering theorem over the pass: authorized-set snapshot, release, chain
read, WTC-12 proof, then alert lock; STO-9's lock order is the owner of the general rule -- cite
it, do not restate it.

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped; both Recognition flips measured locally with exact error counts
in `gates.yml`; the Silence debt paid one way or the other with the docstrings agreeing; no
Markdown requirement body changed. Package ancestry and replacement (WTC-23..25) are .11.5's,
not this ticket's.
close_reason: Landed as a8a87da: Alerts.lean (recognition guard, WTC-17 classification, WTC-20 queue, WTC-21 duty and lock order, WTC-22 lockdown theorem), Exhibits.lean WatchtowerAlerts section, two Recognition controls in gates.yml, Silence debt paid by route (b). Four reviewers PASS, no findings; residue filed as bps-8s0.11.9.

title: M8.6 language-neutral trace format: alphabet record, round trip, decided synthetic trace, negative exhibits; adapter lives in btc-policy-lean
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 6 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "implementation trace adapters — the boundary
at which btc-policy-lean's runtime evidence meets the model"). Planned 2026-09-24 by the
maintainer after a three-adviser consultation; SETTLED, no Consultation
needed. Blocked on .11.2..11.5 because the format names every event they define. NOT blocked
on bps-8s0.7: the FORMAT is a specification this repository owns; the replay ADAPTER is
implementation and lives in btc-policy-lean, whose first commit depends on this repository's
formal layer, so the block runs the other way.

WHAT THIS IS. The language-neutral trace format that btc-policy-lean and any other
implementation replay against the model. AGENTS.md: "Nothing that implements the specified
system belongs here" and ADR-0023: "No implementation, verifier or shadow node ever lives
here". So: no runner, no CLI, no collector, no adapter, no schema file. The repository already
owns encoders (WIR-18..27, `Encode.lean`); this is one more codec plus fixtures.

THE SMALLEST CHECKABLE SPECIFICATION (unanimous): (1) the event alphabet as a versioned Lean
record -- the union of the events the milestone 8 modules and the kernel step on, each with its
explicit mapping to a model input or effect; (2) `decode ∘ encode = id` and a length theorem in
the `Encode.lean` pattern; (3) at least one published synthetic trace whose replay verdict
(final state and effects) is `decide`-proved, in the `check_vectors.py` pattern so the digest of
the published preimage is recomputed by the vector gate; (4) rejected malformed traces as
negative exhibits (wrong version, unknown event, truncated entry). No guard parameter: ADR-0023
says a codec round trip "needs no twin".

SECRETS. STO-11: the listed secrets "MUST never appear in a ... trace ... or replay entry"; hold
it BY CONSTRUCTION -- the record has no field that can carry a PIN, preimage, key, KDF output
or request body. STO-12: no synthetic identifier may be a derivative that lets memory capture
"cheaply test the plaintext PIN". The project rule "synthetic traces only" is stronger than
STO-11 requires; state it as the project's rule, not as STO-11's.

CONFORMANCE. Rows for the adapter's obligations go to 15-conformance-checklist.md (the
implementation records its own status per OVR-17); AGENTS.md: "Never put a `CNF` identifier in
`tools/formal/`".

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped, including the vector gate recomputing the trace digest; the
round trip and the decided verdict present; the negative exhibits present; no Markdown
requirement body changed; the conformance rows added.
close_reason: Landed in b5748aa and bd3a517: Trace.lean (alphabet, codec, round trip, replay, decided published trace, negative exhibits), traceVector region in ADR-0023, CNF-147/CNF-148, two gate controls; nine gates green on bd3a517

title: M8.2 review residue: WTC-14 clause precedence and tip-hash reading for the spec owner; spend and anchorless-cursor notes for .11.3/.11.4
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.11.2 reviews (Rounds 1 and 2: four reviewers), verified on
ef8b256. None is a defect in what landed; each is a note for the ticket named, or a spec-owner
question, so it is filed rather than lost.

1. WTC-14 clause precedence has its home only in a Lean docstring. 10-watchtower-and-chain.md
   states the below-tip clause and the panic clause side by side; Watchtower.lean's `pass`
   resolves a panic below the newest anchor as a reset to genesis (a panic can happen anywhere
   in a pass, the tip comparison included), and its docstring says so. A reimplementer working
   from the Markdown alone could order the two either way. Spec owner's call: a clause in
   WTC-14 ("a panic anywhere in the pass, the tip comparison included"), or nothing.

2. WTC-14's "captured tip hash changes" is read literally: `pass` discards a scan whose
   after-view tip hash differs from the captured one, so an ordinary extension during the scan
   discards the pass (retried next pass; WTC-14 says the redundant re-scan is harmless). A
   reviewer read it as "the block at the captured height changed" and asked for an
   extension-accepting exhibit; rejected as the weaker rule the text does not state. Worth the
   spec owner confirming the reference implementation compares the tip hash, not the height.

3. For bps-8s0.11.4 (recognition and the alert queue), where spends stop being opaque:
   - an empty proven scan still binds its spends: `result .anchored genesis { blocks := [],
     spends := [7], … } = some (genesis, [7])`;
   - nothing asserts the DEF-6 trace binds its spend; `result current genesis def6Scan` yields
     `some [1]` by #eval, and one conjunct on `def6_rescanned_with_current` would carry it (the
     DEF-6 flip count in gates.yml stays 4 if added there);
   - `headerAccepted` and `Anchor.active` share one body; kept as WTC-11's two named sites.

4. For bps-8s0.11.3 (cache and wallet anchor): under `anchored`, an anchorless cursor with a
   non-zero next height reconciles to genesis (`next := 0`). Unreachable from genesis, so no
   theorem depends on it; pin `anchors = [] → next = 0` in `wellFormed` if the cache's proofs
   ever need it.

Done: whichever of 1 and 2 the spec owner takes is a Markdown edit with its own citation and
gate run; 3 and 4 are folded into their tickets or closed as not needed.
close_reason: Spec owner decided 2026-09-27: item 1, WTC-14 states a panic anywhere in the pass, the tip comparison included, resets to genesis; item 2, the tip check compares the active hash at the captured tip height (the reference's reading, panel unanimous). Items 3-4 were folded into bps-8s0.11.11 (closed). The Markdown and the model land together in bps-8s0.11.13.

title: M8.3 review residue: modelling choices for the spec owner (one marker, no birthday without outputs, walk-to-tip reading); docstring and delta-exhibit notes for VaultUnspent.lean
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.11.3 reviews (Rounds 1 and 2: four reviewers), verified on
ca4f964. None is a defect in what landed; each is a note for a later edit of VaultUnspent.lean,
or a modelling choice worth the spec owner's eye, so it is filed rather than lost.

1. Modelling choices the Implementer flagged, accepted by every reviewer, worth the spec owner
   confirming against the reference implementation:
   - the Wallet record holds one completion marker, the one the last import left; WTC-8's "at
     least one marker whose anchor is still active" is that marker's anchor;
   - a vault with no confirmed output has no birthday, so `rebuild` imports nothing (WTC-7 names
     no birthday for that case);
   - block time is modelled by height; WTC-7's birthday is used only as an order;
   - WTC-7's "blank" and "descriptor-based" are creation-time duties the record does not carry
     (route (a) of the Round 2 brief; the alternative was reading them in `usable`).

2. WTC-6's delta walk is read as a walk from the cached anchor to the tip: `deltaFrom` accepts
   the walk's result only when anchored at the served view's tip, else falls through to the cold
   scan (Round 2 item 1). The Markdown says "a bounded delta walk of at most 32 blocks from a
   cached anchor whose block is still active" and does not say "to the tip" in words; the spec
   owner may want those words in WTC-6, as with WTC-14's clause precedence (bps-8s0.11.7 item 1).

3. Docstring and exhibit notes for the next edit of VaultUnspent.lean (reviewer B, Round 2):
   - `deltaFrom`'s docstring says the walk "reads the scan and the ledger only"; it also reads
     the cache it walks from. "takes no view" is the fact being argued.
   - `deltaFrom`'s bound `v.tip.height ≤ c.anchor.height + deltaWindow` is now entailed by the
     tip equality plus `rangeFrom` and `length ≤ deltaWindow`; a half-sentence saying so would
     stop a reader deleting the wrong one as duplication.
   - No exhibit in Exhibits.lean's VaultUnspentCache section walks a delta: the Round 1 regression
     (`chainOf [100, 101, 102]`, base at (0, 100), empty scan → cold scan now) and a walk stopping
     one short live only in the reviewers' probes. `served_at_tip` guards the rule universally;
     a concrete exhibit would make it legible.

4. bps-8s0.11.7 item 4 (pin `anchors = [] → next = 0` in Watchtower.wellFormed if the cache's
   proofs need it): not needed; no proof in VaultUnspent.lean reads the cursor.

Done: 1 and 2 answered by the spec owner (a Markdown edit with its own citation and gate run, or
nothing); 3 folded into the next edit of VaultUnspent.lean or closed as not needed; 4 is closed
by this note.

Item 3 folded into bps-8s0.11.11 (closed). Lands in bps-8s0.11.13.

title: M8.4 review residue: which theorems each Recognition flip refutes, the coSigned twin's premises, the DEF-6 grep slack, a Silence docstring phrase; the unconditional list dedup is false
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.11.4 reviews (Round 1: four reviewers; all PASS, no
findings), verified on a8a87da. None is a defect in what landed; each is a cosmetic note for the
next edit of Alerts.lean, Exhibits.lean or gates.yml, or a note for the bead register, so it is
filed rather than lost.

1. The two Recognition controls count proof failures with refutations. Under `.coSigned`,
   `refused_not_recognised_with_current` and `refused_everywhere_alerts_with_current` stay true
   propositions (Record.wf gives coSigned ⊆ accepted and refused ∩ accepted = ∅) and go red only
   because their proofs rewrite through `.validated`; symmetrically under `.evaluated` for
   `accepted_recognised_with_current` and `accepted_everywhere_silent_with_current`. The controls
   are sound (each of the four is refuted by one of the two flips) and the counts 6 and 5 are
   measured, but the closing `echo`s say "correctly failed on" all four in both steps. Options:
   name in each `echo` which theorems the flip refutes and which merely lose their proof, or
   prove the still-true ones under every value so only refutations are counted (reviewer C proved
   both statements under the flipped values; the counts would then change).

2. `legit_false_alarms_with_coSigned` (Alerts.lean) asserts `federation.length = 5`, the Normal
   branch and the count 2, but not that all five accepted txid 10 and exactly three co-signed
   it, which is what makes 2 read as `n − t`. Its two siblings pin their premises as conjuncts;
   this one could too.

3. The `DEF-6` control's `grep -A3 'proved that the proposition' … reconcile current (chainOf
   def6ChainB) (def6Cursor current)` now matches the third printed line of
   `def6_rescanned_with_current`, at the boundary after bps-8s0.11.7 item 3's conjunct was
   prepended. One more prepended conjunct breaks the step; `-A4`, or a fragment from the first
   line, would give slack.

4. `Silence.lean`'s module docstring says "the authorized set, which is `SPN-33`'s accepted
   txids" where `Alerts.lean`'s says "which under `current` is"; the three words keep the guard
   dependence visible on both sides.

5. For the bead register: bps-8s0.11.4's theorem 6 ("enqueueing the same alerts twice is the
   same as once, universal over the queue and the alert list") is false as an unconditional list
   statement — a pass of more than 1 024 fresh keys evicts its own oldest, and a queue whose
   oldest already carries one of the pass's keys evicts it mid-pass; in both the key is released
   by WTC-20's own rule and the re-scan re-alerts it. `enqueue_twice` is unconditional;
   `enqueueAll_twice` carries the hypothesis that the first pass leaves every key retained, and

title: M8 spec-owner decisions: settled depth 10 for the wallet import, WTC-14 tip at the captured height, chunked delta commit; Markdown + Lean + ADR in one commit
description:
Land the settled-depth amendment and the three reorg readings the spec owner decided on
2026-09-27..29, in the Markdown AND the Lean model in one commit (AGENTS.md: "Change the
declaration and the Markdown together"), plus one ADR. Every choice below is SETTLED by the
maintainer after four consultation rounds (advisers B, C, D; A timed out on three); no
Consultation is needed. This answers bps-8s0.11.7 items 1-2 and bps-8s0.11.8 items 1-2.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/settled-depth-markdown.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends
WTC-6, WTC-7, WTC-8, WTC-9, WTC-11, WTC-14 (10-watchtower-and-chain.md), OPS-71, DEF-21, CNF-89,
CNF-91 and adds six CONTEXT.md entries (Cache anchor, Scan anchor, Settled depth, Settled block,
Birthday, Completion marker). Do not reword it. If a Lean-side fact shows a sentence false,
stop and say so in the report instead of editing the sentence. After applying, the citation gate
reports 13 Lean docstring quotations that no longer match (Chain.lean 1, VaultUnspent.lean 9,
Watchtower.lean 3); every one moves in this commit.

The decisions the patch encodes, in plain terms:
- WTC-14: the tip check compares the ACTIVE HASH AT THE CAPTURED TIP HEIGHT after the scan (the
  reference's reading); a block arriving on top is the next pass's range; a panic anywhere in a
  pass, the tip comparison included, resets to genesis. Rationale: the chain-tip reading can
  never finish a genesis re-scan (WTC-13) on mainnet.
- WTC-6: the wallet read is discarded unless the tip captured before the listing is still the
  tip after the reconciliation (the reference's bracket); the delta walk commits a walk that
  completes even below the tip and continues next refresh (the reference's behaviour); a walk
  failing any proof is discarded whole; WTC-5 refuses a cache below the tip at fire time.
- WTC-7: SETTLED DEPTH 10. Scan anchor A; settled block S = 10 below A, or genesis when A's
  height is below 10. The cold scan plus a WTC-12-proven walk of the blocks above S ending at A
  itself form one result; a failed walk refuses the import. Birthday = LOWEST HEIGHT among S and
  the CREATING blocks of every output the scan found live or the walk found spent. The import is
  bracketed by re-proving S before the descriptors AND before the marker. A repair never starts
  later than the wallet already covers: if its birthday is not below the lowest birthday a held
  marker carries, it imports only a new marker; otherwise it re-imports from its own birthday.
- WTC-8: a marker carries S's height and hash AND the import's birthday; the wallet is usable
  while ANY held marker's anchor is active.
- WTC-9 / WTC-11: repair latches only when NO held marker's anchor is active; a shallow reorg is
  caught by the read's tip bracket.

## 2. The Lean model

- `Watchtower.pass`: replace the chain-tip comparison with the active hash at the captured
  height (Chain.lean's `Anchor.active` on the after-view); restate `pass_tip_changed` and
  `pass_completed`; add an exhibit where a block arrives on top and the pass is KEPT.
- `VaultUnspent`: `settledDepth : Nat := 10` tagged `WTC-7` beside `deltaWindow`; REGISTER BOTH in
  `Render.values` / `check_copies.py`'s owner registry so WTC-7's "10 blocks" and WTC-6's
  "32 blocks" are held (32 is tagged but unregistered today). Model spentness: the cold scan
  yields outputs live at A; the walk of (S, A] yields spends with their creating heights;
  `birthday` = min height over S and those creators (today `birthdayFrom` confirms any vault
  output and `coldScan` includes all confirmed outputs; neither survives). The import bracket
  re-proves S at both points. `Wallet` holds a list of markers `(settled anchor, birthday)`;
  `usable` = some marker active; repair is marker-only or re-import per WTC-7; the birthday never
  rises. `deltaFrom` drops the pre-walk `tip ≤ anchor + deltaWindow` gate and the
  `c'.anchor = v.tip` acceptance, walks through min(tip, anchor + 32) and commits; `served_at_tip`
  becomes a statement about what WTC-5 refuses; the exhibits
  `delta_walk_short_of_tip_refused` and `delta_walk_empty_below_tip_refused` invert.
- Guard parameters (AGENTS.md: "Every semantic choice a dated amendment changed is a guard
  parameter with a `current` value"): at least (a) WTC-7's marker anchor, `settled | scanTip`,
  whose withdrawn value's twin is the hole the amendment closes — an output created below S,
  spent inside the settled depth, resurrected by a shallow reorg that leaves the old anchor
  standing; (b) WTC-14's tip test, `capturedHeight | chainTip`; (c) WTC-6's delta commit,
  `partial | tipOnly`. Each with theorems over `current` in Exhibits.lean and a measured CI
  negative control in gates.yml. The Manager may argue a value is not a dated semantic change and
  drop its parameter, in the brief, with the reason.
- `Trace.lean` wallet/ledger adapters and `Exhibits.lean`'s `def21Birthday` trace follow the new
  shapes. The 13 quotations re-quote the new text.

## 3. The ADR

`docs/adr/0024-the-wallet-import-settles-ten-blocks-below-the-scan.md` (or the next free number):
the decision; the rejected alternatives — anchor at the scan tip (the reference; repairs on every
shallow reorg), trust only the newest marker (the model; refuted as a necessity by the regtest
run, and not recoverable from the wallet since import order is not stored), a full scan whenever
more than 32 behind (the model; contradicts WTC-9's one-scan-per-repair-attempt), an
import-nothing empty vault (the model; contradicts DEF-9's steady state); the regtest evidence
(.context/settled-depth-regtest-result.txt, script .context/settled-depth-regtest.sh — summarise
in the ADR, do not commit .context); and Consequences: the reference implementation
(btc-policy-rust, crate `vault-node`, module `chain`) diverges on the settled depth and walk, the
marker's birthday field and the marker-only repair, and must move in its own repository; nothing
that implements goes here. Keep the settled depth distinct from WTC-13's 100-block cursor window.

## 4. Done when

Gate green unpiped (all nine); every new CI control measured locally at an exact count; the
citation gate verifies the re-quoted text; `settledDepth` and `deltaWindow` held by the copy gate;
bps-8s0.11.7 and bps-8s0.11.8 are already closed pointing here. Out of scope: SEC-50's "every
refresh pays" wording versus WTC-6's delta fallback (pre-existing; file a finding if confirmed).
notes:
Round 2 corrected five defects no gate catches, on top of the landed amendment (8d69be3).

D1 (the marker-anchor twin): the formal fact says NO reachable import history leaves an output
unwatched under the isolated .scanTip flip, so the twin is re-based on the repair. The fact is
VaultUnspent.scanTip_active_marker_watches_everything: under .scanTip a marker's birthday is at
most its anchor's height (scanTip_birthday_le_anchor), so an output created below the wallet's
floor that a reorg makes live again was live at the import of any marker the reorg leaves standing,
whose birthday was floored at or below that output's creating height (WTC-7's "A repair never
starts later than the wallet already covers", which applyImport gives every wallet). The reorg
therefore either unseats every marker and WTC-9 latches a repair, or leaves a marker whose own
import covers the output. markerAnchor_hole_with_scanTip became
markerAnchor_repairs_with_scanTip; the settled half in Exhibits gained the usable/no-latch
conjuncts; ADR-0024's scan-tip alternative now rests on the repair cost.

D2: deltaFrom bounds the walk above at the served view's tip, so the walk runs through
min(tip, anchor + deltaWindow); deltaFrom_some, served_delta_only_when and
delta_commits_completed_walk carry the bound. The two partial-commit exhibits keep their
conclusions.

D3, D4: ADR-0024 reports what the regtest run recorded for the no-marker wallet's birthtime, and
the tip-test attribution is the right way round (the reference read the captured height, which
decision 7 adopts; the formal model read the chain tip and is what moved).

D5: the next-refresh sentence on delta_walk_short_of_tip_committed is scoped to the latch.

All nine gates green. The three VaultUnspent CI negative controls were re-measured locally in
scratch copies, one at a time: counts 3 (import bracket), 5 (marker anchor), 3 (delta commit) all
unchanged, every named proposition still greps, no error outside Exhibits.lean.
close_reason: Every sentence that characterises a Lean declaration checked against its signature. D1: the marker-anchor section named hm, which is membership and holds on scanTipWallet; hagree is what fails, since chain C shows 212 at height 12 where the import's scan view A shows 112. D2: the MarkerAnchor docstring claimed 'exactly that hypothesis' of a theorem with five; it now points at the theorem's own hypotheses. D3: the unexhibited-claim justification now covers both halves. D4: ADR-0024's second copy of decision 4 replaced by a pointer, and its one-hypothesis attribution widened. The 'no deeper than the settled depth' wording now says the depth is measured from that import's own scan anchor. All nine gates green.

title: SEC-50 overstates the cold-scan cost: WTC-6 falls to the delta walk, not to the full scan
description:
`SEC-50` says of the cold full UTXO-set scan: "on a node whose backend cannot serve the descriptor
wallet, every refresh pays it, and Bitcoin Core serialises it process-wide." `WTC-6` orders three
sources, and the middle one is not the wallet: "a bounded delta walk of at most 32 blocks from a
cached anchor whose block is still active". Read by `WTC-6` alone, a node that cannot serve the
wallet falls to the delta walk, not to the cold scan, so it pays the cold scan once to seed a base
and then only when the base has moved or the walk is discarded.

`WTC-6` now says when a walk is discarded and what it costs: "A walk that covers less is discarded
whole, as is one that fails any proof (`WTC-12`), and the refresh falls through to the cold scan."
And it says a walk that cannot reach the tip does not fall through: "A walk that completes becomes
the cache even where it ends below the tip, and any later delta walk starts from that cache". So
under `WTC-6` the cold scan is the price of a discarded walk or a moved base, not of every refresh.

`WTC-9` states the latched case, and as amended on 2026-10-02 it no longer makes `SEC-50`'s "every
refresh" true there: "From the latch setting until a cold scan has replaced the cache, every refresh
with no attempt in progress starts a repair attempt from a cold scan, whatever cache it holds, the
scan replacing the cache before the re-import begins (`WTC-6`); thereafter, while the latch holds,
the cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback (`WTC-6`), and a wallet read never
replaces it." And of an attempt that fails: "one that ends without rebuilding the wallet leaves any
latch set; the next attempt starts only from a cold scan `WTC-6` itself reaches with none in
progress, and starts no scan of its own." So a latched node whose repair keeps failing pays the
cold scans its cache needs and none for the repair. A backend that cannot serve the wallet at all
is not latched: "A wallet holding no completion marker is not latched, `WTC-8` already keeping it
out of use: its first build, and any retry after a failed one, starts the same way, from a cold
scan `WTC-6` reaches with no attempt in progress." That was the open question bps-8s0.11.22
recorded, settled by the owner on 2026-10-02 and landed with bps-8s0.11.25. `WTC-9` states the
consequence itself: "A failed build or repair is therefore not retried while delta walks succeed;
the cache does not depend on the wallet." With that answer `SEC-50`'s "every refresh pays it" is
what neither `WTC-6` nor `WTC-9` says of either case.

(Rewritten 2026-10-01: the earlier text of this bead quoted two sentences the catch-up amendment
removed from `WTC-9` and `WTC-6`, the cost clause for a repair that keeps failing and the clause
on continuing a walk at the next refresh. The quotations above are the text as it stands. Updated
2026-10-02 with bps-8s0.11.25: the paragraph on `WTC-9` quotes it as amended that day.)

Scope: reword `SEC-50`'s cost sentence so it names the source `WTC-6` actually falls to in each
case, and cite `WTC-6`'s and `WTC-9`'s own words for the cost rather than restating a stronger one.
`SEC-50` is a security-residual note, not a normative MUST, so nothing else moves; no Lean
declaration owns it and no gate holds the sentence today. Owner: the specification repository.

Done when: `SEC-50`'s sentence carries the delta walk and the latched case, the citation gate
verifies whatever it quotes, and `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green.
close_reason:
Implemented in 3821cc4f5d4aabf53ea9dfdc84b8bffa46683943. Only SEC-50 and this bead's claim changed. Acceptance checks cover the ordinary delta fallback, completed walks below the tip, the latch's initial cold scan and subsequent delta advancement, the unlatched unbuilt wallet, and failed-attempt retry costs. The availability residual, process-wide scan serialization and need to measure mainnet cost are retained. No normative requirement, formal declaration, gate, baseline or later bead changed.

Verification: nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh ran unpiped before editing and after the final edit, both exit 0 with every summary entry PASS; final log /tmp/bps-8s0.11.14-gates.log. nix develop --command python3 tools/check_citations.py exited 0. Each quoted span in SEC-50 was checked for exact owner text and separately corrupted in memory through the citation gate entry point; every corruption returned 1 and named 12-security-requirements.md and its WTC-6 or WTC-9 owner, with no source or baseline mutation; evidence /tmp/bps-8s0.11.14-citation-probe.log. nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py 'citation gate' exited 0, every selected workflow step passed, and its final summary was DONE 0 failed of 12; evidence /tmp/bps-8s0.11.14-controls.log. git diff --check passed and the complete diff was inspected for scope and acceptance. No further gap found in this bead.

title: CONTEXT.md's Settled depth gloss states a latch condition WTC-9 does not state
description:
`CONTEXT.md`'s **Settled depth** entry, added verbatim by the 2026-09-29 settled-depth patch
(`ADR-0024`, `bps-8s0.11.13`), says:

"How far below the scan anchor a wallet import treats the chain as settled: a reorg no deeper
leaves every completion marker in force, and a deeper one latches a repair (`WTC-7`, `WTC-9`)."

`WTC-9` latches on a different condition: "If no completion marker the wallet holds has an anchor
on the active chain the node MUST latch a repair". The Lean model reads `WTC-9`, not the gloss:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.observe` sets the latch exactly when `someMarkerActive` is false.

So the entry's second clause is false as a universal about the wallet. A reorg deeper than the
settled depth unseats the marker of *that* import; whether the wallet latches depends on whether
any other held marker's anchor is still active. A reorg of 11 blocks can unseat a marker anchored
at height 12 while an older marker anchored at height 2 stays active, and no repair latches.

`ADR-0024`'s decision 1 carries the same shorthand ("A reorg no deeper than 10 leaves every
completion marker in force and costs no repair; a deeper one latches one").

The sentence is the specification owner's: it arrived in a patch the implementing brief required be
applied verbatim and explicitly forbade rewording, so it was not touched when the amendment landed.
Rewording it is a spec-owner call, which is why this is a bead and not an edit.

Note that the *behaviour* is not in doubt — `WTC-9` owns the latch rule and is unambiguous, and
`CONTEXT.md` is the vocabulary file, not a normative source (`AGENTS.md`: "Vocabulary, overloaded
and banned words → `CONTEXT.md`"). This is a precision defect in a gloss, not a contradiction that
leaves behaviour undetermined.

Scope: reword the entry's second clause so it describes what the settled depth does per import (a
reorg deeper than it unseats that import's marker) and cites `WTC-9`'s own words for the latch, and
make the same correction in `ADR-0024`'s decision 1. Nothing normative moves.

Done when: the entry and `ADR-0024` decision 1 no longer state a latch condition `WTC-9` does not
state, the citation gate verifies whatever either quotes, and
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green (all nine, unpiped).

## Third site, found in the 2026-09-29 review (editable here)

`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Exhibits.lean`, the marker-anchor section docstring:

"The reorg to `C` is no deeper than the settled depth, so it leaves `S = (2, 102)` active and
every completion marker in force."

The second clause is the same overbroad gloss. A reorg no deeper than the settled depth below one
import's scan anchor leaves *that* import's settled block active; a marker whose settled block sits
above the reorg's fork point is unseated. Chain `C` forks at height 5, so a marker anchored at a
settled block of height 5 or above — an import with scan anchor 15 or above — is not left in force.
True of the markers this trace holds, not of every marker.

Unlike the `CONTEXT.md` entry and `ADR-0024`'s decision 1, this line did **not** come from the
specification owner's verbatim patch: it was added by commit 8d69be3 during the 2026-09-29 rounds.
So it is editable without a spec-owner call, and can be fixed in the same change as the other two or
ahead of them.

title: WTC-7's covering claim is exhibited, not proved: state the universal over views that leave S active
description:
`WTC-7` claims of the amended birthday: "so the import covers every output a reorg that leaves S
active can make live". The formal model establishes two weaker things:

- `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.settledBirthday_le` proves only the floor, `settledBirthday ≤ S.height`;
- `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.VaultUnspentCache.settled_covers_resurrection_with_current` is a single
  trace on one ledger and one reorg.

The covering claim itself is a universal and is not proved. The natural statement: for any view
`v'` agreeing with the scan view at every height at or below `S.height`, with `S` active on `v'`,
`unwatched L v' (settledBirthday L scanView S s) = []`.

Worth having for two reasons. It is the sentence `WTC-7` actually asserts, and an exhibit is not a
proof of a universal. And it would give `CNF-91`'s first clause — "The wallet birthday covers every
output a reorg that leaves the settled block active can make live" — a proof rather than an
instance.

Raised by the reviewer panel on `bps-8s0.11.13` as a suggestion beyond that bead's scope, which
required only that the amendment land green.

Scope: state and prove the universal in `VaultUnspent.lean`, with the instantiation over `current`
in `Exhibits.lean` per `ADR-0023` decision 6. No Markdown changes; `WTC-7` already says it.

Done when: the universal is proved (no `sorry`, no new axiom — `tools/check_formal.sh`'s axiom
policy holds), it is tagged `@[req "WTC-7"]`, and
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green (all nine, unpiped).

title: Watchtower.lean docstrings misstate what they cite: carry the signature check across tools/formal
description:
Five rounds of prose correction on `bps-8s0.11.13` each rewrote sentences that cite a Lean
declaration, and each rewrite introduced a fresh misstatement about the declaration it cited. The
final round's method — read every such sentence against its declaration's signature, hypothesis by
hypothesis — was applied to `VaultUnspent.lean` and `ADR-0024` and fixed them, but `Watchtower.lean`
was not covered. Three sentences there still misstate what they cite. All were verified against the
signatures, and none is caught by a gate: the citation gate checks quotations of requirements, not
claims about declarations.

## 1. `pass_tip_changed`'s docstring is wrong under one of the two guard values

`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Watchtower.lean`, above `pass_tip_changed`:

"A scan whose captured tip's hash is no longer the active hash at that height, under either test."

The hypothesis is `tipChanged tt tip s.after = true`, and `tipChanged` branches on the guard:

    | .capturedHeight => !tip.active after
    | .chainTip       => after.tip.hash != tip.hash

Under `.capturedHeight` the docstring is right. Under `.chainTip` it is wrong: a block arriving on
top makes `after.tip.hash != tip.hash` true while the captured block is still active at its height,
which is precisely what `def14_discarded_with_chainTip` exhibits. Describe the selected test
returning true, not one value's reading of it.

Introduced by commit 8d69be3 (2026-09-29), which added the `TipTest` guard; the pre-amendment text
read only "A scan whose captured tip hash changed."

## 2. `tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff`'s docstring promotes a fact about the test into one about the pass

Same file, above `tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff`:

"Under `capturedHeight` the test is exactly `WTC-11`'s first site on the captured tip: the pass
discards its candidate iff the hash the chain now has at the captured height is not the captured
one."

The theorem has no hypotheses and concludes
`tipChanged .capturedHeight tip after = true ↔ after.activeAt tip.height ≠ some tip.hash`. It says
nothing about `pass`, and the iff is false of `pass`, which also discards when `belowNewest c tip`
holds or when `candidate` yields none. Scope the iff to the tip test.

Introduced by commit 8d69be3, with the theorem.

## 3. `pass_completed`'s docstring omits the hypothesis that decides its conclusion

Same file, above `pass_completed`. The signature carries five hypotheses — `hb`, `ht`, `hp`, `hr`,
`hl` — and the docstring carries four: `ht` as "whose tip test found no change", `hp` and `hr` as "a
proven scan of the cursor's range", `hl` folded into "the last scanned block". `hb : belowNewest c
tip = false` is missing, and it is what decides the conclusion, since `pass` is
`if belowNewest c tip || tipChanged tt tip s.after then c else …`: with `belowNewest` true the pass
returns the cursor unchanged and `next = last.height + 1` fails.

**Pre-existing**, unlike 1 and 2: the text at 54adc47 omitted `hb` too. Bounded by
`pass_below_tip_never_advances` sitting in the same section with its hypothesis named.

## 4. Two wording points from the same review

- `VaultUnspent.lean`'s marker-anchor section, and `ADR-0024`, say "no declaration runs `repair`
  under `scanTip`". `cleared_only_by_rebuild` takes `ma : MarkerAnchor` and so does state something
  about `repair .scanTip …` for every `ma`. The accurate claim is that no declaration *evaluates* it
  on that trace — "no exhibit runs `repair` at `.scanTip`" survives a reader who greps.
- `ADR-0024`'s "neither exhibited nor proved" sentence gives two reasons for one claim, where
  `VaultUnspent.lean` now pairs each claim with its own reason. The ADR could take the same shape.

## Scope

Prose only. Fix 1, 2 and 4; fix 3 or record it as pre-existing, whichever the owner prefers. Then
carry the signature check across the whole of `tools/formal/`, not one module: for every sentence
that says what a declaration proves, requires or asserts, read the full signature — every hypothesis
and every conjunct — and check the sentence clause by clause. Change no declaration.

Done when: the three sentences match their signatures; no two places in the repository disagree
about what a declaration requires; the report names, for every sentence checked, the declaration and
the hypotheses read; and `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green (all nine,
unpiped). No negative control should move — none of these sentences is a control comment.
close_reason: Covered by bps-8s0.11.18's sweep: pass_tip_changed, tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff and pass_completed now state their signatures (hb named), the section-4 wording points are fixed in VaultUnspent.lean and ADR-0024, and the signature check was carried across every module under tools/formal with each misstatement found corrected. No declaration's statement changed for this bead.

title: M8 catch-up: full-range delta walk, one cache slot, repair attempts start from a cold scan; trace format v2; review sweep (closes bps-8s0.11.17)
description:
Land the catch-up amendment decided 2026-09-30..10-01 in the Markdown AND the Lean model in one
commit, and sweep the 2026-09-30 code review's findings. The wording is SETTLED by the spec owner
after two consultation rounds (all four advisers answering both rounds; no safety
break found in either). No Consultation is needed. This also closes bps-8s0.11.17 (the
Watchtower docstrings), which the sweep in section 3 covers.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/catchup-markdown.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends WTC-6 and
WTC-9 (10-watchtower-and-chain.md) and ADR-0024 (decision 8, the "full scan whenever more than 32
blocks behind" alternative, and Consequences). Do not reword it. If a Lean-side fact shows a
sentence false, stop and say so in the report instead of editing it. After applying, the citation
gate reports 9 Lean quotations that no longer match (VaultUnspent.lean 7, Exhibits.lean 2); every
one moves in this commit.

What the patch decides, in plain terms:
- WTC-6: a delta walk must cover EVERY height above the cache's anchor through the lesser of the
  tip captured when the walk starts and 32 blocks above the anchor. A walk that covers less is
  discarded whole, as is one failing any WTC-12 proof, and the refresh falls through to the cold
  scan. A walk that completes becomes THE cache (one slot) even below the tip; any later delta walk
  starts from it; WTC-5 refuses a cache whose anchor is not the current tip.
- WTC-9: a refresh that finds the latch set and NO repair attempt in progress starts one from a cold
  scan that replaces the cache before the re-import begins; while an attempt is in progress the
  cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback; while latched a wallet read never
  replaces the cache. This is the Rust reference's behaviour (`chain::refresh_vault_unspent_cache_mode`
  refuses the slot as a delta base when a repair is pending with no attempt running).
- The old WTC-9 cost clause ("one cold scan per repair attempt and not one per pass") is deleted:
  a discarded walk during a repair still costs a cold scan.

## 2. The Lean model (`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/`)

- ONE cache slot. Collapse `State.last` and `State.scanDerived` into a single cache; WTC-5's
  fire-time read, every source and every delta walk use it. Model "a repair attempt in progress" as
  you judge best (a flag, or each `repair` call being one attempt), but the following must be
  theorems, not prose: (a) a refresh with the latch set and no attempt in progress serves a cold
  scan, whatever the cache holds; (b) while latched, no wallet read replaces the cache; (c) a failed
  attempt does not leave delta walks running forever with the latch set: the next refresh with no
  attempt in progress starts a new one from a cold scan (the liveness gap round two found).
- FULL-RANGE WALK. `deltaFrom` (or `deltaWalk`) requires the walk's blocks to be exactly the heights
  anchor+1 .. min(tipAtWalkStart.height, anchor.height + deltaWindow); an empty walk is complete
  only when the anchor already is that tip; anything shorter is a failed walk that falls through to
  the cold scan. Define the tip captured when the walk starts as a specific view and say which.
  Note: requiring the anchor active on the served view does NOT close the empty-walk case, since
  every walk check holds vacuously on an empty block list.
- SERVED-CHAIN TIE. A committed walk's anchor must be active on the served view, not merely at or
  below its tip height.
- `Exhibits.delta_walk_empty_below_tip_committed` asserts the defect as current behaviour: invert it.
  Add exhibits for: a short walk falling through to the cold scan; the latched-no-attempt refresh
  cold-scanning; a latched walk advancing the one cache that fire-time reads.
- Keep the `DeltaCommit` guard (`partialWalk | tipOnly`) and the others; RE-MEASURE every CI
  negative control in gates.yml that the change touches (delta commit, import bracket, marker anchor,
  tip test, cursor shape), at exact counts, each run alone in a scratch copy.
- TRACE FORMAT: bump `Trace` format `version` from 1 to 2 (the byte layout changed in 8d69be3:
  LedgerRow.vaultSpends, the wallet's marker list, vaultRepair's atMarker and Scan) and re-render
  the published trace vector/digest through the gates that hold it; update any gate control that
  references the old hex.

## 3. The sweep (the review of 54adc47..HEAD; list at .context/code-review-54adc47.md)

Method, which converged last time: check EVERY sentence in tools/formal/, CONTEXT.md and ADR-0024
that cites a Lean declaration or quotes a requirement against that declaration's signature or that
requirement's current text; sweeping is the task, the list is a starting point, not a promise of
completeness. Items the review named: 5 (Chain.lean's stale "captured tip hash" quote and
Watchtower.lean's pass docstring), bps-8s0.11.17's three Watchtower.lean docstrings
(`pass_tip_changed`, `tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff`, `pass_completed`), 6 and 7 (ADR-0024 context
and decision 6 rationale), 8 (CONTEXT.md "Completion marker" must state all of WTC-8's conditions or
point at WTC-8 without claiming sufficiency), 10 (the module header's guard count), 11 (Chain.lean's
"wallet anchor"), 12 (factor the WTC-12 walk check into one helper used by Watchtower.proven,
deltaWalk and settledWalkProven, only if no theorem statement changes), 13 (register ADR-0024's
inline 10 and 32 in check_copies.py's owner registry, as ADR-0014's figures are).

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an exact
count; the citation gate verifies the re-quoted text; bps-8s0.11.17 closed with this bead. NO commit
message in the Run may carry a Co-Authored-By trailer or any tool attribution. Out of scope: SEC-50 (bps-8s0.11.14), the universal
coverage proof (bps-8s0.11.16), tracker records that name advisers (owner's decision: leave them).
close_reason: Landed in the working tree for one commit: WTC-6/WTC-9 and ADR-0024 amended verbatim from the settled patch; VaultUnspent.lean has one cache slot, an attempt flag, the full-range walk (coversRange/walkEnd) and the served-chain tie, with latched_no_attempt_serves_cold, latched_refresh_never_wallet_read and failed_attempt_restarts_from_cold_scan as theorems; Trace.version = 2 with the vector and digest re-rendered; delta-commit control re-measured 3 -> 2, the other flip controls unchanged, and the DEF-12 marker control corrected 3 -> 4 (stale at HEAD); review sweep items 5-8, 10-13 applied across tools/formal, CONTEXT.md and ADR-0024. All nine gates pass.

ADR-0024's Consequences records that CNF-89 and CNF-91 grew rows for the earlier amendment, but no conformance item demonstrates either new behaviour, so an implementation that commits a short or empty walk, or keeps delta-walking under the latch after a failed attempt, passes the checklist. title: M8 attempt lifecycle and review fixes: WTC-6/WTC-9 latch wording, the walk's own tip, guard controls (delivers bps-8s0.11.20 and bps-8s0.11.19)
description:
Land the attempt-lifecycle wording decided 2026-10-01 together with the Lean model, and resolve
the 2026-10-01 code review of 3a74f89..cb14e72 (findings below). This also delivers
bps-8s0.11.20 (guard parameters and controls for the catch-up rules) and bps-8s0.11.19 (CNF-91),
which close with this bead. The wording is SETTLED by the spec owner after a four-adviser
consultation (all four answered); no Consultation is needed.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/latch-wording.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). Two additions:
- WTC-6 ends: "While the repair latch is set or a repair attempt is in progress, `WTC-9` restricts
  this order." (closes the review's finding that WTC-6's "MUST be served, in order of preference"
  had no latch exception).
- WTC-9 ends: "At most one repair attempt is in progress at a time. An attempt ends however it
  stops, whether or not its re-import began — a cold scan or wallet call that fails or overruns
  its `WTC-4` timeout ends it as a failure — and one that ends without rebuilding the wallet
  leaves the latch set, so the next refresh starts another." (closes the review's finding that
  WTC-9 said when an attempt starts but never when a failed one ends; the reference clears its
  in-progress flag on success, error, panic and spawn failure, and admits one attempt with an
  atomic compare-exchange).
Do not reword. If a Lean-side fact shows a sentence false, stop and say so in the report.

## 2. The Lean model (`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/VaultUnspent.lean` and its exhibits)

a. THE WALK'S TIP (review finding 1, the most important). WTC-6 says the walk covers "through the
   lesser of the tip captured when the walk starts and 32 blocks above that anchor". The model
   takes that tip from `serve`'s `v`, the view captured when the REFRESH starts, before the wallet
   read. If a block lands during the wallet read, the bracket discards the read, the node captures
   the new tip when the walk starts (as `chain::advance_confirmed_scan` does with `tip_height()`),
   and the model refuses that walk twice (`walkEnd` and the served-chain tie both use `v`) and
   cold-scans. Give the walk its own view captured when the walk starts; `coversRange`, `walkEnd`
   and the served-chain tie read it. Add an exhibit: a block arrives during the wallet read, the
   walk covers up to the new tip and is committed, no cold scan.
b. ATTEMPT LIFECYCLE per the new WTC-9 sentence: at most one attempt in progress; an attempt ends
   however it stops, including a cold scan or wallet call that fails or times out before the
   re-import; one that ends without rebuilding leaves the latch set and the next refresh starts
   another. `repair`'s "ends the attempt either way" now has a Markdown home; cite it. Model a
   failure before the re-import as ending the attempt.
c. `repair` takes `scanView`, `atDescriptors`, `atMarker` as free arguments (review finding 5,
   bps-8s0.11.20 item 2): tie the re-import to the cold scan that started the attempt.
d. Theorem (b) `latched_refresh_never_wallet_read` is proved by `rfl` and adds nothing over
   `latched_never_wallet` (review finding 8). Restate it so it has proof content and would go red
   if `refresh` stopped honouring the latch.
e. bps-8s0.11.20: guard parameters with `current` values, theorems over `current` in
   Exhibits.lean, and a measured gates.yml negative control each, for the rules the catch-up
   amendment (387505f) added as unconditional definitions: the full-range walk (`coversRange` /
   `walkEnd`), the latched-no-attempt cold scan, and the served-chain tie; an off-branch walk
   exhibit; and `attempting ⇒ latched` after a refresh stated as a theorem if it holds under the
   new WTC-6 pointer (an attempt can be in progress with the latch clear only on a first wallet
   build; say how the model treats that). AGENTS.md: "Every semantic choice a dated amendment
   changed is a guard parameter with a `current` value"; a value you can argue is not a dated
   semantic change may be dropped with the reason in the report.
f. Re-measure every gates.yml control the change touches, alone, in a scratch copy, at exact
   counts.

## 3. Records

- bps-8s0.11.19: CNF-91 (15-conformance-checklist.md) asks for the full-range walk, the
  latched-no-attempt cold scan and the attempt lifecycle, so an implementation lacking any of
  them fails the checklist.
- ADR-0024 decision 8 (review finding 6) still justifies committing below the tip by "A walk
  bounded at 32 blocks cannot always reach a tip that moved while it ran". Under the full-range
  rule the range is fixed by the tip captured when the walk starts, so the partial commit exists
  for a cache more than 32 blocks behind. Correct the rationale.
- ADR-0023 (review finding 7): the "Published exhibit, 2026-09-24: the trace format" section must
  record that the exhibit was re-published on 2026-10-01 as format version 2 (387505f), why (the
  wallet's marker list, LedgerRow.vaultSpends, vaultRepair's atMarker and Scan; then the single
  cache slot and attempt flag), and that a version-1 trace is now refused.
- bps-8s0.11.14 (review finding 9) quotes two sentences 387505f deleted ("a repair which keeps
  failing costs one cold scan per repair attempt and not one per pass"; "committing a walk that
  completes even where it ends below the tip and continuing on the next refresh"). Update its
  description with `br update --description-file` to cite the current WTC-6 and WTC-9 text.
- If you confirm that a wallet holding no marker (a first build that failed) satisfies WTC-9's
  latch condition vacuously and so retries a cold scan every refresh, where the reference
  deliberately does not latch an unseeded wallet, file it as a bead; do not change WTC-9 for it.

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an
exact count; bps-8s0.11.20 and bps-8s0.11.19 closed with this bead. NO commit message may carry a
Co-Authored-By trailer or a tool attribution. Out of scope: bps-8s0.11.16 (the universal coverage proof), bps-8s0.11.12.
close_reason: WTC-6/WTC-9 wording applied verbatim with the model, guards, controls and records; nine gates green and the six VaultUnspent controls pass at exact counts

title: A wallet holding no completion marker latches a repair vacuously and cold-scans every refresh; the reference does not latch an unseeded wallet
description:
`WTC-9` latches a repair on this condition: "If no completion marker the wallet holds has an anchor
on the active chain the node MUST latch a repair, keep the wallet out of use until a cold scan and
re-import have rebuilt it". A wallet that holds no completion marker at all — the wallet before its
first build, and the one a first build that failed leaves — satisfies that condition with nothing
to check. The formal model reads it that way: `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.no_marker_latches` proves
`observe` latches every wallet whose marker list is empty, on every view.

With the attempt lifecycle `WTC-9` now carries, the consequence is a cold scan on every refresh.
`WTC-9`: "A refresh that finds the latch set and no repair attempt in progress starts one from a
cold scan that replaces the cache before the re-import begins (`WTC-6`)", and of an attempt that
fails, "one that ends without rebuilding the wallet leaves the latch set, so the next refresh
starts another." So on a backend where the wallet build cannot succeed — `WTC-3` lets a node run
with no usable wallet RPC: "The probe warns and does not refuse: a slow node is a live node" — every
refresh that finds no attempt in progress cold-scans, and the delta walk never becomes the source.
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.failure_before_reimport_restarts` and
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.failed_attempt_restarts_from_cold_scan` are that loop in the model. That is
the shape `DEF-9` records as a defect: "every restart and every periodic refresh repeated it."

The reference implementation deliberately does otherwise. `vault-node`,
`chain::refresh_vault_unspent_cache_mode` sets the repair latch only when the wallet handle carries
an anchor and that anchor is no longer active; a wallet it never had is seeded after the cold scan
without the latch, and when that seed fails the next pass finds a warm cache and a clear latch,
takes the delta walk, and does not retry the build until a later reorg or a restart. Its own
comment gives the reason: re-entering the cold-scan branch every pass would turn one transient
failure into a scan storm.

So the specification and the reference differ on an unseeded wallet, and the specification's
reading is the expensive one. Three ways to settle it, for the owner:

1. Keep `WTC-9` as worded and accept the cost: a node with no usable wallet cold-scans every
   refresh. Then `SEC-50`'s "every refresh pays it" is right as it stands and bps-8s0.11.14 closes
   with a citation fix only.
2. Scope the latch to a wallet that holds at least one marker, as the reference does, and say
   separately when an unseeded wallet's build is retried. Then `WTC-9`'s first sentence, `observe`
   in the model, and the first-build treatment in `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.refresh` move together,
   and a first build becomes an attempt with the latch clear.
3. Keep the latch but bound the retry — a failed first build is not retried every refresh — which
   needs a rule `WTC-9` does not have today.

Not changed by bps-8s0.11.21, which landed the lifecycle wording as settled and recorded this
question. Related: bps-8s0.11.14 (`SEC-50`'s cost sentence), `ADR-0024` Consequences.

Done when: the owner has chosen; `WTC-9` (and `WTC-3` or `SEC-50` if they move) say which wallets
latch and when an unseeded wallet's build is retried; the Lean model and its exhibits agree; and
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: repair's scan tie pins the scan's tip and outputs, not the settled block rebuild reads from the scan view
description:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.repair` ties the re-import to the cold scan its attempt started from by
comparing scan results: it rebuilds only when `coldScan L scanView` equals the scan the state
recorded (`State.repairScan`), which is the scan's outputs and its tip. `Chain.View` is a map from
heights to hashes with a tip, and nothing in the model makes a tip's hash fix the blocks beneath
it, so a `scanView` with the same tip and live outputs but a different block at the settled height
passes the tie, and `rebuild` then reads that view's settled block. A probe in review (2026-10-01,
Run 20261001T222811) had `refresh` record a scan on hashes `[100, 101]` and `repair` accept
`[200, 101]`, clear the latch and install a marker anchored at hash 200. `repair`'s docstring
states the limit ("the tie is as strong as the model's standing assumption that a block's hash
fixes the chain beneath it"); `rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan` proves equality of scan results
only. A real hash chain rules such a view out, so no conforming node is affected; the question is
whether the model should hold it.

Options for the owner: (1) accept the limit as stated; (2) have the state record what `rebuild`
reads from the scan view (the settled block, or the view as the trace's hash list) and drop or
bind `scanView`; this changes `State`'s encoding and so the trace format version. Done when: the
owner has chosen, and under (2) the mismatched-view case is an exhibit that is refused.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: The served-chain tie on a delta walk's result has no sentence in WTC-6 and no conformance row
description:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.ChainTie` (`tied` as current) refuses a delta walk whose resulting anchor
is not active on the view captured when the walk starts, even where the walk links from the cached
anchor and covers its range (`off_branch_walk_refused`). `WTC-6` has no sentence for that test: it
says "from a cached anchor whose block is still active" of the base, and "as is one that fails any
proof (`WTC-12`)" of the walk. The guard cites `WTC-11`'s "a block hash at a height that no longer
matches". ADR-0024 records that the reference implementation's `vault-node`,
`chain::advance_confirmed_scan` captures only a height when the walk starts and makes no such
test, and CNF-91 does not ask for it, so an implementation without the tie passes the checklist
while the model holds it as a rule.

Owner to decide: (1) the tie is `WTC-12`'s "the last is active after the loop" or `WTC-11`'s rule
applied to the walk's result, and the guard's citation and CNF-91 should say so; or (2) it needs
its own sentence in `WTC-6`; or (3) it is not required and the guard's current value is wrong.
Done when: the tie has a quoted Markdown home and a conformance row, or is withdrawn.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: M8: unbuilt wallet not latched, retries only at cold scans already needed, served-chain tie dropped, ancestry premise on views (delivers bps-8s0.11.22, .23, .24)
description:
Land three spec-owner decisions of 2026-10-02 in the Markdown and the Lean model in one commit.
Each was put to a four-adviser consultation (all four answered) and then
decided by the owner; no Consultation is needed. Delivers bps-8s0.11.22, bps-8s0.11.23 and
bps-8s0.11.24, which close with this bead.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/unbuilt-wallet.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends WTC-6 (its
pointer now reads "While the repair latch is set or a build or repair attempt is in progress"),
WTC-9 (rewritten lifecycle, below), WTC-11 (the wallet site: "a wallet that holds completion
markers none of whose anchors is still active") and CNF-91. Do not reword it; if a Lean-side fact
shows a sentence false, stop and say so in the report. The citation gate will report about 18
Lean quotations to move (VaultUnspent, Exhibits, Chain).

What WTC-9 now decides (bps-8s0.11.22):
- The latch applies only to a wallet that HOLDS a completion marker and none of whose markers is
  active. A wallet holding no marker (never built, or a first build that failed) is not latched;
  WTC-8 already keeps it out of use.
- STATE-BASED first scan: from the latch setting until a cold scan has replaced the cache, every
  refresh with no attempt in progress starts a repair attempt from a cold scan, whatever cache it
  holds. (A consultation found that "the first refresh after the latch sets" let a refresh after
  a failed first scan delta-walk from the pre-latch, possibly wallet-derived, cache.)
- Thereafter, while latched, the cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback, and
  a wallet read never replaces it.
- After a failed attempt, the next attempt starts ONLY from a cold scan WTC-6 itself reaches with
  none in progress, and starts no scan of its own. An unbuilt wallet's first build and its
  retries start the same way. Stated consequence: a failed build or repair is not retried while
  delta walks succeed; the cache does not depend on the wallet. (Owner's choice over a retained-
  scan retry and over reverting built wallets to retry every refresh.)

## 2. The Lean model

a. `observe` latches only a wallet with a non-empty marker list none of whose anchors is active;
   `no_marker_latches` inverts (an unbuilt wallet is not latched).
b. State records whether a cold scan has replaced the cache since the latch set (or equivalent).
   `refresh`: latched, no scan yet since the latch, no attempt in progress -> cold scan, start an
   attempt, whatever the cache; latched and scanned since -> delta walk with WTC-6's cold-scan
   fallback, and a fallback cold scan reached with no attempt in progress starts one; unlatched
   with no marker -> an attempt (first build) starts only from a cold scan WTC-6 reaches. A failed
   attempt starts no scan of its own.
c. Theorems: (i) a latched refresh before any post-latch scan cold-scans whatever the cache holds;
   (ii) after a failed attempt no refresh cold-scans unless WTC-6's own order reaches one (no
   storm); (iii) an unbuilt wallet never latches; (iv) an exhibit of the stated liveness
   consequence: a failed attempt followed by succeeding walks starts no new attempt.
d. Guard parameters, per AGENTS.md ("Every semantic choice a dated amendment changed is a guard
   parameter with a `current` value"), for: the latch's scope (`scoped` | `vacuous`) and the
   retry trigger (`neededScan` | `everyRefresh`), each with its twin trace, theorems over
   `current` in Exhibits.lean and a measured gates.yml control. Re-examine `LatchedBase`; merge or
   retire it if the new parameters subsume it, with the reason.
e. bps-8s0.11.24: `ChainTie`'s `current` becomes `untied`. All four advisers: WTC-12's "after the
   loop the hash at the last height still equals the last scanned hash" is the rule, compared with
   the chain after the walk, and the extra test against the view captured before the walk only
   discards a correct walk on a branch that reorged in just before it; WTC-5 already refuses any
   cache not at the current tip. Keep `tied` as the documented alternative with its exhibit;
   re-measure its CI control (the flip direction changes).
f. bps-8s0.11.23: in `Chain.lean`, beside `View`, a `Prop` on a pair (or an admissible family) of
   views: each view's tip is active in that view, and two views sharing an active block at height
   h agree at every height at or below h (a block hash commits to its ancestry). A HYPOTHESIS,
   never an axiom. `rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan` keeps its unconditional conclusion; add a
   corollary carrying the premise that proves the settled blocks of the recorded scan view and
   `scanView` are equal, so `rebuild` reads the attempt's settled block. `State`, `repair`,
   `rebuild` and the trace encoding do not change for this item. Keep the review probe (a scan on
   hashes [100, 101], a repair accepting [200, 101]) as an exhibit showing the premise excludes it.
g. If item b changes `State`'s encoding, bump the trace format version and record it in ADR-0023
   beside versions 2 and 3, with the reason.
h. Re-quote every broken quotation; re-measure every gates.yml control the change touches, alone,
   in a scratch copy, at exact counts.

## 3. Records

- ADR-0024: record the three decisions and their rejected alternatives briefly (a retained-scan
  retry; reverting built wallets to retry every refresh; recording the settled block in the
  attempt's state; keeping the served-chain tie as a new WTC-6 rule). Consequences: the reference
  does not latch an unseeded wallet (matches) but retries a failed latched repair on every pass
  (now diverges); the reference makes no served-chain tie (now matches).
- bps-8s0.11.14 (SEC-50): if its description quotes WTC-6 or WTC-9 text this patch changes,
  update it with `br update --description-file` to cite the current text.

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an
exact count; bps-8s0.11.22, .23 and .24 closed with this bead. NO commit message may carry a
Co-Authored-By trailer or a tool attribution. Out of scope: bps-8s0.11.16, bps-8s0.11.12.
close_reason: Delivered in 325c7bc. Nine gates green (Manager's own run, alone, unpiped, RC=0); gates.yml steps 37-42 pass at exact counts; four-reviewer Panel returned no findings.

title: M8: the first build has no scan-tie theorem, and latched-and-attempting-implies-scanned is not stated as an invariant
description:
From the review of bps-8s0.11.25 (commit 325c7bc). Two properties the model has by construction
but no theorem states, so a later edit could break either with every gate green.

1. The first build has no scan-tie theorem. `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan`
   and `rebuild_reads_the_attempts_settled_block` both take `st.latched = true`, so they cover a
   repair only. Since 325c7bc an unbuilt wallet's first build is an attempt that runs with the
   latch clear (`refresh` starts it at a served cold scan where `st.wallet.markers.isEmpty`), and
   `repair` holds it to its scan in code, but nothing proves it. Wanted: the sibling theorem keyed
   on `st.wallet.markers = []` and the wallet gaining a marker, with its corollary under
   `Chain.Ancestry`.

2. `failed_attempt_starts_no_scan` assumes `st.scanned = true`. Every latched attempt a refresh
   starts has it (`cold_scan_starts_attempt` sets it; `refresh`, `repair` and a latched
   `State.observe` keep it), but no theorem states `latched ∧ attempting → scanned` as an invariant
   preserved by `refresh`, `repair`, `endAsFailure` and `State.observe`. Wanted: the one-step
   preservation lemmas, so the "no scan storm" theorem's premise is discharged for every reachable
   state and the unreachable corner `latched ∧ ¬scanned ∧ attempting` (where `deltaBase` walks from
   the cache) is excluded rather than merely not produced.

No Markdown change; no guard parameter; no trace-format change. Done when both are proved, the
nine gates are green and any gates.yml control whose count moves is re-measured.

VaultUnspent.attemptInvariant pairs the latched-running-implies-scanned property with the unlatched-running-implies-marker-free property. Its no-attempt base and preservation lemmas cover refresh, repair, endAsFailure and scoped observation.
