title: CI: run the gates workflow as four parallel jobs; the identifier controls skip the kernel replay
description:
The gates workflow takes about 32 minutes on the public runner: one job, every step in series. The owner
decided on 2026-10-02 to run it as four parallel jobs and to stop the two identifier controls
from paying for a kernel replay they do not use. The design below is settled; no consultation is needed.

## Measured (2026-10-02, commit 28bae18, ubuntu-24.04 public runner, 4 CPU)

- Job: 32.5 min.
- `Run all gates`: 285 s. Inside it: dev shell 22 s, Lean build 73 s, then the index, the
  `leanchecker --fresh` replay, render and values in about 185 s, then the other eight gates in 3 s.
- The 71 controls: 1655 s in series.
- `Prove the identifier gate rejects a tag naming a withdrawn id` and `... an undefined id`:
  196 s and 193 s. Each runs the whole formal gate only to get `.lake/index.jsonl`, and the
  replay is most of that time.
- Per-step GitHub times: `/var/tmp/ctl/gh-steps-28bae18.tsv` (number, name, start, end).
- On this machine, four controls at a time peak at 11.7 GB. Each job runs its steps in series,
  so memory is not a constraint.

## 1. `tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`

- The flag skips only the `lake env leanchecker --fresh BtcPolicy` block. Everything else runs
  unchanged and in the same order: the greps, the build, the import walk, the index, render and
  values. When skipped, it prints one line saying the replay was skipped.
- Any other argument is an error that exits 2.
- `tools/check-all.sh` still calls it with no argument, so the full gate always replays.
- The two identifier controls above pass `--no-replay`. No other control changes its call: the
  other eleven expect a failure before the replay is reached.

## 2. `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: four parallel jobs

- Strategy: `fail-fast: false`, `matrix: shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- Job name: `specification gates (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})`.
- Checkout and install-nix run on every shard, with no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` gets `if: matrix.shard == 0`. Its body is unchanged.
- A new step right after it, `if: matrix.shard != 0`, runs
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`. It builds the `.lake` that the
  controls copy, including the index, regions and values that the citation, copies and regions
  controls read.
- Every control step gets exactly one `if: matrix.shard == N` in that literal form, with N in the
  matrix list. Do not reorder, rename or edit the control bodies. The two `--no-replay` edits
  are the only body changes.
- **Balance the shards from the measured times.** Shard 0 carries `Run all gates` (285 s).
  Every other shard carries the formal setup step, estimated at 130 s. Each identifier control
  is estimated at 196 s minus 150 s for the replay. Assign controls longest first (LPT) so the
  four estimated shard totals sit within 10% of their mean. Record the estimated totals in the
  report, not in the repository.

## 3. A guard that every step runs on the shards it should, with its own negative control

Write a small check (a Python script under `tools/`, run in the dev shell) and run it from a step
on shard 0. It fails, with a message naming the step, unless all of these hold:

- The matrix shard list is exactly `[0, 1, …, N-1]`.
- Checkout and install-nix have no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` has `if: matrix.shard == 0`, and its body is exactly
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`.
- The formal setup step has `if: matrix.shard != 0`.
- Every other step has exactly `if: matrix.shard == N`, with N in the list.
- `tools/check-all.sh` does not contain `--no-replay`.

Following this repository's rule that every gate is proven able to fail, add a control step. In a
scratch copy it deletes one control's `if:` line and asserts the guard exits nonzero with the
exact expected message. It also asserts the guard passes on the untouched copy.

## 4. Prose

Grep `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/` for any sentence that the new layout makes
false: one job, steps in order, or every step running on every push. Fix only those sentences.

- `README.md` lines 25 and 40 stay true. CI still runs `check-all.sh`, now on shard 0, and
  still breaks a document on every run.
- `AGENTS.md` keeps "`.github/workflows/gates.yml` holds the list".

No ADR is needed. This is CI layout, not a specification decision.

## Done when

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` passes, run unpiped and alone in the checkout.
- `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <steps>` passes on the working tree
  for the new guard, its control and the two identifier controls. Split the steps into chunks
  that each finish within 10 minutes.
- Each shard is replayed after the commit, in a clean worktree. That replay is the maintainer's
  job, not this one's.
- The guard's control is measured at its exact message.
- One commit. No commit message, and no added line in any file, names a model, a review tool or
  an adviser, or carries a Co-Authored-By trailer. This repository is public.
close_reason: Workflow runs as four shards; identifier controls skip the replay; tools/check_shards.py guards the layout with its own control

title: Inherit: a pair's duress bit is the OR of every arm intent naming it, and any holder decision arms with it (withdraws per-Carrier)
description:
**Decided 2026-10-02 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel: inherit.** A pair has one
duress bit, the OR of the duress bits of every arm intent naming its spend commitment. Any holder
decision on that pair arms with that bit: overlay `arm`, `sweep_active`, the `selected_escapes`
insertion and the freeze. Per-Carrier is the withdrawn reading. `DUR-10` already applies the same
OR to the Escape entry: "the entry's duress bit becomes the OR of its old value and the new
intent's, so a normal-PIN replay can never clear a duress authorization".

**Why.** `DUR-4` keys intent "by the Carrier identity", and `NCH-31` makes the identity commit to
the plaintext PIN, so two requests for one pair are two Carriers. Under per-Carrier, whichever
reaches `t` first decides.

On the current kernel, from `Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.w0`, this trace releases the coerced hot
partial on an unarmed node:
1. `accept 10 true … c1 e1`;
2. `accept 11 false … c1 e1`;
3. `receipt 11 1`;
4. `firePass`.

The release does not need the normal PIN. `SPN-5`'s gate table stages a `BAD_PIN` refusal at gate
14 (row 14: `consumed`, `yes`, `yes`), and `DUR-4`'s intent holds "its two commitment ids". If a
wrong-PIN Carrier names a resident pair, its holder decision opens it. That breaks `SEC-24`'s
"flooding wrong PINs produces denial and never an unfrozen quorum". The set does not say whether
a gate-12 intent has its commitment ids before the PSBTs decode at gate 17. Inherit closes the
path either way: a node holding the duress intent arms, and a node without it has no pair a
refused request registered.

Freezing without arming was rejected. It makes the node freeze while unarmed and inside the
horizon, which `DUR-1` forbids. Three readers built that rule independently, and `Silence.silence`
failed on `NodeInv.unfrozen`. Two readers independently built inherit:
- `check-all.sh` passes, `Silence.silence` proves, and no exhibit goes red;
- the trace above arms the node, freezes the hot candidate, and releases only the Escape partial
  past the horizon;
- the combined patch with `bps-8s0.29`'s fix also passes.

**Wanted.** Land inherit as a `Kernel.Rules` guard parameter, with per-Carrier as the withdrawn
value. The trace above goes in `Exhibits.lean` as its twin, with a flip step in
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` and its error count measured. Text changes:
- `DUR-5`: "write the overlay with `arm = intent.duress`" becomes the pair's duress bit, and
  "add the pair's Escape to `selected_escapes` with the intent's duress bit (`DUR-10`)" becomes
  "with the pair's duress bit".
- `SPN-23`: "re-applies its schedule and intent, and re-stages" becomes "re-applies its schedule,
  records its own intent (`DUR-4`), and re-stages". Add the converse of its duress-resubmission
  sentence: a resubmission whose pair a duress intent names arms at its own holder decision.
- `SPN-37`: "opened only by its own Carrier's holder decision (`DUR-5`)" becomes "opened only by
  the holder decision of a Carrier naming it (`DUR-5`)". Make the matching change to `DUR-8`'s
  "waits for its own Carrier's holder decision".
- `CNF-29`: add the converse case.
- `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4: dated amendment of "arming is a receipt reaching `t` on a
  Carrier whose intent bit is set".
- `CONTEXT.md`, written after the rule lands:
  - *Release gate*: "opens only on the candidate's own holder decision" becomes "opens only on
    the holder decision of a Carrier naming the candidate's pair".
  - A new *Pair duress bit* entry.
  - *Arm intent*: notes that two Carriers over one pair carry separate intents, and the pair acts
    on their OR.

**`T`'s start (decided).** `DUR-13`'s `first_seen` is the earliest `first_seen` among every arm
intent naming the pair, under both PINs. A later copy must not stretch the hostage window, which
`DUR-13` forbids: "so that slow or selective delivery cannot stretch the hostage window". Taking
the earliest of the duress intents only would make `T` depend on the PIN. Amend `DUR-13`'s "from
the intent's `first_seen`" to match. In `Kernel.newDeadline`, the minimum is read over the
Carriers naming `k.spend`.

**Sticky, on the nonce tombstone (decided).** Inherit's bit must outlive an intent that retires
uncommitted.

On correct clocks, an intent's `D` can lapse before the pair's `E`. `NCH-33` samples `M` "before
authentication", so a wait for the lock shortens `D`. A normal copy accepted while A is resident
can then reach `t` after A retires, and under resident-only inherit it releases. Two readers built
the trace.

The record that already outlives the intent is the nonce tombstone. `NCH-40` says it "keeps `D`
and remains a capacity entry until both wall expiry and `D` have ended". That lifetime is the
window in which a copy of the pair can still be admitted (`SPN-10`: "`expiry > effective_now`").
Storing the bit there:
- adds no store;
- leaves `SPN-32`'s "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is" intact;
- keeps `NCH-34`, because the tombstone confers no holder authority.

Text:
- `NCH-40`: the tombstone keeps, from retirement, the intent's duress bit, `first_seen` and two
  commitment ids, conferring no holder authority (`NCH-34`).
- `DUR-5` and `DUR-13`: the pair's duress bit and `first_seen` range over this intent, every

title: POL-4's beyond-max theorem has premises the documented derive cannot meet, and POL-4's skip rule has no model
description:
`BtcPolicy.Membership.not_matches_beyond_max` is the formal home of the upper end of `POL-4`'s
"derive indices `0..=max` if it has a wildcard", which `CNF-15` tests as "not at `max + 1`". Both
of its premises range over every `SinglePath`, not over `d.paths`:

- `hdistinct : ∀ p q, p ≠ q → ∀ i j, derive p i ≠ derive q j` fails for every `derive` that reads
  only `id`. `SinglePath`'s docstring calls `id` "its identity (keys, origin, script context —
  everything `derive` reads)", so two paths that differ only in `wildcard` derive the same scripts.
- `hinj : ∀ p i j, derive p i = derive p j → i = j` fails for every `derive` that is constant in
  the index on a definite path. `POL-4` says "A definite descriptor ignores `max`".

The two premises can both hold, but only for a `derive` that also reads `wildcard` and puts
distinct scripts at definite-path indices no scan reads. So the theorem is not vacuous in the
abstract; it is vacuous under the module's own description of `derive`. Its premise `_hp` is
unused, and no exhibit instantiates it.

Second, `POL-4` says "An index the library cannot derive is skipped", but
`derive : SinglePath → Nat → Script` is total, so a failed derivation has to be some script. An
empty-script sentinel matches an empty output script. The module docstring's "The structure
covered is the whole of what `POL-4` requires beyond that boundary" is therefore not yet true.

Wanted:
- `derive : SinglePath → Nat → Option Script`, where a failed derivation contributes no match.
- `matchesScript derive max d s = true ↔ ∃ p ∈ d.paths, ∃ i ∈ indices max p, derive p i = some s`.
- The bound stated as locality, with no premise and over the bound itself: two `derive`s that agree
  on every `p ∈ d.paths` and every `i ≤ max` give the same `matchesScript`.
  - Do not state it over `i ∈ indices max p`. That form still proves when the wildcard range is
    `List.range (max + 2)`, so it does not pin the bound.
- `not_matches_beyond_max` kept as `CNF-15`'s formal home, restated for a wildcard path only:
  `p ∈ d.paths` with `p.wildcard = true`. Its premises are that `derive p (max + 1)` differs from
  every `derive q i` with `q ∈ d.paths` and `i ∈ indices max q`. That is local to `d`, and a
  `derive` constant in the index on definite paths meets it. Add an exhibit that instantiates it.
  - The wildcard condition is required, not optional. On a definite path, a `derive` that ignores
    the index has `derive p (max + 1) = derive p 0`, which the scan reads, so the old conclusion is
    false there. `CNF-15`'s "not at `max + 1`" is about wildcard scans in any case.
- An exhibit that a `derive` returning `none` everywhere matches nothing.
- `kindOf` and `member_discharged` carried over, unchanged in meaning.

Evidence: reviewers A, B, C and D of the 2026-10-02 reading, each with scratch builds. The
off-by-one mutation and both locality forms were compiled. The exhibits above land those probes in
the repository.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- in a scratch copy, changing the wildcard range in `indices` to `List.range (max + 2)` turns a
  `POL-4`-tagged theorem red;
- every `POL-4`-tagged theorem that has a premise has an exhibit instantiating it.

title: CHN-11's sighash has no BIP143 instance, but the Kernel docstring and ADR-0023 item 4 say milestone 5 supplied one
description:
`CHN-11`'s sighash has no instance, and two records say it does. The `Kernel` module docstring
and `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4 both say "milestone 5 supplies the BIP143 encoder as its
instance". Milestone 5 (`bps-8s0.5`) never listed a BIP143 encoder and closed without one: its
six tickets are `Encode`, the `CHN-24` edit, `CoordRequest`, `Manifest`, `Witness` and the
packaging test. The sentence entered with milestone 4.

Item 4 also calls the sighash "a structure whose field is a function of the transaction and the
input index". In the code, `BtcPolicy.Kernel.sighash` is a plain `def` over
`abbrev Sighash := Nat × Nat`, so there is nowhere for an instance to plug in.

Because the declaration carries `@[req "CHN-11"]`, the requirement index lists `CHN-11` against
`sighash` alone. What `sighash` actually formalizes is one property of `CHN-11`: the message is a
function of the transaction and the input, "and of no request field". It does not formalize
`CHN-11`'s "BIP143 P2WSH sighash computed with `SIGHASH_ALL` … with the input's `witness_utxo`
value".

The defect is in the accepted ADR's record of what milestone 5 delivered and what the boundary is.
Correcting the code comment alone would be cosmetic.

Wanted:
- `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4 and the `Kernel` docstring name the BIP143 instance as an open
  boundary, not a milestone-5 deliverable.
- Item 4 describes the sighash as it is: a fixed symbolic definition, not a pluggable structure.
- `sighash`'s docstring says which part of `CHN-11` it formalizes and which part is the boundary.

Building a BIP143 framing encoder is a separate `ADR-0023` decision and out of scope here.
`Encode`'s docstring already records why framing stops at the digest: "(decision 3, and the bead:
no SHA-256 in Lean)". Framing alone would prove a field layout and nothing about binding.

Done when `tools/check-all.sh` is green and neither record claims an instance or a structure the
formal layer lacks.

title: Kernel accept re-registers a resident pair: a fresh-nonce resubmission revives a claw-back-defeated hot spend
description:
**Decided 2026-10-03 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel, which agreed unanimously.**
Registration is indivisible. A resident candidate under either requested id is compatible only if
it is resident **as this pair**: in the role the request gives it, with the request's other id
recorded as its sibling (`SPN-36`), over the same `tx`, `hot` and `expiry`. Anything else is a
conflicting resident commitment, `PSBT_INCONSISTENT` / `candidate_identity`, and the refusal leaves
every resident candidate untouched: exactly one id resident; both resident but in two different
pairs (`(S1,E2)` with `(S1,E1)` and `(S2,E2)` resident); the swapped request `(E1,S1)`; a
resident claw-back (`SPN-51`, no sibling) under either id; and `sp.id = es.id`.
- The prototypes' `pairAdmits` (both-or-neither plus per-id fields) MUST NOT land as written: it
  admits the cross and swapped requests and opens `c1` under them.
- Kernel: the role and sibling live on `Cand`, stamped by `register`. An equal-expiry premise on
  `accept` alone refuses neither the cross nor the swapped case; it is the extra premise for an
  invariant that every resident member's sibling is resident with the same expiry.
- A gate-29 refusal still stages (`SPN-5` row 29); its holder decision follows `bps-8s0.34`.
- **The ladder (decided the same day, after a second four-reader panel, unanimous).** Compatibility
  also requires the resident Escape to hold the request's rung txids in the same order, the empty
  list included. A different ladder over the same spend and base Escape is a conflicting resident
  commitment. Compare txids, never PSBT bytes (`SPN-23` sends changed bytes of the same
  transaction to fresh evaluation, and those stay compatible), and never held partials, the rung
  latch, the release floor or `released_through`, which can differ by PIN (`DUR-1`). This is
  `SPN-32` and `CNF-34` text only: `Cand` models no ladder, and no Lean change is wanted for it.
  An honest repeat carries the same ladder (`CHN-17` is a function of the base) and is a gate-19
  replay; a different ladder needs only a coordinator stripping rungs (`SEC-21`).
- **`SPN-29`.** A registration refusal unwinds only the velocity reservation this request placed;
  a reservation an earlier acceptance of the same commitment placed stays (`POL-18`).
- The cross-node ladder split is a different requirement, filed separately; not part of this bead.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round5-pair/` and `round6-ladder/` (briefs, answers, patches, exhibits).

`BtcPolicy.Kernel.accept` re-registers a resident pair, so a fresh-nonce resubmission revives a hot
spend that a claw-back has defeated.

`SPN-32` owns the rule: "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is" and "a
conflicting resident commitment is `PSBT_INCONSISTENT` / `candidate_identity`". `SPN-23`'s replay
"re-stages", and staging belongs to the Carrier: per `SPN-32`, the node "stages the Carrier — pushes
the request to the outbox and counts itself as a holder".

Beside its lockdown guard, `accept` checks resident Carrier ids but not resident candidate ids. On a resubmission it prepends fresh `born` copies with `terminal := false` and
`released := false`.

Trace on the current kernel, from `Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.w0`:
1. `accept 10 false … c1 e1`;
2. `settle claw`, which marks candidate 1 terminal;
3. `accept 11 false … c1 e1`, the same pair under a fresh nonce;
4. `receipt 11 1`;
5. a fire pass after the claw-back is evicted.

The pass emits `queuePartial (sighash tx1 0) 0 true 1`, and a terminal copy of candidate 1 is still
resident. Without step 3 the pass emits nothing.

That is `F57`'s defect class in the model. `SPN-33` says "a hot spend a claw-back has defeated is
not finalized at its Hold expiry even if the claw-back is later evicted", and `terminal_sticky`'s
own disjunct, "or was born by this step", admits the revival. The guard does not read the PIN.

`accept` also takes `sp.id = es.id` and registers two candidates under one id.

Wanted:
- An accept whose pair is resident, with equal `tx`, `hot` and `expiry`, adds its Carrier and
  leaves the candidates exactly as is.
- A resident id with any other field, or `sp.id = es.id`, is refused.
- Say whether a replay still runs `DUR-14`'s shrink and `DUR-20`'s traversal, since `SPN-23` says
  it "re-applies its schedule".
- A theorem: on every `Reachable` world, one id names at most one resident candidate.
- `terminal_sticky` restated so that a resident terminal id is never matched by a non-terminal
  candidate.
- The trace above as an exhibit that releases nothing under `current`, plus a same-PIN and a
  cross-PIN replay that leave the resident candidates' `terminal`, `released` and `heldSigners`
  untouched.

Evidence: reviewer B (scratch builds, with the control run), reviewers C and D (same-PIN
duplication).

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: silence's relation stops at a resubmission after its pair's holder decision: wfEvent refuses SPN-23's repeat
description:
`BtcPolicy.Silence.silence`'s relation stops at a resubmission.

`obsPair` walks a trace only while `wfEvent` holds. `wfEvent` refuses an accept whose candidate ids
are already in `selected`, and `selected` holds Escape ids, which a holder decision inserts. So a
resubmission after its pair's holder decision ends the walk; an earlier one is walked.
`wfEvent`'s docstring justifies the refusal as requiring "what the identifiers intend". But `SPN-23`
specifies that repeat: a request whose acceptance key matches an earlier `Accepted` "re-applies its
schedule and intent, and re-stages".

title: silence's starting premises cannot be derived from Reachable: Reachable.init leaves sweepActive free
description:
`silence`'s starting premises cannot be derived from `Reachable`, because
`BtcPolicy.Kernel.Reachable.init` pins only `armed = false`, `cands = []` and `carriers = []`. It
leaves `sweepActive` free, so a node with `armed = false`, `sweepActive = true` and
`selected = [(7, true)]` is `Reachable`, and it fails `Silence.NodeInv`'s sweep clause (reviewers A
and C, compiled).

`silence` takes `NodeInv` at the trace's first sample, "assumed here and not derived from
reachability", and `Exhibits.TwoRun.nodeInv_A` discharges it for one concrete start only.

No theorem is false. `holderDecision` sets `armed` and `sweepActive` with the same `|| k.duress`,
so `sweepActive = armed` is preserved by every event (compiled), but nothing states it. This is a
missing invariant, not a bug.

Wanted:
- `Reachable.init` pins `sweepActive = false`. Pinning `selected = []` as well is optional: the
  corollary below does not need it.
- A theorem `sweepActive = armed` over `Reachable`.
- `no_entry_released_before_arming` restated over `armed = false`.
- A corollary, after `Init.silence_from_init` in `.context/vault-review-1002/probes/Init.lean`:
  `silence` for two runs from the same node, the same ledger and empty exposure, with
  `armed = false`, `sweepActive = false` and empty candidates. The rule and monotone-sample
  hypotheses stay explicit.

This establishes initialization only, not `NodeInv` for every `Reachable` state. Pinning `init`
removes worlds from every `Reachable` theorem, which is intended: the removed worlds have
`selected` entries that no accepted Carrier put there.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- the guard-parameter flips in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still fail at their asserted
  `Exhibits.lean` sites;
- the corollary is tagged `DUR-1`.
close_reason: Below the filing bar: no theorem is false and the invariant already holds per step. Silence.NodeInv.sweep is sweepActive = armed and inv_sysStep preserves it on every event. Mutating holderDecision so a duress commit no longer sets sweepActive goes red in Silence.lean today, so pinning Reachable.init adds no catching power.

title: DUR-8's coupling has no theorem: prove hot-release provenance at input 0 and the counting corollary
description:
`DUR-8` says "So no honest node ever releases a coerced partial, only `≤ t − 1` compromised nodes
can, and that is never a signing quorum. This coupling, not the holder count, is the safety proof".
No declaration states it. The `Kernel` docstring says "`DUR-8`'s federation consequence is a
counting statement under `compromised < t`, not a theorem here", and `no_hot_partial_while_armed`
covers armed nodes only.

Wanted, node-local and at input 0, with no federation and no scheduler:
- **Provenance.** On every reachable world, a hot `queuePartial` for candidate `cid` is emitted
  only by an unarmed node, and only after a normal-PIN holder decision that opened `cid`, tied to
  the emitted message and commitment. Prove it over the event trace or recorded commit history:
  `holderDecision` retires the Carrier, so the Carrier need not stay resident. A ghost field on
  `Node` changes every `Node` literal in `Exhibits.lean`.
- **Counting corollary over the world's exposure.** The premise that every honest exposure row for
  a message carries that provenance is a named hypothesis, since `adversaryExposes` and
  `receivePartial` admit any signer. Under that premise, with no honest normal holder decision for
  the message and fewer than `t` distinct compromised signers, `exposedQuorum` is false for it.

Input 0 is enough for prevention. Under `SIGHASH_ALL`, `DUR-28`'s "`≥ t` distinct valid partials
on every input" makes a quorum at input 0 necessary for finalization, so counting there
over-approximates availability (reviewers A and B).

On an unarmed node every committed Carrier is normal-PIN: `holderDecision` sets
`armed := n.armed || k.duress`. So the statement holds on the current kernel and needs neither
`bps-8s0.26` nor `bps-8s0.31`.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- both theorems are tagged `DUR-8`;
- an exhibit instantiates the corollary at a concrete world, and another shows a successful normal
  release;
- a twin in which quorum opens without a holder decision refutes the provenance statement;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: A refused-but-staged Carrier's holder decision opens a resident pair: DUR-4 names commitment ids before SPN-23 computes them
description:
**Decided 2026-10-02 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel, which agreed unanimously.**
1. An arm intent names a pair only once `SPN-23` has computed the pair's commitments.
2. The holder decision of a refused Carrier opens nothing. A refused Carrier carrying a duress
   intent still arms.

**The defect.** `DUR-4` says the intent recorded at ingress (`SPN-5` gate 12) holds "its two
commitment ids". But the PSBTs decode at gate 17, and `SPN-23` computes the commitments "After all
preceding admission, PIN and post-preflight clock gates pass". The set never says when a gate-12
intent learns its ids.

`SPN-5`'s gate table stages some refusals: they consume the nonce, propagate and stage.
- **Before `SPN-23`:** gate 13 and 16 (clock predicates) and gate 14 (`BAD_PIN`). Read literally,
  `DUR-4` lets such an intent name a pair.
- **After `SPN-23`:** gate 21 (prevout fetch), gate 22 (only `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`), gate 24
  (`HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED`) and gate 27 (`EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` / `commitment_expiry`). These do name
  a pair.

`DUR-5`'s holder decision sets "`holder_quorum_reached` on both members of the pair, which opens
their release gate". So a refused Carrier that reaches `t` holders opens a resident pair that
this node refused to authorize, though `SPN-9` says "Neither path signs a partial". A gate-14
refusal needs no valid PIN at all. That contradicts `SEC-24`: "flooding wrong PINs produces denial
and never an unfrozen quorum".

**Wanted.**
- `DUR-4`: "its two commitment ids" becomes "its two commitment ids once `SPN-23` has computed
  them; an intent refused before then names no pair".
- `DUR-5`: a holder decision opens the pair only for a Carrier this node accepted, or replayed as
  accepted (`SPN-23`). For a refused Carrier it performs the same arm write, scan and set work
  under both PINs, and opens no candidate. It still arms with the duress bit, as `SEC-24` requires
  ("MUST arm regardless of lockout") and as `DUR-4` requires ("the duress bit MUST be set for a
  refused-but-staged duress request just as for an accepted one").
- `DUR-10`: "**Every** holder decision adds its intent's Escape id" applies only when the intent
  names a pair.
- The kernel gains a refused-but-staged acceptance event. A theorem states that its holder
  decision opens no candidate, with an exhibit replaying a staged refusal that reaches `t`.
- The `DUR-1` relation covers the new event.

**Interaction.** Independent of `bps-8s0.26`'s inherit rule, and needed under every reading. One
reader judged inherit's sticky extension unnecessary once this lands, so decide this before the
sticky question.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round4-sticky/` (briefs, four answers, four prototype
patches).

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count;
- the staged-refusal exhibit opens nothing under `current`.

title: A per-node ladder split leaves only the base Escape completing; SPN-38 and DUR-28 claim cross-node rung agreement
description:
**Correction 2026-10-04, after the first Run's review.** Decision 4's last sentence below ("The
escape-class spend/residual swap (ADR-0016, ADR-0012) can still suppress the residual sweep; keep
that power stated") is wrong and is withdrawn. ADR-0022 removed the escape-class pair: "Every
SpendRequest is now exactly a hot spend plus its Escape", and it removed "the swap in `SEC-21`'s
list". `CHN-23` and `OPR-25` refuse an `(Escape, Escape)` pair, and they stay unchanged. The swap is
history, not a live power. Decisions 1–3 and the rest of decision 4 stand.

Do now, inside this bead:
- `SEC-21`: delete the sentence asserting the swap as a current power.
- `SEC-21` still owns the suppression that other text files under it, and the change must not drop
  that. `16-open-findings.md`'s row "A selected Escape naming an absent or inflated prevout …
  raises every later denominator and can fail every real Escape" is filed as "accepted residual
  inside `SEC-21`'s suppression", and ADR-0020 calls the split-selection denial "inside the
  residual `SEC-21` already grants". State that suppression where it actually comes from: censoring
  or selectively delivering requests, including one whose selected Escape inflates the coverage
  denominator (`DUR-22`), and never from stripping. The denominator contract does not change.
- `DUR-10` and ADR-0020: ground "choosing which selected Escape confirms" in `SEC-21`'s "censor,
  selectively deliver", not in the stripping sentence. ADR-0020's Consequences quote `SEC-21` with
  words it no longer contains (the swap sentence); quote what `SEC-21` now says.
- ADR-0016's "A separate escape-class role-order residual is accepted" section, and anything else
  the first Run added about the swap: mark them as historical and withdrawn by ADR-0022, not as a
  current residual. ADR-0012's swap mention gets the same treatment if it reads as current.
- Re-grep for "swap", "spend/residual", "role-order" and "suppress" across the Markdown, ADRs and
  Lean docstrings, and reconcile every active reference.

The first Run's commits (924be5c, fa3ddb5, 8a83a8d) stay as they are: add commits and rewrite
nothing. Land this as one commit plus a `beads: close bps-444` commit.

**Decided 2026-10-04 (owner).** Implement as recorded; do not reopen. This block supersedes the
original finding below where they disagree, including its "Owner decision wanted", its "Also
unverified" section and its "Done when".

1. **Nodes do not recompute `CHN-17`.** ADR-0016 §4a and `MAN-13`'s "nodes never enforce it"
   stand, and the per-node ladder split is an accepted residual. Record the reasons in ADR-0016:
   ADR-0012's "Nodes validate the escape; they do NOT build it"; a gate-25 refusal stages nothing
   and so arms nothing, so any disagreement between the composer's and a node's derivation would
   leave an honest duress request unarmed; and with decision 2, every stripping outcome is bounded
   at the base.
2. **Every Escape transaction signals.** The base and every rung, with or without a ladder, set
   every input's `nSequence` to `0xfffffffd`, as refresh (`CHN-18`) and claw-back (`CHN-35`)
   already do. The non-signalling form is withdrawn. Signalling only permits a replacement and
   never blocks relay or confirmation, and under full-RBF (`CHN-15`'s own text) the mark buys
   nothing. The ladderless `0xffffffff` rule is what made a stripped base unbroadcastable.
3. **Gate 25 refuses an Escape transaction that does not signal**, base or rung, as
   `escape:bump_ladder`, the code `CNF-142` already gives `nSequence` faults. `DUR-23` drops its
   `nSequence` condition: ingress owns it.
4. **Consequence.** Stripping rungs, alike on every node or differently per node, only downgrades
   the `T`-time sweep, at worst to the base Escape when the base is admissible. The escape-class
   spend/residual swap (ADR-0016, ADR-0012) can still suppress the residual sweep; keep that power
   stated.

**Lands on** (every site found by grep; re-grep before closing):
- `CHN-15`: one rule, every Escape transaction at `0xfffffffd`; delete the opt-in-relay sentence.
  The "unlike the Escape (`CHN-15`) it never has the non-signalling form" asides in `CHN-18` and
  `CHN-35`. `OPR-25`'s "ladderless Escape carries `nSequence` `0xffffffff`".
- `SPN-27` names the signalling check and its refusal; `DUR-23` as in decision 3.
- `CNF-142`'s `nSequence` sentence; `CNF-118`'s "a ladderless Escape carries `0xffffffff`".
- `SEC-21`: stripping only downgrades, at worst to the base, whether alike or per node; ground any
  remaining "suppress" in the spend/residual swap. `DUR-10` quotes `SEC-21` ("strip ladder rungs
  and re-sign, and thereby suppress or downgrade the `T`-time sweep"), so change the quotation in
  the same commit; the citation gate checks it.
- `SPN-38`'s "so every honest node's cumulative prefix begins at the same rung" holds only over a
  common ladder. `DUR-28`'s "quorum on an Escape's own commitment id IS cross-node agreement on
  that Escape" holds for the base; append to it rather than replace it, because
  `16-open-findings.md` quotes it.
- ADR-0016, rewritten in place: the strip-all arm (now: the base sweeps at its own fee), the
  sentence on the composer rewriting the base to `0xfffffffd`, and any ladderless-sequence
  statement; add decision 1 and the per-node split as an accepted, bounded residual.
- A new `CNF-` item: `{base, r1}`, `{base, r2}` and `{base, r3}` delivered to 2, 2 and 1 nodes on
  `n = 5`, `t = 3`; every node finalizes at the base and no rung completes.
- A new `DEF-` entry in `14-known-defects.md`, owned by `CHN-15` and `DUR-23`: the reference
  composes `0xffffffff` for a ladderless Escape and refuses a signalling base with an empty ladder
  at fire (ADR-0016 names the test `a_ladderless_escape_still_requires_a_non_signalling_sequence`).
  Not reproduced here, so not marked *verified*.
- No Lean change: `CHN-15` has no Lean declaration, and the `SPN-38` and `DUR-28` sentences are
  prose. No vector change: the commitment vector's `0xffffffff` is encoding data, not an Escape.
  No glossary change.

Out of scope: a coerced user signing the base twice with different signature bytes. It needs the
user's key, so it is not a `SEC-21` power.

**Done when** every site above is changed, the new `CNF-` and `DEF-` entries exist, a grep finds no
remaining non-signalling Escape rule, and the full gate passes unpiped with every affected
`gates.yml` step run against the working tree.

---

**Original finding (2026-10-03).**

A post-wrench coordinator can deliver different ladders over one Escape to different nodes, so no
rung reaches `t` and the sweep finalizes at the base. `SPN-38` and `DUR-28` state a cross-node
agreement that holds only for the base transaction.

**Mechanism.** `SEC-21` gives the coordinator "selectively deliver, strip ladder rungs and
re-sign". Stripping needs no user key: any non-empty subset of a signed ladder still satisfies
`CHN-16`. Each node registers the ladder it receives first. `bps-8s0.29` (decided 2026-10-03)
refuses a later different ladder as `candidate_identity`, and honest relays (`SPN-35`, `NCH-27`)
deliver every variant to every node. A rung pools partials only where `NCH-24` finds that "the
rung is found by txid".
- **Three variants, n = 5, t = 3.** Delivering `{base, r1}`, `{base, r2}` and `{base, r3}` to 2, 2
  and 1 nodes leaves every rung below `t`, so every node finalizes at rung 0. A scratch model
  confirms this (`.context/vault-review-1002/round6-ladder/split-model.lean`).
- **Two variants on n = 2t − 1 nodes.** One group has at least `t` nodes, so its ladder can still
  complete there.
- **The base.** Rung 0 is the commitment itself, and `DUR-28` walks down to it, so an admissible
  base completes. A split ladder is therefore no worse than no ladder. The base splits only if the
  user signs it twice with different signature bytes, since `NCH-24` also requires "the
  user-signature hash matches"; that needs the user's key.
- **Bound.** `SEC-21`'s "suppress or downgrade the `T`-time sweep" covers this outcome. Freeze and
  Lockdown are untouched, so this is not `DUR-34`.

**Text that overstates.**
- `SPN-38`: "so every honest node's cumulative prefix begins at the same rung" needs a common
  ladder and matching user-signature hashes.
- `DUR-28`: "quorum on an Escape's own commitment id IS cross-node agreement on that Escape" is
  true of the base transaction only. `16-open-findings.md` quotes the sentence, so append to it
  rather than replace it.
- `SEC-21` does not say that stripping differently per node is the same power.

**Owner decision wanted.** Should nodes recompute `CHN-17`'s ladder at gate 25, so the Escape's id
fixes its ladder and the rung split closes?
- Cost: `SEC-21`'s and `DOM-3`'s rung-stripping power ends, and `CHN-17` is frozen for the vault's
  life.
- Gate 25 does not stage, so that refusal grants nothing new.

Rejected already:
- Binding the ladder into `CHN-24`: partials name `commitment_id` (`NCH-23`), so a ladder split
  becomes an Escape split and not even the base completes (same scratch model).
- Merging two ladders: it mutates a resident candidate.

**Also unverified, `SPN-27`.** Does gate 25 refuse a `0xfffffffd` base with no rungs?
- `CHN-15` and `CNF-142` say that combination is invalid.
- `SPN-27` applies the ladder rules "to every rung", which checks nothing when there are none.
- `ADR-0016` says the reference "returns `Ok(())` on an empty `escape_bumps`".
- If gate 25 admits it, `DUR-23` refuses that Escape at fire time, base included.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round6-ladder/` (brief, four answers, two scratch models).

Done when:
- the decision on recomputing `CHN-17` is recorded;
- `SPN-38`, `DUR-28` and `SEC-21` state the per-node ladder split;
- a conformance item exercises the three-variant split: the base completes and no rung does;
- the `SPN-27` empty-ladder question is answered, with a refusal row if gate 25 admits it.

title: Citation gate accepts false direct possessive quotations
description:
The citation gate accepts a false direct possessive quotation in a Lean docstring. This is a check's ability-to-fail gap discovered while reviewing bps-8s0.29, not a request to change its registration semantics or to file a cosmetic correction.

Reproduction at de452ffcf952aeee34f8c192b0b81d8610723b99 (also present at closure commit 64d457c): tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Ledger.lean's module header attributes the superseded unwind sentence to SPN-29 using the form `SPN-29`'s followed immediately by a quotation. The requirement now says "only a reservation placed by this request MUST be unwound in the same step". The header's old quotation is not recognized by tools/check_citations.py.

In an isolated copy of the tracked tree, with the generated requirement index copied in, the following runs of the actual citation gate established the gap:
- Unmodified tree: exit 0.
- Replace that SPN-29 quotation with "the moon is made of green cheese and nothing else", retaining the direct possessive attribution: exit 0, unchanged verified-attribution count.
- Use the same false text with the attribution written as `SPN-29`: followed immediately by the quotation: exit 1, reporting the false SPN-29 attribution.

ATTRIB recognizes speech verbs, the possessive noun-plus-that form, and colon quotations. It does not recognize a possessive followed directly by a quotation, even though that form attributes exact words just as directly. No change to the check's intentionally excluded summary-verb paraphrases is requested.

Done when the direct possessive quotation form is checked against its named requirement in Markdown and Lean docstrings, a deliberately false quotation in that form fails for the owning requirement, valid quotations still pass, and a workflow negative control demonstrates the new failure. Preserve existing historical-quotation exemptions, attribution ownership, nested-quotation behavior, and the unquoted baseline. Run the full repository gate unpiped and the affected workflow controls against the working tree.

This follow-up is outside the fixed bps-8s0.29/.34/.26/.30/.32/.27/.28 sequence and must not be picked by it.

title: Citation gate omits ADR attribution sources and accepts unrelated ADR quote text
description:
Found during review of bps-444 at fa3ddb5b16aad778066527890e3ca8dd28a55364. This is a separate check's ability-to-fail defect, not additional work for that Run.

tools/check_citations.py describes its quoted-attribution contract as: "A quoted phrase attributed to `X` must appear in X's own body." Its load and find functions do not enforce that boundary around ADRs:

- load includes root Markdown and Lean docstrings as attribution sources, but concatenates docs/adr/*.md only as quote text. Attributions made inside an ADR are never examined. ADR-0020's consequences section contains an attribution to SEC-21 that does not match the requirement, yet the full gate passes.
- find adds the entire concatenated ADR corpus to every requirement's acceptable quote pool. A false quotation attributed to a root requirement can therefore pass solely because the words appear in an unrelated ADR.

Read-only reproduction against the actual functions (no repository files changed):

```python
import runpy
m = runpy.run_path('tools/check_citations.py', run_name='citation_probe')
docs, adr, reqs, lean, nested = m['load']()
assert not any(p.startswith('docs/adr/') for p in docs)
quote = 'every input sequence carries a purple umbrella'
source = {'probe.md': '`CHN-15` says "' + quote + '".'}
assert m['find'](source, '', reqs)[0]
assert not m['find'](source, quote, reqs)[0]
```

The first false quotation produces a bad-attribution result naming CHN-15. Supplying the identical words only as unrelated ADR text removes that result. This is a function-level probe, not a claim that an end-to-end mutant gate was run. The real full gate passed independently at this revision.

This differs from bps-l9b's direct-possessive syntax recognition gap: the probe uses the already supported "says" syntax. No work on that bead is requested here.

Done when supported quoted attributions in ADR files are checked, quotes attributed to a requirement cannot be validated by unrelated ADR text, legitimate owner quotations and deliberately marked historical passages still pass, and CI negative controls run the actual gate on both defects and require the expected owner/file diagnostic. Preserve the existing ownership, nested-quotation, historical-marker and unquoted-baseline behavior. Run the repository full gate unpiped and all affected workflow steps against the working tree. Fix discovered false attributions on their owners' evidence without changing requirement behavior merely to silence the gate.

title: M8: attempt invariant over every reachable state; a first-build ancestry instance that says something; the .vacuous observation counterexample
description:
From the two-axis review of bps-8s0.11.14–.26 (range 2e044d4..7e2a98e). bps-8s0.11.26 landed the
attempt invariant as a base and four one-step lemmas, and its own closing comment states the
boundary: "not a new trace-level reachability theorem". Its description asked for the one-step
lemmas so that

> the "no scan storm" theorem's premise is discharged for every reachable state and the
> unreachable corner `latched ∧ ¬scanned ∧ attempting` (where `deltaBase` walks from the cache) is
> excluded rather than merely not produced.

Three gaps, each a statement no gate can fail on today.

1. No reachability theorem. `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.attemptInvariant`'s docstring: "no
   trace-level reachability theorem is asserted here". The pieces exist:
   `attemptInvariant_of_no_attempt`, `attemptInvariant_refresh` (every `Rules`),
   `attemptInvariant_repair`, `attemptInvariant_endAsFailure`, and `attemptInvariant_observe`
   (scope `.scoped` only). Wanted: a reachability predicate over the states those operations
   produce from a no-attempt state, with observation under `.scoped`, and the theorem that every
   such state satisfies `attemptInvariant`. Then the corollary that discharges
   `failed_attempt_starts_no_scan`'s `st.scanned = true` for every reachable latched attempting
   state, so the corner is excluded by a theorem.

2. The first-build ancestry corollary has no instance whose conclusion says anything.
   `Exhibits.first_build_provenance_with_current` instantiates `first_build_is_of_the_attempts_scan`
   and `first_build_reads_the_attempts_settled_block` with `scanView = v = deltaView`, so its last
   two conjuncts are `x = x` and its `Ancestry deltaView deltaView` is reflexive. Its first three
   conjuncts (marker-free, no attempt, marker gained) do show the premises are satisfiable.
   Wanted: an instance in which the repair's scan view is not the refresh's view. If `View` admits
   no such pair that is not artificial, drop the two reflexive conjuncts and say in the docstring
   that the exhibit shows the premises are satisfiable, not the conclusion.

3. Nothing shows the `.scoped` restriction on observation preservation is needed.
   `attemptInvariant_observe`: "observation under `.vacuous` can latch a running first build".
   The latch-scope flip makes `Exhibits.attemptInvariant_observe_with_current` fail to prove, but
   no declaration exhibits the invariant breaking. `unbuilt_wallet_latches_with_vacuous` latches
   an unbuilt wallet that is not running. Wanted: beside it in `VaultUnspent.lean`, a running first
   build whose observation under `.vacuous` latches it, clears `scanned` and leaves it attempting,
   so `attemptInvariant` is false after the step. This follows the precedent of
   `mismatched_scan_view_excluded_by_ancestry` for the ancestry premise.

Scope: `VaultUnspent.lean` and `Exhibits.lean` only. No Markdown change, no new guard parameter,
no trace-format change. A theorem in `VaultUnspent.lean` names values (`.scoped`, `.vacuous`),
never `current`.

Done when: all three are landed (no `sorry`, no new axiom), each new declaration is tagged
`@[req "WTC-9"]`, `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green unpiped, and every
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` guard-flip control whose count moves is re-measured and updated.
close_reason: Implemented all required formal coverage in 49f402f; full gates and selected workflow controls passed.

comments.author: implementer
comments.text:
Implemented in 49f402f23362b954e3b1bd43587d1b69dfdcde1c.

Reachable admits every no-attempt state, without constraining its other fields, and finite compositions of refresh under every Rules value, repair under every MarkerAnchor and ImportBracket, endAsFailure, and State.observe .scoped with arbitrary operation inputs. attemptInvariant_reachable reuses the base and all one-step lemmas. reachable_failed_attempt_starts_no_scan supplies the invariant internally and proves both repair and endAsFailure retain the original cache as deltaBase .neededScan; callers need no scanned premise. External record replacement is outside this boundary.

The permitted first-build fallback is used. A successful repair pins scanView.tip to the refresh tip, and Chain.Ancestry.below_shared_tip forces agreement through that shared tip. View documents no active blocks past its tip, so a distinct pair would differ only in artificial or invalid map entries. first_build_provenance_with_current retains the marker-free initial wallet, absent attempt, and gained marker, removes the reflexive conclusions, and documents success-premise satisfiability. The general provenance theorems remain unchanged.

running_first_build_breaks_invariant_with_vacuous starts the first build through refresh from the marker-free no-attempt state using literal rule values. It proves the running invariant, then the observed latch set, scanned cleared, attempt still running, and invariant false. Every new declaration is tagged WTC-9. The existing refutes sentences are unchanged.

Verification: baseline and final full specification gates exited 0, including kernel replay, requirement index and citation checks. Before the implementation commit, workflow steps 1-3, 5-15, 44-51 and 57-80 each reported PASS, with DONE 0 failed of 46. The measured guard-flip error counts for steps 44-51 are 3, 5, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2, 3; expectations did not change, and every control retained its declaration attribution and Exhibits-only checks. Step 56 subsequently reported PASS and DONE 0 failed of 1 against this committed revision; it checks packaging with the existing consumer declarations, not the new theorem statements. The full gate and requirement index verify the new declarations.

title: Archive the superseded Lean proposals and the closed findings' narratives in docs/archive/
description:
Owner decision, 2026-10-05: the set stops carrying history in its working documents. The two
superseded Lean proposals and the narratives of closed findings move to `docs/archive/`, which no
gate reads. Rewriting ADR-0023 is a separate bead that follows this one.

Do:

1. Create `docs/archive/` with a `README.md` of a few lines: what the folder holds; that nothing in
   it is normative; that no gate reads it; and, for each file, the commit it was frozen at.
2. Move `lean-01.md` and `lean-02.md` there unchanged (`git mv`). Repoint every path that cites
   them outside `.beads/`. ADR-0023 and `16-open-findings.md` cite them today.
3. In `16-open-findings.md`, move the full text of every finding whose heading says `CLOSED`
   unchanged into `docs/archive/closed-findings.md`. Today those are the sixteen F15, F32, F33,
   F44, F50–F59, F61 and F65; take the list from the headings, not from this sentence. Give each one a
   row in the existing "Withdrawn findings" table, in its current shape: the finding, what it was
   (its heading title), and why it went (the requirement, ADR or declaration that now carries the
   correction, plus a pointer to the archive file).
4. Before archiving a finding, grep for every citation of it outside `docs/archive/` and `.beads/`.
   Where a citing sentence relies on content that only the finding's narrative holds (a rule, a
   boundary or an argument used as current), move that content to its owner (the requirement,
   the ADR, or the Lean docstring) first. This is the README's rule: "Withdrawn wording is retained
   only where a trap sits behind it". A sentence that merely names the finding keeps its citation,
   which still resolves through the table row.
5. Rewrite the two sentences that state the old policy so that they state the new one:
   - `16-open-findings.md`'s CLOSED status word ("kept for the record (`F32`, `F33`)");
   - README's "this set carries its history in `docs/adr/` and `16-open-findings.md` instead".
   Check that these, the findings header ("moves to the withdrawn list at the end") and the
   archive README agree with each other.

Scope: `16-open-findings.md`, `README.md`, the new `docs/archive/` files, and the citation repoints
the moves force (including Lean docstrings). No normative requirement changes. ADR-0023's own
rewrite is the next bead; here, only repoint its paths and any quote this move breaks.

Done when:
- Every `F<n>` cited anywhere outside `docs/archive/` and `.beads/` has a `**F<n>.` heading or a
  Withdrawn-findings row in `16-open-findings.md` (a one-off script; record its output in the
  closing comment);
- `git grep -n 'lean-0[12]\.md' -- . ':!.beads' ':!docs/archive'` finds only pointers into
  `docs/archive/`;

title: Formal: POL-6's checks over one decoded PSBT, acceptance exact and hint-independent
description:
`Policy.lean` models only which code each `POL-6` row returns: its docstring says "the checks
themselves (`POL-7` to `POL-12`) are not modelled". This bead models them, over one decoded PSBT.
It meets `ADR-0025`'s four points:

1. It ranges over every decoded PSBT and every sealed configuration.
2. An evaluator that admits a stranger output signs a theft. `POL-4`: membership is decided
   "never by trusting a PSBT's `bip32_derivation` hint".
3. The rules are this set's (`POL-6` to `POL-12`). Derivation stays the assumed boundary
   `derive`, as in `Membership.lean`.
4. Its control is a planted hint-trust mutation, below.

## Spec amendment (lands on `POL-10` and `CNF-17`)

`POL-10` does not say which output's hint decides the code when several outputs do neither, and
the two codes differ. Add to `POL-10`: when several outputs do neither, the first of them in
transaction order decides the code. Add the same case to `CNF-17`. Owner's decision of
2026-10-05.

## Scope

- New `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`, imported by `tools/formal/BtcPolicy.lean`.
- The decoded PSBT, as the pure checks read it and nothing more:

  ```lean
  structure Psbt where
    txInputs    : List Encode.Input           -- the unsigned transaction's inputs
    txOutputs   : List Encode.Output          -- its outputs: script and amount
    inputMaps   : List (Option Encode.Output) -- each input map's witness_utxo
    outputHints : List Bool                   -- each output map: bip32_derivation non-empty
  ```

  The maps are lists of their own, so `POL-7`'s count rows can be represented. No
  `non_witness_utxo` (`F48` is open). Nothing reads `nVersion`, `nLockTime` or `nSequence`,
  and counts are read only for `POL-7`'s emptiness and equality rows, never bounded (`POL-15`).
- `Cfg` holds `derive`, `max`, `vault`, `escape`, `allow : List Membership.Descriptor` and
  `hotMaxPerTx`.
- `request : Cfg → Psbt → Policy.Request` computes the five flags from `POL-7`, `POL-9`, `POL-10`,
  `POL-11` and `POL-12`. Define `evaluate cfg p := Policy.evaluateSpend (request cfg p)`. `POL-6`'s
  order then exists once, and `dest_outranks_budget`, `budget_outranks_fee` and
  `evaluate_in_reachable` apply unchanged.
- Each output becomes a `Classification.Output` whose `kind` is `Membership.kindOf …` of its
  script. `allowlisted`, `hotBudgetOk` and `member_discharged` are reused, not restated.
- The fee row is a three-way `Policy.Fee` built from the totals, with two lemmas:
  `fee = .ok ↔ feeCapOk totalIn totalOut` and `fee = .inconsistent ↔ totalIn < totalOut`.
- When a `POL-7` row fails, the later flags read defaults. Nothing is proved about them, since
  row 1 hides them.

## Theorems (each `@[req]` on its owner; no `sorry`, no axiom, no `native_decide`)

0. **One characterisation lemma per `request` field**, each an iff against concrete predicates
   over the PSBT and `Cfg`, never against another flag. Without these, a `request` that refuses
   too eagerly or files a defect under the wrong row satisfies theorems 1–3. That is lost recovery,
   since the same evaluation runs over Escapes (`POL-13`), and a wrong code, since `POL-6` calls
   the order load-bearing.
   - `psbtInconsistent = true` ↔ one of `POL-7`'s five rows fails.
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `unknownInput = true` ↔ some `witness_utxo` script does not
     `matchesScript` the vault descriptor (`POL-9`).
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `dest` is `.allowed` ↔ no output's kind is `.unknown`. Otherwise it is
     `.changeNotDerivable` or `.notAllowed`, according to the hint of the first `.unknown` output in
     transaction order (`POL-10`).
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `overHotCap = true` ↔ `hotBudgetOk` fails (`POL-11`).
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `fee` is `.inconsistent` ↔ `totalIn < totalOut`, and `.ok` ↔
     `feeCapOk totalIn totalOut` (`POL-12`).
1. **Acceptance is exact** (`POL-6`). `evaluate cfg p = none` holds exactly when all of these hold:
   - `POL-7` holds: inputs and outputs are non-empty, both map counts equal their transaction
     counts, and every input map has a `witness_utxo`;
   - every `witness_utxo` script `matchesScript`es the vault descriptor (`POL-9`);
   - no output's kind is `.unknown`, which is `allowlisted` over the computed outputs (`POL-10`);
   - `hotBudgetOk` holds (`POL-11`), and so does `feeCapOk` (`POL-12`).
2. **Hints never admit** (`POL-10`). Take two PSBTs that differ only in `outputHints` (lists of
   the same length). They get the same result once `CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE` is read as
   `DEST_NOT_ALLOWED`. In particular, one is accepted exactly when the other is.
3. **The first failing output decides** (`POL-10` as amended). Suppose `POL-7` and `POL-9` hold,
   stated as concrete predicates rather than flag values, and some output's kind is `.unknown`.
   Then `evaluate` returns `CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE` if the first such output in transaction order
   has a hint, and `DEST_NOT_ALLOWED` if it does not.
4. **Exhibits**, all by `decide`, over a toy `derive` with a small `max` and a definite vault
   descriptor (`CHN-3`), so that no exhibit relies on a vault script past the bound:
   - one accepting PSBT;
   - one PSBT failing each `POL-7` row;
   - one PSBT for each of `POL-6` rows 2–4, and two for row 5 (one `.inconsistent`, one
     `.overCap`);
   - a stranger output with a hint, refused `CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE`;
   - two strangers with hints `[false, true]` and `[true, false]`, refused by the first.

## Control (`ADR-0025` point 4)

Add one `.github/workflows/gates.yml` step, in exactly one shard, shaped like the `DEF-15` step:
- `sed` plants the hint-trust mutation, so the destination check counts an output with a hint as
  recognised;
- `grep` confirms the `sed` applied;
- `lake build` runs, and the step asserts it fails with the measured exact error count, naming
  theorem 2 and the hinted-stranger exhibit.

Mark the line the `sed` targets with a trailing comment, as the `DEF-15` control's `-- mixed` is
marked. Run the step locally with
`nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>`.

## Spec text

- Add the `POL-10` and `CNF-17` amendment above.
- In `POL-6`, add a formal-home sentence naming `BtcPolicy.Evaluate.evaluate` and theorems 1–3,
  as `POL-4` names its own.
- In `Policy.lean`'s module docstring, replace "the checks themselves (`POL-7` to `POL-12`) are
  not modelled" with a pointer to `Evaluate.lean`.

## Out of scope

- Classification and request shapes (`CHN-30`, `CHN-32`, `CHN-35`), already modelled over

- `SPN-47`: `POL-15` says "no refresh interval or feerate".
- `SPN-25`'s chain comparison, signatures, `POL-13`'s `escape:` twin, and `check` strings.

title: Formal: move bps-nfx's general proofs into Evaluate.lean, drop the hint seam and POL-10's dated tag
description:
This bead fixes three findings from the review of `bps-nfx` (`e5c0810`). None of them changes a
verdict or a theorem statement.

## Findings

1. **General proofs live in `Exhibits.lean`.** `ADR-0023` keeps each model's general proofs in
   its own module. `Exhibits.lean` holds the `current` instantiations and the executable verdicts
   (decision 6, decision 12 and Consequences: "`BtcPolicy/Exhibits.lean` holds the current
   exhibits"). Its other theorems with general binders are all `_with_current` instantiations of
   proofs owned elsewhere.

   `bps-nfx` instead put these general proofs under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`:
   - `softenCode`, `FirstAt`;
   - `hints_never_admit`, `hints_acceptance_iff`;
   - `recognised_iff`;
   - `firstUnknown_none_iff`, `firstUnknown_some_iff`;
   - `allowlisted_iff`;
   - `dest_allowed_iff`, `dest_notAllowed_iff`, `dest_changeNotDerivable_iff`;
   - `acceptance_exact`, `first_failing_output`.

   `POL-6`'s formal-home sentence therefore points into `Exhibits`. The cause was `bps-nfx`'s own
   control clause, which named "theorem 2 and the hinted-stranger exhibit" in one build. That
   clause is withdrawn here.
2. **`recognised` takes a `_hint` argument it never reads.** Its docstring says the argument
   exists only for the negative control, so the definition is shaped by its test.
3. **`POL-10` ends "(amended 2026-10-05)".** README forbids inline dated tags ("The reference
   project kept every correction inline with a dated tag, and its documents became hard to
   read"). No earlier value exists, because `POL-10` was silent on the case before.

## Scope

- **Move the general proofs listed in finding 1** into `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`,
  namespace `BtcPolicy.Evaluate`, without changing their statements. The decided exhibits stay in
  `Exhibits.lean`, under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`: `cfg`, `accepted`, `consistencyRows`,
  `fixture_membership`, the `POL-7` rows, `foreign_input`, the stranger exhibits,
  `hot_budget_refused` and the two fee exhibits.
- **Drop `_hint` from `recognised`.** `recognised_iff` loses its hint argument.
- **Move the mutation seam into `firstUnknown`.** Its `if recognised …` line carries a trailing
  `-- hint-trust` marker, and the `gates.yml` control's `sed` adds `|| hs.headD false` to that
  condition.
- **Rewrite the control so its errors fall in `Evaluate.lean`.** It must name
  `hints_never_admit`. Measure the exact count with
  `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>` and pin the measured value.
  The decided exhibit is no longer part of the control, since `Exhibits.lean` cannot build once
  `Evaluate.lean` fails. Keep it in one shard.
- **Rewrite the docstrings written around the test.** These are `Evaluate.lean`'s module
  docstring ("The planted hint-trust mutation must leave this upstream module buildable…") and
  `hints_never_admit`'s "independently of all mutation-sensitive characterisation lemmas". A
  docstring states what the declaration says, not how CI breaks it.
- **Update `POL-6`'s formal-home sentence** to the `BtcPolicy.Evaluate.*` names.
- **Delete "(amended 2026-10-05)" from `POL-10`.** The rest of the sentence stays verbatim, since
  `CNF-17` quotes it.

## Out of scope

Any change to a theorem statement, an exhibit's verdict, `request`, `evaluate`, or the
`CNF-17`/`POL-10` rule. Leave the other dated tags in `ADR-0020` and `05-duress-and-lockdown.md`
alone.

## Done when

- The three findings are fixed.
- No general proof remains under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.
- The rewritten control passes locally with its measured count.
- Every other `gates.yml` control whose count or line moves is re-run with `run-steps.py` and
  updated to the measured value. This includes the `DEF-15`, `F57` and citation declaration-name
  controls.

title: API-25: a refusal carries a bounded fault list for the first per-item check that refuses
description:
The owner needs to debug production cases where a node and the client disagree: which inputs or
outputs a node refused, and why. Today a refusal says only `{code, check, detail}`, and the client
may parse only `code` (`API-16`). The design below came from four readers over two rounds on
2026-10-05, and the owner accepted it that day, with printing on a live terminal only.

## The member (new `API-25`)

```json
{"refusal": {"code": "CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE", "check": "verified_change", "detail": "…",
  "faults": {"tx": "spend",
             "entries": [{"output": 1, "code": "CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE"},
                         {"output": 3, "code": "DEST_NOT_ALLOWED"}],
             "truncated": false}}}
```

- **`tx`** names the transaction the indices point into: `spend`, `escape`, `refresh` or
  `clawback`. The client does not parse `check`, so `check`'s `escape:` prefix cannot tell it.
- **Fee-bump rungs carry no list.** `CHN-16` gives a rung "the same ordered input set, the same
  ordered output script set" as its base, so a rung fails a per-item check only if its base does,
  and the base is checked first. State this in `API-25`.
- **Each entry** has exactly one of `input` or `output`, a zero-based index into `tx`, and a
  `code` from `API-13`.
- **Order and length.** Entries are strictly ascending with no duplicates, and all name the same
  side. They are the first 32 failing items; `truncated` is true exactly when more exist. The
  operator program's 64 KiB `/sign` cap (`OPR-50`) needs this bound, and policy sets no output
  count limit (`POL-15`).
- **Only the first refusing check contributes**, and only one of these:
  - `POL-7`'s missing-`witness_utxo` row, reached after its four preceding rows pass: each entry
    `PSBT_INCONSISTENT`;
  - `POL-9`: `UNKNOWN_INPUT`;
  - `POL-10`: each output's hint-selected code;
  - `SPN-25`'s confirmed-prevout mismatch: `PSBT_INCONSISTENT`;
  - `SPN-43`/`SPN-50`'s replacement-test `UNKNOWN_INPUT`. This refusal has no `check` string
    today, and `POL-9` returns the same code, so give it its own check string in `API-14`;
  - `SPN-46`'s too-young or unconfirmed refresh inputs: `REFRESH_TOO_SOON`.

  Every other refusal omits `faults`.
- **The top-level `code` and `check` are the first entry's.** Under `POL-10` that is the existing
  first-failing-output rule.
- **Agreement and silence.**
  - Honest nodes give the same list for the pure checks on identical inputs.
  - Chain-check lists may differ between nodes at different tips, and that difference is the
    debugging signal. No byte-identity across nodes is required.
  - The member is response bytes under `DUR-1`, so it must be identical under the normal and the
    duress PIN. Every listed check runs after the PIN gate; say so in `API-25`.
- **Replay.** `SPN-23`/`SPN-24` return a cached refusal with its member verbatim. Which refusals
  are cached does not change.

## The client (`API-16`, `OPR-8`, `OPR-9`)

- **Validate first.** A coordinator discards the member whole unless all of these hold:
  - `tx` names a transaction it sent;
  - every index is below that transaction's input or output count;
  - every code is one the check can return;
  - the first entry's code equals `code`;
  - the order is strictly ascending, with at most 32 entries.

  Allocation is bounded before decoding.
- **Show it only on a live terminal.** The operator program MAY render a validated list on an
  interactive terminal, in locally authored words, attributed to the node, beside its own
  evaluation of the same items where it can compute one. It MUST suppress the list when its
  output is not a terminal. It MUST NOT write the list, or any comparison derived from it, to
  logs, artifacts or persisted state. Only the closed code is retained, as today.
- **Never act on it.** Nothing the program sends, retries, recomposes, selects, or reports as the
  outcome or exit status reads a fault list. A node may lie: `SEC-9` keeps `t − 1` compromised
  peers in the model.
- **`check` and `detail`** stay never-printed and never-retained.
- **`OPR-65`** keeps one coin per refresh transaction. Its stated reason ("could not name the
  input at fault") becomes false, so replace it with the never-act rule.

## Requirement ids

- New: `API-25` and one new `CNF` item covering:
  - order, the cap and `truncated`;
  - PIN-uniformity;
  - a malformed list being discarded;
  - the chain-dependent rows;
  - replay.
- Amended: `API-12`, `API-14`, `API-16`, `WIR-8` (one example with the member), `POL-7`, `POL-9`,
  `POL-10`, `POL-13`, `SPN-23`/`SPN-24`, `SPN-25`, `SPN-27`, `SPN-43`, `SPN-46`, `SPN-50`,
  `OPR-8`, `OPR-9`, `OPR-65`, and `CNF-17` (two unrecognised outputs, both listed, in order).

## Out of scope

The Lean model of the list, which is the next bead; `OVR-13`; batched refresh; any change to which
refusals exist or to `POL-6`'s order.

## Done when

- The text above has landed.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped, including the fixtures
  gate on the new JSON example.
- Every `gates.yml` control whose count moves is re-measured and updated.

title: Formal: API-25's fault list for the pure checks in Evaluate.lean
description:
This bead models `API-25`'s fault list for the pure checks in `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`. The
previous bead adds `API-25` and amends `POL-7`, `POL-9` and `POL-10` to define their entries; this
bead depends on it.

It passes `ADR-0025`'s four points:
- It ranges over every decoded PSBT.
- A wrong list either names the wrong output, so an operator debugging a production
  disagreement is misled, or contradicts the top-level code, which `POL-6`'s order makes
  load-bearing.
- The rules are this set's own.
- It has a planted control, below.

## Scope

- **A fault entry and its list.**
  - A `Fault` is an index and a `Policy.Code`, tagged input or output.
  - `faults : Cfg → Psbt → List Fault` gives the complete list for the first refusing check among
    `POL-7`'s `witness_utxo` row, `POL-9` and `POL-10`, and is empty otherwise.
  - The 32-entry cap is a `take 32` over the complete list, and `truncated` is `32 < length`.
  - Reuse `recognised`, `owned` and `firstUnknown`'s scan rather than restating them.
- **Theorems in `Evaluate.lean`, each tagged `@[req]` on its owner:**
  - when `faults` is non-empty, `evaluate` returns its head's code;
  - for each listed check, the list is empty exactly when that check passes;
  - replacing the hints with an equal-length list changes only entry codes, never the indices;
  - the indices are strictly ascending;
  - the transmitted list is a prefix of the complete one, and `truncated` is exact.
- **Exhibits in `Exhibits.lean`:**
  - mixed hints over two strangers with a recognised prefix;
  - two foreign inputs;
  - a missing `witness_utxo` on the second of two inputs;
  - a list longer than 32, truncated.
- **Control (`ADR-0025` point 4):**
  - plant a mutation in `faults` that scans outputs in reverse, marked with a trailing comment;
  - `.github/workflows/gates.yml` asserts that the build fails at the head-code theorem, with an
    exact count measured by `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>`;
  - the step lives in exactly one shard;
  - re-measure the existing hint-trust control, since `faults` reads the same scan.
- **Formal-home sentence.** Add one sentence to `API-25` naming the theorems.

## Out of scope

- The chain-dependent rows (`SPN-25`, `SPN-43`/`SPN-50`, `SPN-46`), which have no pure model.
- `Silence.lean`: `DUR-1` already covers the member as response bytes.
- Any change to `request` or `evaluate`'s verdicts.

## Done when

- The theorems, exhibits and control have landed, with no `sorry`, no axiom and no
  `native_decide`.
- The gate is green, run unpiped.
- Every control whose count moves is re-measured and updated.

title: Finding: a compromised node release can write the normal PIN into state the coordinator persists
description:
Record an open finding in `16-open-findings.md`, using the next unused finding number, from the
design review of `API-25`'s fault list (2026-10-05, four readers). This bead records the finding
and leaves it open: no requirement changes. Write it as an open finding in the file's existing
format, with provenance by reviewer letter or role.

## The finding

The SILENCE adversary holds the coordinator and the physical scene but no node (`OVR-13`,
`SEC-10`, `DUR-1`). `DOM-2` describes it as a coordinator "holding the coordinator auth key but no
history of the normal PIN". `OVR-13` puts a compromised node out of scope for silence, because
"A node sees the submitted PIN in plaintext".

That boundary assumes nothing PIN-derived reaches what the coordinator retains. A node can break
the assumption without colluding with the wrench holder: a backdoored node release, whose encoding
anyone holding the release can recover, writes the normal PIN into node-chosen values that the
operator program persists. Whoever later seizes the coordinator reads those values while holding
no node, which is exactly the adversary the guarantee covers, and gains the PIN history `DOM-2`
says it lacks.

The channels exist today, without `API-25`:
- `OPR-60` persists each node's returned `/events` cursor. `API-18` makes it an integer the node
  assigns, up to 2⁵³ − 1 under `WIR-1`.
- `OPR-60` also persists events whose txids, outpoints and scripts the node chooses (`API-18`).

`OPS-47`'s reproducible, signed releases reduce the backdoor risk but do not exclude it.
`ADR-0012` already accepts that a compromised node "can hand the harvested normal pin to a
hostile-at-wrench coordinator". The difference here is that the hand-off needs no coordinated
adversary.

## The open question to record

Either state the premise the guarantee actually rests on, that no node runs a compromised
release, or constrain what the operator program persists from node-chosen values. Name both
options, and the requirements each would touch (`OVR-13`, `SEC-10`, `DOM-2`, `OPR-60`,
`API-18`). Do not choose between them.

## Done when

- The finding has landed, with every quotation verbatim; the citation gate checks them.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.

title: F66: a compromised node release is outside SILENCE; disclosure sweeps first and rotate forgets the old vault's node data
description:
This bead resolves `F66` with the owner's decisions from a design interview on 2026-10-05. The glossary
already carries the premise: `CONTEXT.md`'s SILENCE entry now ends "It assumes no node ran a
compromised release while the current PINs were in use."

## Decisions

1. **The premise.** SILENCE, and `DOM-2`'s coordinator with "no history of the normal PIN",
   assume that no node ran a compromised release while the current PINs were in use.
   - The rule has one home: `SEC-10`, which owns "The scope of SILENCE MUST be stated wherever
     it is claimed".
   - `OVR-13`, `DOM-2` and `DUR-1`'s boundary sentence point at it and do not restate it.
2. **The compromise matrix.** Add a row to `SEC-54` for a compromised node release whose encoding
   a later coercer of the coordinator can read.
   - The outcome: silence is not claimed for PINs entered while that release ran.
   - Where it is enforced: `OPS-30`'s sweep-first rotation.
   - Record the decision in `ADR-0021` with the rejected alternative. The rejected alternative
     constrained what the operator program persists from node-chosen values. It cannot close the
     channel, because the closed refusal code `OPR-8` retains, the choice of which events to
     report, and their timing are all node-chosen.
3. **Rotation order.** A disclosed compromised node release is a compromise signal under
   `OPS-30`, so the rotation sweeps first.
4. **New PINs.** A compromise-signal rotation SHOULD enrol PINs such that neither new PIN
   verifies against either of the predecessor's digests. This is a recommendation only: the
   enrolment tooling does not check it, and routine rotations are unaffected.
5. **The old vault's node data (`OPR-66` `rotate`, with `OPR-60` and `OPR-8`).**
   - **When.** After a compromise-signal rotation, once the program's own chain view shows that
     every predecessor coin the sweep named is spent, `rotate` deletes everything the program
     persisted from the predecessor's nodes: `OPR-60`'s consumed events and cursors, and any
     retained refusal codes.
   - **Polling stops.** It stops polling the predecessor's nodes. A sweep-first rotation leaves
     nothing to steal, and its nodes are not locked down, since `OPS-15`'s claw-back needs "`t`
     nodes that are not locked down".
   - **Late coins.** A later deposit to a predecessor address, or a coin unconfirmed at the
     sweep, is found through the program's own chain view (`balance`) and clawed back.
   - **What it cannot reach.** State that the deletion cannot reach copies outside the program's
     own state: backups, and notifications already delivered.
   - **Conformance.** Extend the conformance item that covers `OPR-66` to require the deletion
     and the stop.
6. **Close `F66`.** Move it to the withdrawn-findings table with a "Corrected at …" row naming the
   requirements above, and move its narrative unchanged to `docs/archive/closed-findings.md`,
   as the earlier closed findings were.

## Out of scope

The escape wallet's key structure, which is a separate bead. Any change to `API-25` or to what a
node emits.

## Done when

- The six decisions have landed, each on the identifier named, with completeness checked by grep.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.

title: Escape wallet: multisig preferred, single-sig accepted, with a bring-your-own descriptor checked per cosigner
description:
The owner decided on 2026-10-05 that the escape wallet should preferably be multisig, with single-sig
still accepted. `CONTEXT.md` already defines it as "An offline wallet, preferably multisig with
single-sig accepted". The rest of the set still assumes one key.
- `MAN-26` makes `keygen` emit `wpkh([<fingerprint>]<xpub>/*)` for the escape.
- An escape bundle carries one `master_fingerprint`.
- `MAN-28` compares fingerprints as if there were one key.
- `OPS-16`, `OPS-30` and `ADR-0021` say "single-key escape wallet".
- `OPS-60` and `DOM-11` speak of "the escape-wallet key".

## Decisions

1. **The escape wallet SHOULD be multisig, and single-sig stays accepted.** Put the SHOULD in
   `DOM-11`. `keygen`'s escape banner (`MAN-26`) gains one line saying a multisig escape wallet
   is preferred.
2. **The Operator brings their own descriptor.** The ceremony accepts an escape bundle with:
   - a descriptor in `MAN-39`'s grammar whose keys are all ranged extended keys with origin;
   - the master fingerprint of every cosigner.

   It is built with the Operator's own multisig tooling. `keygen` keeps its `wpkh` path for
   single-sig. The spec adds no multisig construction tooling.
3. **The independence check covers every cosigner (`MAN-28`).**
   - Each cosigner's derived and ancestor keys are checked against the user, node, recovery and
     coordinator keys and against the hot wallet.
   - Each cosigner's fingerprint is checked against the hot wallet's.
   - The check refuses two cosigners that share a master fingerprint, since that is a multisig
     in name only.
   - `independence.txt` records every cosigner.
4. **Key-count wording.**
   - `DOM-11`: each escape key is generated on a device that holds no other vault role.
   - `OPS-60`: custody covers a threshold of escape keys and their backups, and duress becomes
     theft when the attacker holds that threshold.
   - `OPS-16`, `OPS-30` and `ADR-0021`: "single-key escape wallet" becomes "escape wallet".
   - `SEC-54`: row 10 and row L6 become thresholds. The coercer needs `k` escape keys; a loss
     needs more than `m − k` keys gone.
5. **Check every other single-key assumption** about the escape, including `CHN-35`'s claw-back,
   `WIR-7`'s fixture comment, the formal exhibits and the conformance items. Change only the
   ones that are wrong for a multisig descriptor. `CHN-34` already counts the actual output
   bytes.
6. **Conformance.** Extend the independence-check conformance item with these cases:
   - a valid 2-of-3 accepted;
   - two cosigners sharing a fingerprint, refused;
   - a cosigner key equal to a node key, refused;
   - a cosigner sharing the hot wallet's fingerprint, refused;
   - a single-sig escape still accepted.

## Out of scope

Requiring multisig; multisig construction or signing tooling; the escape wallet's own spending
policy.

## Done when

- The decisions have landed, with completeness checked by grep for "single-key", "escape-wallet
  key" and "master_fingerprint".
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.
- Every control whose count moves is re-measured.
